text:
Season 1 Overview (Story Setup)
The story unfolds over several months in a world where seasons last for years. In the Seven Kingdoms of Westeros, the long summer is ending and winter approaches. Lord Eddard “Ned” Stark of Winterfell is summoned by his old friend King Robert Baratheon to become the new Hand of the King after the sudden death of the previous Hand, Jon Arryn (Ned’s mentor and father-figure). Ned is reluctant but accepts after learning Arryn may have been murdered; he plans to investigate using his new authority.

Across the Narrow Sea in Essos, the exiled Targaryen siblings Viserys and Daenerys (children of the Mad King Aerys II, overthrown by Robert) plot their return. Viserys arranges for Daenerys to marry Khal Drogo, leader of a massive Dothraki horse-lord army of tens of thousands, in exchange for warriors to invade Westeros and reclaim the Iron Throne. Daenerys seeks safety more than power.

At the northern edge of the realm, the Night’s Watch guards the massive ice Wall against wildlings and darker threats from the lands of always-winter. Rumors of ancient evils stir. The season follows these three main threads—the political intrigue and family conflicts in Westeros, the Dothraki journey and rising power of Daenerys, and the Watch’s grim duties—as they intertwine toward war, betrayal, and change.
1

Season 1 Episode 1: Winter Is Coming
Beyond the Wall, three Night’s Watch rangers—Ser Waymar Royce, Will, and Gared—ride into the Haunted Forest to check reports of wildlings. Will, the best scout, finds a group of wildling corpses arranged in a strange pattern and a dead girl pinned to a tree. He reports back. Gared urges caution and a return to Castle Black, but young Ser Waymar insists on seeing the bodies. When they arrive the corpses have vanished. A tall figure with ice-blue eyes—a White Walker—appears and easily kills Waymar. Gared tries to flee and is beheaded. Will watches in horror as the dead wildling girl rises as a wight with glowing blue eyes. He flees south in terror.

In Pentos, Viserys Targaryen prepares his younger sister Daenerys for marriage to Khal Drogo. He is harsh and controlling, inspecting her body and insisting she must please the Khal so he can gain an army. Daenerys bathes in scalding water without flinching. Drogo arrives, looks her over briefly from horseback, and rides off; Illyrio Mopatis reassures Viserys this means approval. Daenerys does not want the marriage, but Viserys threatens her and says he would give her to the entire khalasar if it meant reclaiming the throne. At the wedding celebration there are deaths in fights (normal for Dothraki). Gifts include books from the exile knight Ser Jorah Mormont (who swears to Viserys), three ancient petrified dragon eggs from Illyrio, and a white mare from Drogo. That night on the beach Drogo consummates the marriage roughly; Daenerys is frightened and in pain.

In King’s Landing the bells toll for Jon Arryn’s death. Queen Cersei Lannister worries that Arryn discovered something dangerous and may have told someone. She confides in her twin brother Jaime of the Kingsguard. He tells her not to worry—if the King knew their secret they would already be dead. Cersei wants Jaime as the new Hand; he has no interest in the work.

In the North at Winterfell, Ned Stark watches his young son Bran practice archery with help from older brothers Robb and the bastard Jon Snow. Little sister Arya shows better aim. News arrives of a Night’s Watch deserter. Ned takes Robb, Jon, Bran, ward Theon Greyjoy, and guards to carry out the sentence himself with the great Valyrian steel sword Ice, teaching Bran that the man who passes the sentence must swing the sword. The deserter Will begs them to warn of White Walkers before dying. Ned dismisses it as madness—the Walkers have been gone for thousands of years.

On the ride home they find a dead stag and a dead mother direwolf killed by an antler. Five pups survive. Jon argues it is an omen—the direwolf is the Stark sigil and Ned has five trueborn children—so the pups are taken home. Jon finds a sixth albino runt and keeps it. Later a raven brings word of Jon Arryn’s death and that King Robert’s court is riding north. Ned realizes Robert will ask him to be Hand. He does not want to leave Winterfell.

The Stark children name and bond with their growing direwolves: Grey Wind (Robb), Lady (Sansa), Nymeria (Arya), Summer (Bran), Shaggydog (Rickon), and Ghost (Jon). Bran is caught climbing again as the royal party approaches. The courtyard fills for the arrival. King Robert greets Ned warmly and immediately demands to visit the crypts to pay respects at Lyanna Stark’s tomb (Ned’s sister, once betrothed to Robert). Cersei is impatient. Jaime finds their younger brother Tyrion (a dwarf) in a brothel with the prostitute Ros and hauls him to the feast. In the crypts Robert still rages about Rhaegar Targaryen “kidnapping” Lyanna and says not all Targaryens are dead. The episode ends with the threads of family duty, hidden secrets, ancient threats, and forced alliances all set in motion.
2

Season 1 Episode 2: The Kingsroad
The Dothraki khalasar leaves Pentos and rides into the vast grassy Dothraki Sea. Viserys stays with them, impatient for his army. Jorah explains he is an exile because he sold poachers into slavery and fled Ned Stark’s justice. Daenerys struggles with her new life and Drogo’s rough nightly visits; she finds some comfort looking at her dragon eggs. Her handmaiden Doreah teaches her how to take control in bed and gain her husband’s respect rather than submit like a slave. Daenerys begins speaking Dothraki and using her body differently; Drogo responds more gently.

At Winterfell Bran lies unconscious after his fall. Tyrion forces a reluctant Joffrey to pay respects to the Starks. Tyrion tells his family he will ride north to see the Wall before returning south and notes Cersei and Jaime’s guarded reactions when he says Bran will live. Cersei visits Catelyn at Bran’s bedside and shares the story of her own first son (a black-haired boy) who died of fever, offering to pray for Bran.

Jon has a light sword forged for Arya; she names it Needle. He tells her “stick them with the pointy end” and says goodbye. He kisses the comatose Bran farewell. Ned says goodbye to Jon, promising to tell him about his mother next time they meet and affirming he is a Stark by blood even without the name. The parties split: Ned, Arya, Sansa and the royals south on the Kingsroad; Jon, Tyrion and Benjen Stark north to the Wall.

On the road Robert tells Ned that spies report Daenerys has married Drogo and the khalasar is huge. He fears another war. Ned points out the Dothraki have no ships. Robert presses Ned about Jon’s mother; Ned stays silent.

Back at Winterfell Catelyn refuses to leave Bran’s side. A fire is set as a distraction; an assassin tries to kill the boy with a Valyrian steel dagger. Catelyn fights him off until Summer the direwolf kills the man. Later Catelyn finds a long blonde hair in the tower where Bran fell. She gathers Robb, Theon, Maester Luwin and Ser Rodrik and concludes the Lannisters tried to silence Bran because he saw something. She decides to ride south secretly to warn Ned, leaving Robb in charge with Rodrik as escort.

On the northern road Jon and Tyrion talk. Tyrion says books are his weapons. New recruits (criminals who chose the Wall over mutilation) join them. Tyrion warns Jon the Night’s Watch is full of broken men, not heroes. They reach the Wall; its sheer size impresses even Tyrion.

At the Inn at the Crossroads the royal party stops. Joffrey takes Sansa walking by the river. They find Arya practicing swordplay with the butcher’s boy Mycah. Joffrey torments the boy with his sword Lion’s Tooth. Arya hits him with a stick; Nymeria bites Joffrey’s arm. Arya throws the sword in the river and runs. Sansa is torn. Later before the King, Joffrey lies about the fight. Sansa, pressured, will not contradict him. Cersei demands a direwolf’s death. Nymeria has fled (Arya drove her off with a rock), so Lady is killed instead on Robert’s reluctant order. Ned does the deed himself. The Hound returns with Mycah’s corpse, saying the boy ran but not fast enough. Far away in Winterfell, Bran finally wakes.
3

Season 1 Episode 3: Lord Snow
The royal party reaches King’s Landing. Ned is immediately called to a Small Council meeting. He meets Jaime in the throne room; old bitterness over Jaime killing the Mad King (who murdered Ned’s father and brother) surfaces. The council members are: Petyr “Littlefinger” Baelish (Master of Coin, who knew Catelyn as a girl), Grand Maester Pycelle, Renly Baratheon (Robert’s younger brother, Master of Laws), and the eunuch Varys (Master of Whisperers). Ned learns the crown is six million gold dragons in debt—half to Tywin Lannister—and Robert has ordered an expensive tournament to celebrate Ned’s appointment. Ned wants to cancel it; the others doubt the King will listen.

Cersei coaches Joffrey: when he is king the truth will be whatever he says. She warns him the North cannot be easily conquered and that anyone who is not a Lannister is an enemy. She tells him to be kind to Sansa for now.

Arya and Sansa are still angry over the river incident. Ned explains Sansa was trapped and gives Arya permission to keep practicing with Needle. He hires the Braavosi water dancer Syrio Forel (former First Sword of Braavos) to train her. Watching them, Ned realizes his daughter may be preparing for real conflict.

Catelyn and Rodrik arrive secretly but are spotted by Littlefinger’s men and taken to one of his brothels, where Varys also waits. Littlefinger reveals the assassin’s ornate dagger once belonged to him—he lost it betting against Tyrion Lannister. He fetches Ned; after a tense moment Ned is reunited with his wife. He vows to expose the Lannisters. Littlefinger offers help for old affection toward Catelyn.

News of Bran’s recovery reaches the city. Cersei fears exposure; Jaime comforts her. Robert trades war stories with Barristan Selmy and jokes with Jaime about the Mad King’s last words (“Burn them all”).

At Winterfell Bran is awake but paralyzed and remembers nothing of the fall. Old Nan tells him dark tales of the Long Night and White Walkers instead of heroic stories. Robb confirms he will never walk again; Bran says he would rather be dead.

At Castle Black Jon dominates the training yard against the other ragged recruits. Ser Alliser Thorne mocks him as “Lord Snow.” Tyrion watches with Lord Commander Jeor Mormont. Later the other boys jump Jon; Tyrion stops it and tells Jon he is alienating them by being better trained and standoffish. Benjen refuses to take Jon ranging yet—rank means nothing here; everything must be earned. Benjen leaves on a ranging. Tyrion talks with Mormont and the ancient blind Maester Aemon; they beg him to ask the court for more men. Aemon warns winter is coming harder than anyone remembers and darker things than wildlings may come with it. Tyrion climbs the Wall, urinates off the edge (an old ambition), shares a moment with Jon, and departs south with recruiter Yoren.

In the Dothraki Sea Daenerys boldly orders the khalasar to halt. Viserys is furious and threatens her; a bloodrider whips him and forces him to walk in shame. Irri tells Daenerys she is pregnant. She shares the news with Drogo; they hope for a boy. Jorah and Rakharo discuss fighting styles. Jorah leaves briefly for Qohor on business but will rejoin before Vaes Dothrak.
4

Season 1 Episode 4: Cripples, Bastards, and Broken Things
At Winterfell Bran dreams of a three-eyed raven. Tyrion (passing through with Yoren) gives Bran designs for a special saddle that will let him ride by voice and reins alone, saying he has a soft spot for “cripples, bastards and broken things.” He does it partly to repay Jon’s earlier friendliness. Robb allows him to stay but Tyrion prefers the town brothel. Theon is rude; Tyrion needles him about being a glorified hostage.

At Castle Black soft, fat, fearful Samwell Tarly arrives. Thorne and the others mock him mercilessly as “Ser Piggy.” Jon protects him, fighting multiple boys at once. Sam explains his father Lord Randyll Tarly gave him a choice on his eighteenth nameday: take the black or suffer a convenient “hunting accident.” Jon is shocked a trueborn son could be treated worse than a bastard. That night Jon uses Ghost to intimidate the bully Rast into going easy. Next day no one will fight Sam hard. Thorne is furious and later describes a blizzard beyond the Wall that forced cannibalism. Jon and Sam clean together and admit neither has been with a woman; Jon does not want to risk fathering another bastard.

In Vaes Dothrak the khalasar arrives at the sacred city (no walls, only a horse-statue gate). Viserys is angry they are going the “wrong” way. He bathes with Doreah and rants about dragons and destiny. Later he storms into Daenerys’s tent when she invites him to dinner (he sees it as being commanded). He insults her Dothraki clothes and gifts. She fights back for the first time, hitting him with a belt and warning that if he ever strikes her again he will lose the hand. She tells Jorah she now sees Viserys will never be a real king.

In King’s Landing Sansa visits the Iron Throne room with Septa Mordane and frets about producing heirs and Joffrey’s lingering anger. At the Small Council Ned hears of rising crime from the coming tournament crowds and lends men to the City Watch. He questions Pycelle about Jon Arryn’s final days. Pycelle says Arryn borrowed a thick book of noble lineages and his last words were “the seed is strong.” Ned takes the book. He finds Arya practicing balance and tells her Bran can still have a full life as a lord or counselor even if he cannot be a knight; when she asks if she can do those things he says she will marry a lord and have sons. She replies that is not her.

Littlefinger advises Ned to keep the investigation quiet and points him toward Jon Arryn’s former squire (now a knight fighting in the tourney) and an armorer. Ned’s man Jory is rebuffed by the arrogant new knight Ser Hugh. At the smithy Tobho Mott, Ned meets the apprentice Gendry, who made a fine bull’s-head helm. Jon Arryn had visited and asked about Gendry’s mother. Looking at the boy’s face Ned realizes Gendry is one of Robert’s bastards. He does not yet understand why Arryn cared. Later Jory tries to deliver a message to Robert and finds Jaime on guard outside while the King beds other women; Jaime is bitter and reminisces with Jory about the Greyjoy Rebellion.
5

Season 1 Episode 5: The Wolf and the Lion
Catelyn’s party (with Tyrion as prisoner, plus sellsword Bronn and others) rides through the Vale. She has been loudly claiming they are going to Winterfell as misdirection. Hill tribes attack; Tyrion fights and kills a man, saving Catelyn’s life. They reach the Eyrie. Lysa Arryn (Catelyn’s sister) is unstable and furious that Tyrion has been brought there. She sends him to a sky cell—a three-sided room open to a sheer drop. Tyrion must sleep carefully or roll to his death.

At Winterfell Bran is frustrated by his mother’s absence and his paralysis. Maester Luwin suggests he learn a short bow for mounted shooting. Theon is with Ros and bristles when she compares him unfavorably to Tyrion.

In King’s Landing Ned questions Barristan Selmy about Ser Hugh’s sudden death in the lists (Hugh had expensive new armor right after being knighted). Robert wants to joust himself; Ned points out he is too fat for his armor and the knights would let him win. The tourney begins. Ser Gregor “the Mountain” Clegane faces Ser Loras Tyrell (the Knight of Flowers). Loras rides a mare in heat that distracts Gregor’s stallion; Gregor is thrown, beheads his own horse in rage, and attacks Loras. Sandor Clegane (the Hound, Gregor’s brother) intervenes. Robert stops the fight. Loras names the Hound the victor.

Varys privately tells Ned that Robert will soon be dead unless Ned saves him, that Jon Arryn was poisoned with the Tears of Lys for asking questions, and that Ned is one of the few honorable men left. Arya chases cats into the dungeons and overhears Varys meeting with Illyrio Mopatis. They discuss how the lion and wolf will soon be at war (as planned), but it has come too soon—Drogo will not invade until his son is born. Illyrio suggests killing Ned; Varys refuses. Later Varys and Littlefinger trade veiled threats about each other’s schemes.

Yoren arrives with urgent news of Catelyn’s arrest of Tyrion. At a Small Council meeting Robert learns Daenerys is pregnant and orders her, the child, and Viserys assassinated. Ned refuses on principle and resigns as Hand. Robert is furious. Renly and Loras (lovers) discuss Renly claiming the throne himself with Tyrell support; Renly is fourth in line and hesitant. Cersei and Robert share a rare drink and talk about the Targaryen threat and Lyanna; their marriage was doomed from the start.

Littlefinger takes Ned to a brothel to show him another of Robert’s bastards—a baby girl with black hair. Leaving, Ned and his men are ambushed by Jaime and Lannister guards. Jaime demands answers about Tyrion. Fighting breaks out. A Lannister guardsman stabs Ned through the leg; Jory is killed. Jaime leaves Ned wounded in the street.
6

Season 1 Episode 6: A Golden Crown
Ned wakes from his injuries. Robert restores him as Hand and orders him to make peace with the Lannisters before leaving on a hunt. Cersei is furious; Robert strikes her when she insults him. Arya trains with Syrio even while grieving Jory; Syrio teaches that one must be ready to fight especially in dark times.

On the hunt Robert drinks heavily (kept supplied by Lancel Lannister) and waxes nostalgic; Renly storms off. Back in the city refugees report a huge knight (the Mountain) burning Riverlands villages—Lannister retaliation for Tyrion’s capture. Ned strips Gregor of titles and lands and sends Lord Beric Dondarrion with men to bring him to justice. He summons Tywin Lannister to court or be named traitor. Littlefinger and Pycelle are alarmed at the escalation.

Joffrey apologizes to Sansa (on Cersei’s earlier orders) and gives her a necklace; she forgives him. Ned decides to send the girls home. Sansa protests she will marry Joffrey and have golden-haired babies. That phrase sends Ned back to the lineage book. Every Baratheon-Lannister match produced black-haired children—except Cersei’s three blond ones. He realizes the truth.

At Winterfell Bran rides with his new saddle. Robb and Theon discuss war rumors. Bran wanders off and is attacked by wildlings. Robb kills two; Theon shoots the third who holds a knife to Bran. The survivor Osha yields and is taken prisoner. Ros leaves for King’s Landing, correctly sensing war will empty Winterfell of customers.

At the Eyrie Tyrion nearly rolls out of his sky cell. He bribes the jailer Mord to take a message. Lysa brings him to court expecting a broken confession. Instead Tyrion demands a trial. Since Lysa’s son Robin is a child, Tyrion claims trial by combat. He first names Jaime (absent), then accepts any champion present. Bronn volunteers. In the fight Bronn uses speed and terrain against the heavily armored Ser Vardis Egen, kills him, and kicks the body out the Moon Door. Tyrion is free. He and Bronn leave.

In Vaes Dothrak Daenerys tests a dragon egg in fire; she is unburned while Irri is scalded. She eats a raw stallion heart before the dosh khaleen. The crones prophesy her son will be the Stallion Who Mounts the World. She names him Rhaego after her dead brother. Viserys is jealous. He later tries to steal the dragon eggs; Jorah stops him. Drunk and furious at a feast, Viserys draws a sword in the sacred city (a capital offense) and demands his crown. Drogo “crowns” him by pouring molten gold over his head. Viserys dies screaming. Daenerys watches coldly and says he was no dragon.
7

Season 1 Episode 7: You Win or You Die
On the Riverlands border Tywin Lannister has raised 60,000 men. He tells Jaime this war will make or break their house for a thousand years. He orders Jaime to take half the army and besiege Riverrun. Even the “least” Lannister (Tyrion) must be avenged or the family looks weak.

At Winterfell Theon tries to bully Osha; she is unimpressed. She tells Maester Luwin the wildlings fled south because the White Walkers have returned. Luwin is skeptical.

At the Wall Benjen’s horse returns without him. Jon and the other recruits take their vows. Jon is assigned as Lord Commander Mormont’s personal steward (not a ranger); Sam becomes Maester Aemon’s steward. Sam suggests it may be so Mormont can groom Jon for command. Jon (who keeps the old gods) and Sam swear before a heart tree beyond the Wall. Ghost finds a severed hand in the woods.

In Vaes Dothrak Daenerys tries to persuade Drogo to invade Westeros for their son’s future throne. Drogo is uninterested in an “iron chair.” In the market a wineseller offers her poisoned Arbor gold (an assassination ordered by Robert). Jorah, who has just received a royal pardon via one of Varys’s little birds (realizing he is no longer needed as a spy), stops her from drinking. The seller is captured. Enraged, Drogo vows to cross the “poison water,” take the Iron Throne for his son, and kill the usurper’s men. The khalasar leaves the next day, dragging the wineseller to death.

In King’s Landing Ned confronts Cersei with the truth: her children are Jaime’s, not Robert’s. She does not deny it and is proud, comparing it to old Targaryen custom. She has hated Robert since their wedding night when he called her “Lyanna.” Ned tells her to flee with the children before Robert returns. She warns him: “When you play the game of thrones, you win or you die. There is no middle ground.”

Littlefinger coaches new prostitutes (including Ros) and recounts his past duel for Catelyn and his realization that he must win by cunning, not honor. He wants “everything.”

Renly finds Ned: Robert has been mortally wounded by a boar on the hunt. Ned goes to the dying king. Robert names Ned Protector of the Realm until Joffrey comes of age and asks him to stop the hit on Daenerys. Ned writes “the rightful heir” instead of Joffrey’s name. He does not tell Robert the truth about the children, sparing him. Varys hints that Lancel kept Robert drunk. Renly offers Ned swords to seize Joffrey now; Ned refuses to shed blood while Robert still lives and insists Stannis is the true heir. He writes to Stannis. Littlefinger urges a quieter path—control Joffrey as a puppet or switch to Renly later—but Ned calls it treason. Littlefinger agrees to “help” secure the City Watch.

Robert dies. Ned is summoned to the throne room. Joffrey sits the Iron Throne and demands fealty. Ned presents Robert’s decree. Cersei tears it up and offers Ned a chance to bend the knee and go home. He refuses and orders the City Watch to seize the queen and her children. Instead the gold cloaks turn on Ned’s men. Littlefinger holds a knife to Ned’s throat: “I did warn you not to trust me.”
8

Season 1 Episode 8: The Pointy End
At the Wall Jon and Sam bring back two corpses from Benjen’s party (Jafer and Othor). The bodies do not smell of rot. Mormont wants Maester Aemon to examine them first. News arrives that Ned has been arrested for treason. Jon is devastated; Mormont reminds him of his oath. Alliser Thorne taunts him; Jon attacks and is confined. That night Ghost alerts him. A wight (the reanimated Othor) attacks Mormont’s chambers. Jon’s sword does nothing; he finally destroys it with fire from a lamp. The bodies are burned. Sam has read that only fire kills wights raised by White Walkers.

In the Vale Catelyn is furious that Lysa did not warn her of Ned’s arrest and will not send the knights of the Vale to war. Lysa cares only for her son’s safety. Tyrion and Bronn, free, are captured by hill tribes led by Shagga. Tyrion talks fast, promising them gold, weapons, and vengeance against the Arryns if they help him reach his father. They agree and escort him west.

In the North Robb receives a letter (dictated by Cersei via Sansa) demanding he bend the knee. He refuses and summons the northern banners. At a feast Greatjon Umber challenges Robb’s authority; Grey Wind bites off two of his fingers. Robb turns the moment into dark humor and wins the Greatjon’s fierce loyalty. Robb says goodbye to Bran and Rickon. Osha tells Bran the Old Gods are real and the real war is in the north against what is coming, not the south. Catelyn and Rodrik intercept Robb’s host. She tells him he must win for the family’s sake. They debate strategy: Tywin’s army or Jaime’s at Riverrun. To reach Jaime they need the crossing at the Twins (held by Walder Frey). A Lannister scout is captured and sent back with a message that 20,000 northerners are coming.

Tyrion arrives at Tywin’s camp with the hill tribes. Tywin shows little warmth but accepts the fighters—on condition Tyrion leads them from the front.

Tyrion arrives at Tywin’s camp with the hill tribes. Tywin shows little warmth but accepts the fighters—on condition Tyrion leads them from the front.

In Lhazar the Dothraki raid a peaceful village for slaves and loot to fund ships. Daenerys is horrified by the rapes and killings and claims the remaining women as her own to protect them. An angry warrior named Mago challenges Drogo; Drogo kills him but takes a deep chest wound. Daenerys insists the Lhazareen healer Mirri Maz Duur treat it despite the bloodriders calling her a maegi (witch).

In King’s Landing Lannister men slaughter the Stark household. Septa Mordane tells Sansa to run; the Hound takes Sansa. Ser Meryn Trant and men interrupt Arya’s lesson. Syrio sees they are not Ned’s men. He holds them off with a wooden sword, telling Arya to run: “The First Sword of Braavos does not run.” Arya flees to the stables, finds Needle, and accidentally kills a stableboy who tries to stop her. She escapes via the tunnels. Varys visits Ned in the black cells. He is shocked Ned warned Cersei. Ned’s mercy, Varys says, got Robert killed. Catelyn no longer holds Tyrion, so there is no hostage to trade. Varys serves “the realm.” Cersei’s council forces Sansa to write a letter begging Robb to bend the knee, implying Ned’s life depends on it.
9

Season 1 Episode 9: Baelor
Robb’s army reaches the Twins. Catelyn negotiates with the elderly, lecherous Lord Walder Frey. In exchange for crossing, troops, and support, Robb must marry a Frey daughter and Arya must marry a Frey son; Robb also takes a Frey squire. He agrees.

Tywin plans to use the hill tribes as expendable vanguard and puts Tyrion in front. Tyrion is given the whore Shae by Bronn. The night before battle they play a drinking game. Tyrion tells the story of his secret youthful marriage to Tysha (a common girl Jaime had set up as a kindness). Tywin had the marriage annulled, revealed she was a prostitute, and forced Tyrion to watch as his guards raped her for silver. The memory still wounds him.

Next morning the Starks have stolen a march. Tyrion’s speech to the tribes is cut short when he is knocked unconscious. He wakes to learn the Lannisters “won” a diversionary fight, but Robb’s main force smashed Jaime’s army at the Whispering Wood, lifted the siege of Riverrun, and captured Jaime himself. Robb refuses Jaime’s offer of single combat and has him chained. Two thousand of Robb’s men died in the feint; he tells the army the war is far from over.

At Castle Black Mormont gives Jon the Valyrian steel bastard sword Longclaw (once meant for his own exiled son Jorah) in thanks for saving his life. He is sending Alliser Thorne south with a wight hand as proof. Sam tells Jon that Robb is marching to war. Jon wants to go. Blind Maester Aemon reveals he is Aemon Targaryen—he had to stand by while his family was slaughtered in Robert’s Rebellion. Duty is hard; Jon must choose and live with it.

In the Dothraki Sea Drogo’s wound festers. He falls from his horse—a terrible sign. Daenerys stops the khalasar and has Mirri Maz Duur treat him. The bloodriders are furious. Jorah arms himself and warns Daenerys that when Drogo dies his rivals will kill her and the baby. She refuses to leave. Mirri begins a blood magic ritual, sacrificing Drogo’s prized stallion. As supernatural noises rise from the tent, Qotho attacks Daenerys; Jorah kills him. Daenerys goes into labor. No Dothraki midwife will help the “cursed” woman, so Jorah carries her into the tent.

In King’s Landing Varys urges Ned to confess treason so he can take the black and save Sansa’s life. Ned is torn. Arya lives rough on the streets, catching pigeons. She hears the Hand is being taken to the Great Sept of Baelor and climbs a statue of King Baelor for a view. Ned sees her and mouths “Baelor” to Yoren, who understands and moves to grab her. On the steps Ned looks at both daughters and chooses to save them. He falsely confesses that he betrayed Robert and that Joffrey is the true king. Joffrey pretends he will be merciful and send Ned to the Wall (as Cersei and Sansa begged), then suddenly orders his head instead. The crowd riots. Yoren pulls Arya away and shields her eyes. Sansa screams and faints. Cersei and Varys try to stop it too late. Ser Ilyn Payne uses Ice to behead Ned Stark. Pigeons fly up; Arya knows.
10

Season 1 Episode 10: Fire and Blood
In King’s Landing Ned’s head is mounted on a spike. Yoren cuts Arya’s hair, calls her “boy,” and takes her into a group of Night’s Watch recruits (including Hot Pie, Lommy, and Gendry—Robert’s bastard, now cast out). He warns her half the recruits would sell her to Cersei. They leave the city heading north through war zones. Joffrey has a singer’s tongue cut out for an offensive song, then forces Sansa to look at her father’s head and promises her Robb’s next. She quietly says maybe Robb will give her Joffrey’s. He has Meryn Trant beat her. The Hound quietly wipes her blood and advises her to give the king what he wants. Cersei takes Lancel as a lover. Pycelle drops his frail act in private with Ros. Littlefinger and Varys trade barbs about ambition and the throne.

At Winterfell Bran dreams again of the three-eyed raven flying into the crypts. He and Osha go down; Rickon and Shaggydog are already there—Rickon had the same dream. Outside, Maester Luwin’s face tells them Ned is dead.

In the Riverlands Catelyn receives the northern lords’ condolences, then breaks down alone in the woods. She finds Robb destroying a tree with his sword in grief. They embrace; she promises revenge after they free the girls. At a war council the lords debate allying with Stannis or Renly. Greatjon Umber declares the North was independent before the dragons and will not bow to southern kings now that the dragons are gone. He names Robb the King in the North. The others take up the cry and swear fealty. Catelyn visits the captive Jaime; he taunts her, admits pushing Bran, and says there are no men like him. She hits him with a rock.

At Tywin’s camp the capture of Jaime is a disaster. They now face Robb, Stannis, and Renly. Tyrion points out Ned’s execution ended any chance of easy peace. Tywin decides to fall back to Harrenhal, send Gregor to burn the Riverlands, and dispatch Tyrion to King’s Landing as Acting Hand to control Joffrey and Cersei (and kill schemers if needed). He orders Tyrion to leave Shae behind. Tyrion defies him and takes her anyway.

At the Wall Jon learns of Ned’s death and tries to desert to join Robb. Sam, Grenn, and Pyp stop him and recite the oath. He returns. Mormont overlooks it and tells him the real war is coming from beyond the Wall—wildlings, White Walkers, wights. He will lead a great ranging to learn the truth and find Benjen. Jon recommits.

In the Dothraki Sea Daenerys wakes to learn her son Rhaego was born dead and monstrously deformed. Most of the khalasar has left. Drogo lives but is a vacant shell. Mirri Maz Duur reveals her revenge: the Dothraki destroyed her temple and people; she has taken Drogo’s mind and the child’s life so the Stallion Who Mounts the World will never conquer. Daenerys tends the empty Drogo, then smothers him out of mercy. She builds a funeral pyre, places the dragon eggs on it, and has Mirri bound to the wood. She frees any remaining slaves and invites the few loyal ones to stay as equals. Ignoring Jorah’s pleas, she lights the pyre and walks into the flames. At dawn the fire is ash. Daenerys sits unharmed amid the embers, naked and soot-covered, with three living baby dragons—one on her shoulder, one on her arm, one climbing her leg. Jorah and the remaining Dothraki kneel. The dragons are reborn. The Mother of Dragons rises.

Episode 1: The North Remembers

The Night's Watch ranging party under Lord Commander Jeor Mormont reaches Craster's Keep after passing empty wildling villages. Jon Snow, Samwell Tarly, Grenn, and Eddison Tollett find Craster repulsive. He keeps many wives who are also his daughters and has no sons. Craster claims he has not seen the missing Benjen Stark and says the wildlings are gathering under Mance Rayder, the King-Beyond-the-Wall. Jon challenges Craster's crude insults toward Mormont. Mormont reprimands Jon, explaining that Craster provides needed shelter and information in the harsh lands north of the Wall despite his disgusting ways. Mormont tells Jon that to lead one day he must first learn to follow. The keep is a rough, filthy place filled with Craster's fear and control over his household. The rangers rest uneasily there as the cold winds blow and the threat of what lies further north hangs over them.

In King's Landing, King Joffrey Baratheon celebrates his nameday with a tournament on the walls of the Red Keep. Ser Dontos Hollard arrives late and drunk. Joffrey orders his men to funnel an entire barrel of wine down Dontos's throat until he dies. Sansa Stark steps in, saying it is bad luck to kill on one's nameday. Sandor Clegane supports her. Joffrey makes Dontos his new court fool instead. Tyrion Lannister arrives in the city. Joffrey is disdainful, but Tommen and Myrcella are happy to see their uncle alive. The Small Council meets and learns from the Conclave that the long summer has ended. Cersei orders the city gates closed against war refugees. Tyrion presents Tywin's letter naming him acting Hand of the King. Cersei is furious and suspicious. Tyrion criticizes her failure to control Joffrey and the disastrous decisions, especially Ned Stark's execution, which started the war they are losing

. Cersei is furious and suspicious. Tyrion criticizes her failure to control Joffrey and the disastrous decisions, especially Ned Stark's execution, which started the war they are losing. He is shocked Arya escaped, noting how much better their position would be with three Stark hostages. Tyrion hides Shae in the Tower of the Hand against his father's orders. Shae is excited by the big city.

Cersei tasks Petyr Baelish with finding Arya. She mocks his old love for Catelyn. Baelish hints at her relationship with Jaime, saying knowledge is power. Cersei has her guards seize him and threaten to cut his throat, then stops them, saying power is power. Joffrey redecorates the throne room to make it more intimidating like the Targaryen days. He refuses to ask Tywin for help finding Arya. He blames Tywin for war losses and Jaime's capture. Hearing rumors about his parentage, Joffrey confronts Cersei. She dismisses it as enemy gossip. He asks about Robert's bastards and insults her by saying Robert grew tired of her. She slaps him. He warns her never to hit him again or he will have her killed. Janos Slynt leads a massacre of Robert's bastard children across the city. Baby Barra is killed in Littlefinger's brothel in front of her mother and Ros. Tobho Mott is questioned and reveals Gendry left with the Night's Watch recruits, identifiable by his bull's head helmet
. Tobho Mott is questioned and reveals Gendry left with the Night's Watch recruits, identifiable by his bull's head helmet. Gendry and Arya travel north on the Kingsroad with Yoren's group.

At Winterfell, Bran deals with the petty complaints of vassals unhappy that Robb called the banners and took the young men south. Maester Luwin guides him in lordly duties. Bran dreams he is his direwolf Summer walking in the godswood. Looking in the pool he sees Summer's face instead of his own and wakes. He has Osha and Hodor take him to the pool to confirm his own reflection. They talk about the red comet. Osha believes it means dragons have returned to the world.

On Dragonstone, Stannis Baratheon lets Melisandre burn the statues of the Seven as offerings to the Lord of Light. Maester Cressen is outraged at the insult to the old gods and fears Melisandre is leading Stannis into a hopeless war. Melisandre proclaims Stannis the champion of the Lord of Light as he draws a burning sword from a statue. Cressen asks Davos for help, but Davos says the timing is wrong. Stannis has Ned Stark's letter naming him Robert's true heir. He sends copies across the realm declaring Joffrey a bastard born of incest between Cersei and Jaime and claiming the throne. He rejects Davos's suggestion of alliance with Renly or Robb. Renly has the bigger army but Stannis sees him as a usurper; Robb wants Northern independence which Stannis views as theft of half his kingdom. Cressen pretends to apologize and poisons a cup of wine, hoping Melisandre will share it. Davos sees the poison and tries to stop him. Cressen drinks first then offers it to her

. Cressen pretends to apologize and poisons a cup of wine, hoping Melisandre will share it. Davos sees the poison and tries to stop him. Cressen drinks first then offers it to her. Melisandre drinks unharmed while Cressen dies.

In the Riverlands, Robb receives Stannis's letter. He questions captive Jaime about crippling Bran. Jaime reveals nothing and mocks Robb for keeping him close instead of with a bannerman, showing lack of trust. Robb says he trusts his men but knows the Lannisters would go to any lengths to free Jaime. Grey Wind, nearly grown, menaces Jaime. Robb sends Alton Lannister to King's Landing with peace terms: release of his sisters, return of Ned's bones and those who served him, and recognition of the North as an independent kingdom. Theon asks to go to Pyke to seek alliance with Balon, saying they need ships to attack King's Landing. Catelyn warns against trusting Balon after his past rebellion. She wants to trade Jaime for the girls and return to her younger sons, but Robb sends her to seek alliance with Renly instead and sends Rodrik Cassel to Winterfell.

In the Red Waste, Daenerys leads her small remaining khalasar east to avoid rival khals who would kill her for the dragons. The dragons struggle to eat the little meat available. Her people starve. Her beloved white mare, Drogo's first gift, dies. She stops the march and sends three bloodriders in different directions to scout for food, water, and refuge. The endless red desert stretches around them under a merciless sun, with no end in sight and enemies closing in.

Episode 2: The Night Lands

Episode 2: The Night Lands

In the Riverlands, Arya continues posing as a boy named Arry while traveling with Yoren and the Night's Watch recruits. She urinates in private to hide her sex. She is drawn to the caged prisoners Jaqen H'ghar, Rorge, and Biter. Jaqen asks for water and introduces himself. Gold Cloaks approach seeking Gendry, one of Robert's bastards. Arya hides, thinking they want her. Yoren intimidates them into leaving empty-handed, though they promise to return with more men. Arya asks Gendry why he is wanted. He does not know but recalls being questioned by Jon Arryn and Ned Stark. He has seen through her disguise. Arya reveals she is Arya Stark and makes him swear secrecy.

In King's Landing, Varys finds Shae living with Tyrion in the Tower of the Hand and implies threats about revealing her. Tyrion warns Varys not to underestimate him. Alton delivers Robb's peace terms. Cersei rejects them. Pycelle shares a Night's Watch message requesting men and warning of wights. Only Tyrion takes it seriously. Ros struggles after witnessing Barra's murder. Littlefinger threatens her with a story of selling an unhappy girl to a depraved man to recover his investment and orders her to return happy after a night off. Tyrion dines with Janos Slynt and questions him about the bastard massacre. Janos admits involvement but will not name who ordered it. Tyrion arrests him, exiles him to the Night's Watch, and makes Bronn commander of the City Watch. Cersei confronts Tyrion. He warns she is losing the people's support. She claims not to care. He realizes Joffrey ordered the killings. He jokes about her and Jaime

. Cersei confronts Tyrion. He warns she is losing the people's support. She claims not to care. He realizes Joffrey ordered the killings. He jokes about her and Jaime. She says he has always been funny, then ends by saying his finest joke was killing their mother in childbirth.

On Dragonstone, Davos recruits the Lysene sellsail Salladhor Saan and his thirty ships for Stannis. Matthos urges Davos to learn to read the Lord of Light texts, but Davos puts his faith in Stannis alone. Melisandre seduces Stannis with the promise of a son. He hesitates because of his wife Selyse but gives in.

On the Iron Islands, Theon arrives by merchant ship after sleeping with the captain's daughter. He expects a warm welcome but no one meets him at Lordsport. A woman offers him a ride to Pyke and he tries to seduce her. Balon questions Theon's loyalty after nine years as a Stark ward. Theon delivers Robb's letter offering alliance against the Lannisters and a crown for Balon. The guide enters and Balon greets her warmly—she is Theon's sister Yara. Balon rejects the offer, comparing Theon unfavorably to Yara. He will pay the iron price and take what he wants by force. No one gives him a crown. When Theon says he cannot beat the Lannisters, Balon replies he has no intention of fighting them.

In the Red Waste, Daenerys's khalasar waits exhausted for the bloodriders, water nearly gone. Rakharo's horse returns riderless. Jorah finds his head and severed braid in the saddlebag. A rival khalasar killed him. Irri is devastated, believing the mutilation bars him from the Night Lands. Daenerys promises a funeral.

At Craster's Keep, Sam rescues Gilly from Ghost when the direwolf bothers her for food. She confides she wants to flee because she fears what Craster will do if her unborn child is a boy. She begs Jon to take her, but will not say why. Jon says it is impossible as they go deeper into wildling lands. Sam and Jon argue about it. Jon later sees Craster take a baby into the woods at night. He follows and watches Craster leave the child for the White Walkers. Before Jon can act, Craster knocks him out.

Episode 3: What Is Dead May Never Die

Episode 3: What Is Dead May Never Die

Craster drags the beaten Jon back to the keep after catching him spying on the baby sacrifice. He orders the Night's Watch out, blaming Jon. Mormont questions Jon and reveals he has long known Craster sacrifices his sons. Craster is too valuable for information and shelter to risk offending. Mormont is disgusted by the incest and sacrifices but will not interfere, forbidding Jon from doing so. Craster has helped many, including Benjen. Jon says he saw something take the child. Mormont says Jon will see it again. Sam gives Gilly a thimble that belonged to his mother and promises to return for her.

At Winterfell, Bran dreams of seeing through Summer's eyes, following Hodor into his own bedroom and looking down on himself sleeping. He tells Luwin, who dismisses the dreams as unimportant.

At Winterfell, Bran dreams of seeing through Summer's eyes, following Hodor into his own bedroom and looking down on himself sleeping. He tells Luwin, who dismisses the dreams as unimportant.

In the Stormlands, Catelyn arrives at Renly's camp during a tournament. She watches Brienne of Tarth defeat Loras Tyrell and win a place in Renly's Kingsguard. Renly introduces his new wife Margaery Tyrell and shows off his 100,000-strong army. Catelyn warns him to take the war seriously. Renly tries to have sex with Loras but is rebuffed. Loras reminds him of the need for an heir and fetches Margaery. She fails to seduce Renly but is pragmatic about his preferences and suggests including her brother, stressing the importance of producing an heir.

On the Iron Islands, Theon sits in Balon's war council. Balon plans to attack the lightly defended North while its armies fight the Lannisters. Theon is assigned one ship to raid Stony Shore fishing villages while Yara commands thirty ships to take Deepwood Motte. Theon begs reconsideration, saying attacking the North risks total destruction if they lose, while allying with the Starks could win Balon the Iron Islands crown plus Casterly Rock. Balon refuses and hits him for his Stark loyalty. Theon considers warning Robb but instead reaffirms family loyalty by being baptized by a Drowned Man, drowning and rising again.

In King's Landing, Shae complains of confinement. Tyrion works with Varys to find her a job for more freedom. Cersei hosts an awkward dinner with her children and captive Sansa. Sansa maintains her loyal façade. Shae arrives as Sansa's new handmaiden, giving Sansa someone to confide in. Tyrion tests Small Council loyalty by feeding each a different marriage plan for Myrcella. Cersei confronts him about the plan given to Pycelle, exposing Pycelle as her spy. Tyrion insists on the Dornish marriage alliance over Cersei's protests and has Bronn arrest Pycelle. Littlefinger is angry at being used. Tyrion offers him the chance to act as envoy to Renly and Catelyn.

In the Riverlands, Arya suffers insomnia. Yoren advises her to focus on retribution for her painful memories. Ser Amory Lorch arrives with Lannister men and Gold Cloaks demanding Gendry. Yoren refuses and fights bravely but dies. Arya frees Jaqen from a burning prisoner wagon. Lommy picks up Gendry's helmet and is wounded. Polliver takes Needle from Arya. Gendry and Hot Pie are captured. Lommy begs to be carried; Polliver stabs him in the throat with Needle. Arya claims Lommy was Gendry because of the helmet. The prisoners are taken to Harrenhal.

Episode 4: Garden of Bones

Episode 4: Garden of Bones

Robb's Northern army launches a surprise night assault on a Lannister camp at Oxcross. Grey Wind causes heavy damage. It is a crushing victory, another Whispering Wood as Robb promised Cersei. The next day Silent Sisters tend the wounded. Roose Bolton argues for killing all Lannister prisoners because supplies are short and prisoners slow them down. Robb refuses, insisting on honorable conduct under the laws of war so the Lannisters have no excuse to torture Sansa and Arya. Robb sees Talisa of Volantis treating a wounded Lannister soldier whose leg must be amputated. He helps hold the man down. Talisa criticizes the war. Robb wants only revenge on Joffrey for Ned's death and independence for the North afterward; he does not care who takes the Iron Throne. She points out he has not hurt the real killers, Joffrey and Tywin, and has slaughtered unwilling boy soldiers instead of Tywin's main force.

Arya, Gendry, and Hot Pie arrive at Harrenhal with other prisoners under Amory Lorch. The vast ruined castle still bears the scars of dragonfire from Aegon's Conquest. Gregor Clegane, the Mountain, commands. The stench of corpses is overwhelming. The Tickler and others sadistically torture prisoners—tying a rat in a bucket to a man's belly and heating it so the rat eats through him—seeking hidden valuables or information on the Brotherhood Without Banners. Gendry is about to be tortured when Tywin arrives with the main Lannister host retreating after Whispering Wood. Tywin halts the tortures as inefficient and puts the prisoners to work. He immediately notices "Arry" is a girl and is impressed by her intelligence when she explains dressing as a boy was safer. He makes her his cupbearer.

In King's Landing, Joffrey is furious at Robb's victory. He has Sansa brought before the court in the redecorated throne room. Lancel claims Robb won by trickery and sorcery. Joffrey threatens Sansa with a crossbow, considering killing her as a message. She refuses to show fear and pledges loyalty. He has Meryn Trant beat and strip her, ordering her face left pretty. The court watches in horror; no one intervenes. Sandor is disgusted. Tyrion storms in, stops it, and has Sandor cover her with his cloak. He berates Joffrey for shaming his future queen and hostage, calling him a halfwit and comparing him to the Mad King. When Meryn speaks, Tyrion orders Bronn to kill him if he opens his mouth again. Tyrion comforts Sansa. She still claims love and duty for Joffrey. Tyrion respects her survival skills. Bronn suggests giving Joffrey prostitutes to release frustration. Tyrion sends Ros and Daisy

. Tyrion comforts Sansa. She still claims love and duty for Joffrey. Tyrion respects her survival skills. Bronn suggests giving Joffrey prostitutes to release frustration. Tyrion sends Ros and Daisy. Joffrey forces Ros at crossbow-point to beat Daisy unconscious and dump her in Tyrion's chambers as a warning. Late at night Lancel delivers Cersei's order to free Pycelle. Tyrion traps him into admitting he comes from Cersei's bed smelling of her perfume. Tyrion blackmails Lancel into spying on Cersei, threatening to tell Joffrey that Lancel killed Robert and sleeps with his mother.

In the Stormlands, Littlefinger arrives at Renly's camp as Joffrey's envoy. He hints he can help from inside if Renly marches on the capital. He tries to intimidate Margaery about Renly's preferences, but she already knows and does not care; she entered the marriage for the Tyrell-Renly alliance. He meets Catelyn, who is still furious at his betrayal of Ned. He tries to rekindle romance; she draws a dagger. He presents Tyrion's offer of a prisoner exchange—Jaime for Sansa and Arya (lying that they have Arya)—and as good faith brings Ned's bones. Catelyn grieves then hardens with resolve. Stannis arrives with Melisandre and Davos to demand Renly yield. Renly refuses, citing his huge army. Catelyn criticizes both brothers for childishness. Stannis offers Renly his old Small Council seat and to name him heir if he yields. Renly declines. Melisandre warns Renly the night is dark and full of terrors. Later Davos rows pregnant Melisandre through caves near Renly's camp

. Renly declines. Melisandre warns Renly the night is dark and full of terrors. Later Davos rows pregnant Melisandre through caves near Renly's camp. She births a shadow creature as Davos watches in horror.

In Qarth, Kovarro returns with news of the city. The desert around it is called the Garden of Bones because those turned away die of thirst. Daenerys reaches the gates. The Thirteen demand to see the dragons first. She insists her people be fed and sheltered. They refuse and prepare to abandon her. She swears fire and blood vengeance. Xaro Xhoan Daxos vouchsafes for her with a blood oath. They are allowed inside.

Episode 5: The Ghost of Harrenhal

Episode 5: The Ghost of Harrenhal

Renly is assassinated in his tent by the shadow baby Melisandre birthed with Stannis, just after agreeing to ally with Robb. Brienne is blamed and flees with Catelyn. Brienne swears fealty to Catelyn. Renly's army collapses; the Tyrells return to Highgarden while others join Stannis. Littlefinger goes with the Tyrells, seeing opportunity. Davos challenges Stannis on using Melisandre's magic and convinces him to leave her behind for the attack on King's Landing to avoid rumors. Stannis puts Davos in command of the fleet. Alone, Stannis briefly grieves his brother.

Tyrion brings news of Renly's death to Cersei. She is pleased, but he predicts Stannis's attack. She keeps defense plans secret. Through Lancel, Tyrion learns she has been meeting the Alchemists' Guild. He visits Wisdom Hallyne and discovers thousands of jars of wildfire stockpiled as catapult ammunition. Bronn warns it could burn the city itself if mishandled. Tyrion takes control of the wildfire from Cersei. He passes a street protest blaming him for the city's ills.

Theon takes command of his ship but finds the crew insubordinate. Dagmer says he must prove himself. Theon plans a feint on Torrhen's Square to draw Winterfell's remaining forces away. It works; Rodrik leads 200 men to relieve it.

Bran gives good counsel but is troubled by dreams of a three-eyed raven. Osha will not interpret. He also dreams of the sea flooding Winterfell and drowning people including Rodrik.

Bran gives good counsel but is troubled by dreams of a three-eyed raven. Osha will not interpret. He also dreams of the sea flooding Winterfell and drowning people including Rodrik.

At Harrenhal, Tywin holds a long war council on strategy against Robb. Arya serves as cupbearer. Tywin realizes she is Northern and questions her without knowing her identity. She avoids revealing herself. Fetching water she meets Jaqen, now a Lannister man-at-arms. Because she saved him and the other two prisoners, he owes her three deaths. She names the Tickler. Soon the Tickler is found dead with his neck twisted completely around. Jaqen signals to Arya from above.

The Night's Watch reaches the Fist of the First Men and meets scout Qhorin. He warns their tactics must change against Mance Rayder's army and suggests a small party to neutralize lookouts in the Skirling Pass. Jon joins Qhorin's group. Sam becomes Mormont's steward.

In Qarth, Daenerys has taught her dragons to breathe fire on command and they eat meat independently. Xaro hosts a gathering. She is disturbed by warlock Pyat Pree's tricks and his invitation to the House of the Undying. Quaithe warns Jorah that Daenerys needs protection from those who lust after her dragons. Xaro offers to fund her Westeros invasion for her hand in marriage. Jorah advises against accepting and reveals his feelings for her, which she does not return. He says she can win her throne with just one ship if she reaches Westeros.

Episode 6: The Old Gods and the New

Episode 6: The Old Gods and the New

At Winterfell, Luwin frantically sends a raven. Theon and Ironborn raiders take the undefended castle after the Torrhen's Square feint. Theon uses grappling claws to infiltrate. He forces Bran to surrender to save the people. Rodrik is captured returning from Torrhen's Square. He spits on Theon. Dagmer insists Theon must kill him or lose face. Theon botches the beheading with multiple hacks and a kick, horrifying everyone. That night Osha sleeps with Theon then sneaks out, frees Bran, Rickon, Hodor, and the direwolves, kills a guard, and escapes.

In the Westerlands, Robb talks with Talisa, who has followed the army. He introduces her to Catelyn and Brienne, returned from the Stormlands. Roose brings Luwin's raven news of Winterfell's fall. Robb wants to march north immediately. Roose advises leaving it to his bastard Ramsay Snow at the Dreadfort with the remaining Northern forces. Retreating the main army would lose all gains. Robb agrees but wants Theon taken alive so he can ask "why" before executing him.

At Harrenhal, Tywin berates Amory Lorch for delivering a letter to enemies because he cannot read. He discovers Arya can read. Littlefinger arrives and discusses Renly's death, Stannis gaining Stormlands houses, and the Tyrells staying neutral at Highgarden. They discuss a possible Lannister-Tyrell alliance. Tywin questions Arya further. She steals a letter about Robb while he is distracted. Amory sees her with it and grows suspicious. She runs to Jaqen and names Amory as the second death, urgently. Amory dies of a poisoned dart just as he reaches Tywin.

In King's Landing, the court sees Myrcella off to Dorne for the marriage alliance with Trystane Martell. Cersei is heartbroken and blames Tyrion. The streets overflow with starving refugees. On the return, a crowd throws cow dung in Joffrey's face. He orders the entire crowd killed. Riots erupt. The High Septon is torn apart. The royal party barely escapes. Tyrion slaps Joffrey for the stupidity that endangered them all. Sansa is lost in the crowd and nearly raped by a mob before Sandor kills her attackers and carries her to safety. Tyrion thanks him; Sandor says he did not do it for Tyrion.

Beyond the Wall, Qhorin's scouting party fights wildling scouts and captures red-haired Ygritte. Qhorin orders Jon to execute her while the others continue. Jon hesitates; she runs. He catches her but they are separated. Night falls; they must camp together.

In Qarth, Daenerys fails to get ships from the Spice King, who sees her as too risky with no army or Westerosi supporters. Returning to Xaro's, she finds her guards dead, Irri strangled, and the dragons stolen. A hooded figure carries them away in a box.

Episode 7: A Man Without Honor

At Winterfell, Theon wakes to find Osha, Hodor, Bran, Rickon, and the wolves gone. He beats Black Lorren for letting it happen (Lorren notes Theon slept with Osha). Theon hunts with hounds. At a farm they find walnut shells proving the boys were there, but the scent is lost. Theon ends the hunt, saying his mercy is exhausted, and returns. He hangs two burned small children's bodies on the gates. Luwin cries out, believing Bran and Rickon dead.

At Harrenhal, Tywin discusses Amory's assassination with Gregor, convinced it targeted him. Gregor blames the Brotherhood. Tywin orders villages burned in reprisal. Tywin suspects Arya is highborn because she says "my lord" properly instead of "m'lord" and has an educated way of speaking. She claims her mother was a handmaiden who taught her.

In King's Landing, Sansa thanks Sandor for saving her. He says a dog needs no courage against rats and warns that one day his violence will be all that stands between her and Joffrey. Sansa wakes to bloody sheets from her first period. She panics, knowing it means she must marry and bear Joffrey's child. Shae helps hide the sheets, but Sandor finds them. Sansa is brought to Cersei, who tries to comfort her in her way. Cersei describes Robert abandoning her in childbirth while Jaime stayed, and says Sansa should never expect such from Joffrey. Love only your children, Cersei advises, because loving others makes you weak. "You can try" to love Joffrey. Privately Cersei regrets her children with Jaime and wonders if Joffrey's nature is the price of their sins. Tyrion points out Myrcella and Tommen are good. They share a moment of sympathy.

In the Westerlands, Alton returns with Cersei's rejection of peace terms. Robb imprisons him with Jaime. Talisa needs medical supplies; Robb invites her to the Crag to get them. That night Jaime kills Alton to lure guard Torrhen Karstark into the cell, strangles him, and escapes, but is recaptured. Torrhen was Rickard Karstark's son. Rickard demands Jaime's head. Catelyn argues to spare him as a valuable hostage. She confronts Jaime, calling him without honor. Jaime explains his Kingsguard vows required defending the innocent and serving the king, but the Mad King slaughtered innocents. Honor and loyalty are naïve or hypocritical. He says he has only been with Cersei and mocks Ned for fathering a bastard. Catelyn reaches breaking point and asks for Brienne's sword.

Beyond the Wall, Jon travels with captive Ygritte, still separated. They argue about freedom, oaths, and whose lands are whose. Jon says as Ned's son and a Northman he has First Men blood like her. She asks why the Watch fights wildlings when the only difference is living north of the Wall when it was built. She mocks his virginity and offers to teach him. She escapes and leads him into an ambush, saying he should have taken her when he had the chance.

In Qarth, Daenerys desperately seeks her dragons. Jorah returns; she orders him to find them. Xaro claims distress at breaking his protection promise. Quaithe tells Jorah the thief is already with Daenerys and knows Jorah once spied on her. Daenerys pleads with the Thirteen. Pyat Pree confesses to the theft and declares Xaro King of Qarth. Magical doubles of Pyat slit the other Thirteen members' throats. Xaro and Pyat had allied. Pyat urges Daenerys to the House of the Undying for her dragons.
8

Episode 8: The Prince of Winterfell

Episode 8: The Prince of Winterfell

Ygritte brings Jon before the Lord of Bones, who wants him executed since he already has Qhorin. Ygritte spares him for his Stark blood. Qhorin plans for Jon to spy among the wildlings. At the Fist, Grenn and Sam find a cache of dragonglass weapons. Jon's absence is noted; Sam refuses to believe he is dead.

In Qarth, Jorah advises Daenerys to abandon the dragons and flee; he has passage to Astapor. She insists on reclaiming them and has him lead her to the House of the Undying.

At Winterfell, Yara arrives with few men, not reinforcements. She advises Theon that Winterfell is too far inland, poorly defended with so few, and the North is rising. She urges him to abandon it and come home. He refuses. Dagmer admits that after killing the orphan boys he also killed the farmer and wife.

Luwin sees Osha enter the crypts and follows. She explains they doubled back using a stream to hide their scent. Luwin urges her not to tell Bran and Rickon about the murdered children. Bran overhears.

Stannis's fleet nears King's Landing. He admires Davos and offers him the Hand of the King position once he takes the throne.

In King's Landing, Tyrion studies history for defense ideas, takes advice from Bronn and Varys, and decides to use the wildfire. Joffrey is full of bravado; Cersei worries and kidnaps Ros, thinking she is Tyrion's lover, as collateral. Tyrion hides his relief that Shae is safe and vows revenge on Cersei.

At Harrenhal, Tywin is torn between defending King's Landing and driving Robb from the Westerlands. Kevan warns Stannis will kill Cersei and Joffrey. Tywin marches west, leaving Arya to serve Gregor. Episode 9: Blackwater

On Tyrion's torch signal from the walls, Bronn fires a flaming arrow from shore, igniting a massive explosion that devastates Stannis's fleet, destroys Davos's ship, and kills Matthos.

Mandon betrays and slashes Tyrion's face. Podrick kills Mandon from behind. Tyrion, barely conscious, sees the battle seemingly lost.

Cersei takes Tommen to the throne room, sits on the Iron Throne with him, tells a story of a young lion who need not fear the wolf or stag, and prepares lethal nightshade doses. Tywin and the Tyrells arrive with cavalry, led by a knight in Renly's armor (Loras). They smash Stannis's forces. Survivors flee. Stannis is dragged away screaming for his men to fight. Tyrion collapses as the tide turns. Tywin enters the throne room announcing victory just as Cersei is about to kill Tommen. Loras reveals himself.

Tyrion recovers in shabby new quarters from Mandon's wound. Pycelle gloats that Tywin has returned and taken over as Hand; Tyrion is no longer acting Hand. In the Riverlands, Arya, Gendry, and Hot Pie meet Jaqen, who waited for them. He offers to take Arya to Braavos to learn his killing arts. She declines to find her family. In Qarth, Daenerys enters the House of the Undying and is separated from Jorah and Kovarro. She leaves after touching the child's hair. Back in the room her dragons are chained. Pyat Pree appears, saying she and they restored his magic, and chains her. Unafraid, she says "Dracarys." She locks Xaro and Doreah inside to die and takes enough wealth to buy a ship. The Dothraki seize the rest as she watches with her dragons.

Beyond the Wall, Jon and Qhorin are taken to Mance Rayder's camp by the Lord of Bones. Qhorin sacrifices himself so Jon can pose as a deserter spy. He attacks Jon, insulting his parentage to enrage him. Ygritte returns Jon's sword. Jon kills Qhorin, who whispers "We are the watchers on the Wall" as he dies. The wildlings free Jon, believing he betrayed his oath. Ygritte shows him Mance's vast army in the valley and takes him to their king.

At the Fist of the First Men, Sam, Grenn, and Edd hear three horn blasts—the signal for White Walkers. They run back. Sam is left behind in a sudden blizzard. He hides and watches dozens of wights led by a White Walker on an undead horse pass. The Walker ignores him, raises an ice spear, shrieks, and the army of hundreds advances on the Fist.

Episode 1: Valar Dohaeris
Beyond the Wall, the Night's Watch faces disaster. In the darkness and blizzard at the Fist of the First Men, White Walkers and their army of undead wights overrun the camp of Lord Commander Jeor Mormont. Screams and clashes of steel fill the night as the three hundred black brothers are slaughtered. Samwell Tarly stumbles through the snow looking for safety. He comes across a decapitated brother whose head has been placed in his own hands. A wight with an axe lurches toward Sam. Ghost, Jon Snow’s white direwolf, leaps in and tears at the creature. The wight keeps crawling until Mormont arrives with a torch and sets it ablaze, destroying it. Only a few dozen men survive. Mormont is furious that Sam failed to send any ravens during the chaos. He orders an immediate retreat south to the Wall. They must warn Castle Black and the rest of Westeros, or everyone they know will die. The survivors limp south through the cold, exhausted and broken.

Meanwhile, Jon Snow is taken by Ygritte and the Lord of Bones into the main wildling camp in the Frostfangs. The Free Folk are not just an army—women, children, and entire clans are moving south to escape the White Walkers. Jon sees a real giant lumber past carrying mammoth bones. Wildlings shout “Crow!” at his black cloak and throw ice and stones until Ygritte drives them off. Inside Mance Rayder’s tent, the Lord of Bones presents Jon as Eddard Stark’s bastard who killed Qhorin Halfhand. Jon kneels before a large bearded man eating chicken, calling him “Your Grace.” The wildlings roar with laughter. That man is only Tormund Giantsbane. Mance himself sits quietly in a corner—an unassuming former Night’s Watch brother. No one kneels among the Free Folk. Mance is glad Jon killed Qhorin, who had slain many of his people, though Qhorin was once his brother. Jon claims he wants freedom, but Mance suspects he wants to play the hero

. Mance is glad Jon killed Qhorin, who had slain many of his people, though Qhorin was once his brother. Jon claims he wants freedom, but Mance suspects he wants to play the hero. Jon tells the truth: at Craster’s Keep he watched Craster leave newborn sons in the woods for the White Walkers, and Mormont knew and did nothing. Jon wants to fight for the living, as the First Men once did against the Long Night. Mance accepts him and tells him to get a new cloak. Jon is now among the Free Folk.

In King’s Landing the Lannisters celebrate victory after the Battle of the Blackwater. Tywin Lannister coldly informs his son Tyrion that he intends to disinherit him. Jaime gave up his inheritance by joining the Kingsguard, so Tyrion should be next, but Tywin refuses to believe Tyrion did anything useful as acting Hand. He calls Tyrion a whore-mongering, drunken, spiteful creature who lies out of envy. Tywin is especially angry that Tyrion brought Shae to the capital against orders. When Tyrion asks why, Tywin says Tyrion killed his mother Joanna in childbirth. The laws force Tywin to let Tyrion keep the name Lannister, but he wishes he could prove the boy was not his. Tyrion fumes to his newly knighted sellsword Bronn, now Ser Bronn of the Blackwater.

Joffrey rides in a palanquin from the Great Sept. Margaery Tyrell suddenly stops the procession in Flea Bottom. She gets out, walks among the poor, visits an orphanage, and has her servants hand out bread and toys. The smallfolk love her. That evening Joffrey and Cersei dine with Margaery and Loras. Cersei scolds Margaery for the charity, reminding her those same streets saw the royal party assaulted weeks earlier. Joffrey defends Margaery and criticizes his mother. Cersei realizes Margaery wins love while she only rules through fear. Sansa and Shae sit on the docks watching ships. Littlefinger arrives and hints he can smuggle Sansa out on his next voyage. Sansa is eager but warns she is a terrible liar. Ros, working for Littlefinger, asks Shae to watch over Sansa.

Davos Seaworth is pulled from the sea by Salladhor Saan after the wildfire explosion. Mourning his son Matthos, Davos learns Melisandre has begun burning people alive who speak against her. He convinces Salladhor to take him to Dragonstone. There Stannis sits broken with Melisandre. Davos calls her his enemy and blames her for the disaster. She turns it back on him—he kept her from the battle. When she mentions Matthos, Davos draws a knife. Guards stop him and Stannis throws him in the dungeon.

In the Riverlands Robb Stark’s army takes Harrenhal, but Tywin has already withdrawn. The courtyards are filled with the bodies of two hundred Northern and Riverlands prisoners massacred by the Lannisters. One survivor remains—the maester Qyburn. Morale is low. Robb has won every battle, but the Lannisters now refuse to fight him head-on and simply wait him out while gaining the Tyrells as allies.

Daenerys Targaryen’s ship reaches Astapor in Slaver’s Bay. Her dragons are the size of small dogs. They fly around the ship, snatching fish and roasting them mid-air. They are still too small for war. She needs an army. Jorah suggests the Unsullied, the elite slave eunuch soldiers of Astapor, said to be among the finest in the world. Slavery is illegal in Westeros, but they have no better option. Daenerys wants more Dothraki, but Jorah says other khalasars will only join a strong queen who already has an army. She decides to look into buying the Unsullied.

The massacre continues outside the Twins. Frey men butcher the Stark camp. Robb’s body is desecrated—his head replaced with Grey Wind’s—and paraded while Freys chant “King in the North.” The Hound rides away with unconscious Arya under a Frey banner. At the Dreadfort Ramsay forces Theon to accept the name Reek after more torment. On Pyke Balon receives Theon’s severed penis and a demand to withdraw. He is indifferent. Yara gathers men and a fast ship to rescue her brother.

Arya and the Hound pass Freys bragging about the desecration. Arya stabs one in the neck with the Hound’s knife, whispers “valar morghulis,” and recovers her coin.

In King’s Landing Tyrion and Sansa walk; she is learning to ignore mockery. News of the Red Wedding arrives. Joffrey wants Robb’s head served at his own wedding. Tyrion forbids it. SEASON 3, EPISODE 1 — “Valar Dohaeris”

SEASON 3, EPISODE 1 — “Valar Dohaeris”

Beyond the Wall, the Night’s Watch survivors are in full retreat after the disaster at the Fist of the First Men. Sam is nearly killed by a wight in the blizzard chaos, but he’s saved as the remaining brothers regroup under Jeor Mormont’s command. 1

At the wildling camp, Jon is marched through a rough, crowded world that’s nothing like Castle Black’s rigid order—he even sees a giant among them. He’s brought before Mance Rayder and quickly learns that surviving here means telling a story people want to believe. Jon finally earns Mance’s attention by condemning Craster’s baby sacrifices and claiming the Night’s Watch leadership tolerated it, painting himself as a man disgusted by “southern” hypocrisy and Watch weakness. 
1

In King’s Landing, Tyrion crawls out of the shadow of the Blackwater: scarred, bitter, and convinced his own family tried to finish him off. Across the Narrow Sea, Daenerys reaches Astapor and is shown the Unsullied: disciplined slave-soldiers built through cruelty. SEASON 3, EPISODE 2 — “Dark Wings, Dark Words”

SEASON 3, EPISODE 2 — “Dark Wings, Dark Words”

With Mance’s host, Jon learns the wildlings aren’t one nation—they’re many rival peoples forced into one desperate migration. Mance makes the stakes plain: if they don’t get south, they die. He also introduces Jon to the reality of wargs in wildling society through Orell, whose scouting isn’t rumor or superstition but a living weapon. Meanwhile on the Watch’s side of the story, Sam collapses from exhaustion and shame, and Jeor Mormont brutally shuts down any talk of abandoning him. 
2

In the North, Bran’s “three-eyed raven” dreams sharpen into something more like a calling. Jojen and Meera Reed find the group, and Jojen explains that Bran’s abilities aren’t just wolf-dreams: there’s a wider kind of seeing tied to the raven—visions that can reach across time and truth. 2

In King’s Landing, Sansa is handled gently and then cornered expertly by the Tyrells—especially Olenna—who want the truth about Joffrey before marrying him to Margaery. 2

Elsewhere, Theon wakes into a nightmare of systematic torture that doesn’t even seem to have a clear goal beyond breaking him. SEASON 3, EPISODE 3 — “Walk of Punishment”

Tywin takes control of the Small Council the way he takes control of everything: by quietly forcing everyone to reveal what they are. Beyond the Wall and at Craster’s Keep, survival strips away the Watch’s pretense of unity. Craster’s “hospitality” is a trap made of insults and domination, but the Watch is too desperate to refuse. SEASON 3, EPISODE 5 — “Kissed by Fire”

SEASON 3, EPISODE 6 — “The Climb”

SEASON 3, EPISODE 7 — “The Bear and the Maiden Fair”

SEASON 3, EPISODE 8 — “Second Sons”

In King’s Landing, Tyrion and Sansa are pushed into marriage at swordpoint wrapped in ceremony. In the Riverlands, Arya tries to kill the Hound in his sleep, but he’s already awake—always half-expecting betrayal. Beyond the Wall, Sam’s fear finally breaks into action when a White Walker attacks. His steel sword shatters against it, but dragonglass works: Sam kills the Walker and saves Gilly’s baby, proving the Night’s Watch has a weapon that matters—and that the war to come is not folklore.
