SEASON 3, EPISODE 9 — “The Rains of Castamere”

SEASON 3, EPISODE 9 — “The Rains of Castamere”

In the North and around the Wall, several storylines collide in one stormy night. Bran’s group hides in an abandoned mill as Jon and the wildlings raid nearby; Hodor’s fear nearly gives them away, and Bran uses warging to silence him by taking over his mind. The wildlings try to force Jon to kill an innocent old man to prove loyalty; Jon can’t do it, and Ygritte kills the man instead, confirming Jon’s heart isn’t with them. When the wildlings turn on Jon, Bran—warging into Summer—helps create the opening Jon needs to escape back toward the Wall. Bran then makes a painful choice: he tells Osha to take Rickon away to safety, splitting what remains of the Stark children’s path. 
9

Across the Narrow Sea, Daenerys commits to the invasion of Yunkai with a small strike team: Daario, Jorah, and Grey Worm infiltrate through a rear gate plan. They fight through an ambush and succeed, returning to Daenerys with the city effectively in her hands. It’s a preview of the kind of campaign she intends to run—surgical violence aimed at changing a system, not just taking a throne. 
9

At the Twins, the story becomes tragedy. Robb’s army arrives and is given bread and salt—guest right—supposedly guaranteeing safety under Walder Frey’s roof. Robb apologizes, Walder performs hospitality with a sneer, and the wedding proceeds: Edmure is surprised to find Roslin kind and beautiful, and the feast begins in a deceptively normal swirl of music and drink. But the doors close, and the Lannister song begins. Catelyn’s instincts scream, and then the massacre erupts—Talisa is murdered, Robb is shot and finished, Grey Wind is killed, and Arya arrives just in time to see the betrayal’s full horror before the Hound drags her away. Catelyn’s final attempt to bargain fails, and she is executed after retaliating. 
9

SEASON 3, EPISODE 10 — “Mhysa”

SEASON 3, EPISODE 10 — “Mhysa”

In King’s Landing, the capital reacts to the Red Wedding not with grief but with power-politics. Tyrion and Sansa share a rare moment of mutual understanding as two people trapped by the same system—until Tyrion learns Robb and Catelyn are dead. Joffrey wants Robb’s head brought to the city as a “gift” to Sansa, pushing Tyrion close to violence again, and Tywin responds by asserting dominance the only way he can: he has Joffrey restrained and sedated, showing that even the king is manageable when the real authority decides it. 
10

Varys tries to remove Shae from the board by offering her diamonds and a new life in Essos, framing it as protection for Tyrion as much as mercy for her. Shae refuses, choosing pride, love, anger—or some blend of all three—over flight. Jaime, Brienne, and Qyburn arrive in the city, and Jaime immediately runs toward the one person he still defines as “home”: Cersei. 
10

At the Twins, the Freys celebrate their crime openly by desecrating Robb’s corpse—an image that pushes Arya over the edge. She attacks a Frey soldier in pure rage, and the Hound kills the rest, saving her even while he continues treating her like property to be sold. Walder and Roose discuss their rewards—Riverrun and the North—while Bolton casually reveals Ramsay’s brutality at Winterfell, confirming that the new order will be held together by terror, not legitimacy. 
10

In the North, Bran’s path briefly intersects with the Night’s Watch: Sam recognizes him and helps take Bran’s group through a hidden passage at the Wall, giving them dragonglass before they separate. Sam and Gilly reach Castle Black and warn Maester Aemon, who sends ravens across Westeros about the White Walkers’ return. Jon limps back to Castle Black after Ygritte shoots him multiple times as he flees, and the Watch takes him in—his cover as a wildling shattered, his war with them now inevitable. Meanwhile, Theon’s story hits its bleak reveal: the “rescuer” is Ramsay, and Theon is forced into a new identity—“Reek”—through violence and humiliation. 
10

On the Iron Islands, Balon receives a grotesque message from Ramsay, and Yara chooses action over her father’s pride, sailing with a small force to attempt a rescue. At Dragonstone, Davos tries to save Gendry by smuggling him out, but is caught—only to stay alive because the letter from the Wall forces Stannis to confront a larger war than his claim to the throne. Melisandre burns the message and sees the coming conflict in the flames, redirecting Stannis northward. 
10

Across the Narrow Sea, Daenerys walks into the role she’s been chasing all season: not just conqueror, but liberator. The freed people of Yunkai surge toward her, chanting “mhysa”—“mother”—and lift her above the crowd as her dragons fly overhead. It’s a triumphant image, but also a warning: devotion can become a weapon, and liberation creates expectations that can crush the liberator if she can’t meet them. 
10

Season 4 Overview (Story Context)
The War of the Five Kings nears its end after Robb Stark’s death at the Red Wedding. The Lannisters control much of Westeros with Tywin as Hand, but face internal tensions, the Tyrell alliance via Joffrey’s wedding to Margaery, Dornish demands for justice over Elia Martell’s death, and Stannis still holding out. Sansa is married to Tyrion; Arya travels with the Hound; Bran seeks the Three-Eyed Raven beyond the Wall; Jon prepares Castle Black against Mance Rayder’s wildling army (with raiders already south of the Wall under Tormund, Styr, and Ygritte). Daenerys marches on Meereen with dragons and Unsullied, freeing slaves. Theon (as Reek) suffers under Ramsay Snow/Bolton. Littlefinger maneuvers with Sansa toward the Vale. White Walkers and wights loom farther north.
1

Episode 1: Two Swords
In King’s Landing, Tywin Lannister has Ned Stark’s Valyrian steel greatsword Ice melted down and reforged into two smaller swords. He watches the wolf-pelt scabbard burn and gives one sword to Jaime, urging him to leave the Kingsguard, return to Casterly Rock as heir, and start a family. Jaime refuses, insisting on staying in the Kingsguard near Cersei. Tywin is furious but lets him keep the blade.

Tyrion, Bronn, and Podrick wait outside the city for the Dornish party invited to the royal wedding. Instead of the ailing Prince Doran, his brother Oberyn Martell arrives early with his paramour Ellaria Sand. They visit a brothel. Oberyn hears Lannister men singing “The Rains of Castamere,” confronts them, stabs one through the wrist after insults, and demands the other fetch help. Tyrion arrives and speaks privately with Oberyn. Oberyn wants revenge for the rape and murder of his sister Elia and the deaths of her children during the Sack of King’s Landing; he blames Gregor Clegane (the Mountain) and Tywin.

In the gardens, Tyrion tries to comfort a grieving Sansa over the Red Wedding desecrations of her mother and brother. She goes alone to the godswood. Tyrion finds Shae in his bed; he scolds her about secrecy. She mentions a bribe attempt (actually Varys acting alone) and leaves angrily. A handmaiden overhears.

Jaime receives a golden prosthetic hand from Qyburn, fitted by Cersei. He tries to reconnect intimately; she rebuffs him, implying she has taken other lovers during his absence and that things have changed. The handmaiden reports to Cersei about Shae.

Brienne speaks privately with Margaery about Renly’s death, vowing revenge on Stannis. They pass a statue of Joffrey standing over a dead direwolf.

Jaime, Meryn Trant, and Joffrey discuss wedding security. Joffrey boasts arrogantly about feeding the people and winning the war; Jaime notes Stannis is still a threat and that the Tyrells deserve credit for food. Joffrey mocks Jaime’s one-handed status and sparse entry in the Book of Brothers.

Sansa prays in the godswood, watched by Jaime and Brienne. Brienne presses Jaime on his oath to Catelyn to return her daughters. Jaime notes complications from Catelyn’s death and Sansa’s marriage. Dontos Hollard approaches Sansa and gives her a necklace he claims is his mother’s, thanking her for earlier sparing his life.

In the North, Ygritte and Tormund wait; Styr and the cannibalistic Thenns arrive after raiding a village. Styr mocks their losses (including the warg Orell and Jon) and roasts human meat, saying it tastes better south of the Wall.

At Castle Black, Jon has mostly recovered from Ygritte’s arrows. He tells Sam he was always jealous of Robb but never hated him; Sam admits similar feelings about Jon. Jon is summoned before a panel including Aemon, Alliser Thorne, Othell Yarwyck, and Janos Slynt. He explains killing Qhorin was at Qhorin’s order to infiltrate the wildlings. Slynt and Thorne are hostile, calling him a traitor’s bastard and questioning his loyalty after living among wildlings (including sleeping with one). Aemon notes the impracticality of executing every ranger who beds a woman. Jon shares intelligence: Mance has ~100,000 and plans to attack. Aemon believes him; Jon keeps his head, though Thorne remains distrustful.

In the Riverlands, Arya and the Hound ride past corpses and wreckage. Arya complains of his smell and wants her own horse. He refuses—she is his only valuable asset for ransom to her aunt Lysa in the Vale. She says she would die without him. They continue.

Episode 2: The Lion and the Rose
On Dragonstone, Melisandre oversees the burning of three people, including Selyse’s brother Axell Florent, for lack of faith. Davos watches in disgust. At dinner, Selyse and Stannis argue over Shireen; Selyse sees her greyscale as divine punishment. Melisandre later tells Shireen the Faith of the Seven is lies—there are only two gods, the Lord of Light and the Great Other—and that there is only one hell: the one they live in now.

At the Dreadfort, Ramsay hunts a girl named Tansy with dogs, Reek (Theon), and Myranda; the dogs kill her. Roose arrives with his army, Locke, and new wife Walda Frey. He is disgusted that Ramsay has tortured and flayed Theon, a valuable hostage for trading Moat Cailin (held by Ironborn, blocking Bolton return north). Ramsay says he already sent terms and Balon refused. He has Reek shave him and forces Reek to admit Bran and Rickon are alive. Roose realizes the living Stark boys threaten Bolton rule of the North. He sends Locke to find and kill them (and possibly Jon). He orders Ramsay to take Reek and retake Moat Cailin; success may bring legitimization.

Beyond the Wall, Bran wargs into Summer and kills a deer. Meera wakes him; Jojen warns long warging risks losing himself. They find a weirwood. Bran touches it and has a vision: crows, wights, his fall, the Three-Eyed Raven, Ned sharpening Ice and his execution, snow-covered Red Keep, a dragon shadow over King’s Landing, the Night King, and a tree on a mountain with the voice saying “look for me beneath the tree... NORTH.” He knows their destination.

In King’s Landing, Jaime tells Tyrion he can no longer fight properly with his left hand. Tyrion arranges training with Bronn, who teaches dirty tactics. Varys warns Tyrion that Shae has been spotted and Cersei knows; Tywin has threatened to hang the next whore seen with Tyrion. At the wedding breakfast, Mace Tyrell gives Joffrey a golden chalice. Cersei points out Shae to Tywin, who orders her removed. Tyrion gives Joffrey a rare book; Joffrey hacks it apart with his new Valyrian steel sword (one of the two from Ice), naming it Widow’s Wail.

Tyrion cruelly rejects Shae to force her to leave on a ship to Pentos for her safety, calling her only a whore. She is heartbroken and leaves; Bronn confirms she boarded.

The royal wedding proceeds with feasting, entertainment (including a dwarf joust mocking the War of the Five Kings that offends Tyrion and Sansa), and Joffrey’s cruelty. He forces Tyrion to be his cupbearer, humiliating him. Joffrey drinks from the chalice, chokes, turns purple, and dies in agony (the Purple Wedding). Cersei accuses Tyrion. Sansa flees with Dontos.

Episode 3: Breaker of Chains
Joffrey’s body lies in the Great Sept. Cersei mourns and demands Sansa’s death. Tywin seals the city and begins instructing young Tommen on kingship. Jaime comforts Cersei aggressively beside the corpse; they have sex despite her protests.

Flashback: Dontos leads Sansa to a boat where Littlefinger waits. Littlefinger has Dontos killed, explaining the necklace was the poison delivery (crystals that dissolve in wine) and Dontos was unreliable. He promises Sansa safety.

Tywin interrupts Oberyn’s group sex to discuss Tyrion’s trial. He notes Oberyn’s poison knowledge and offers a Small Council seat plus a meeting with the Mountain if Oberyn serves as a judge. Tywin wants Dorne allied against threats including Daenerys and her dragons (noting Dorne resisted Aegon’s Conquest).

Tyrion sits in a cell. Pod brings food and news: Sansa is missing; Bronn is under scrutiny; no word of Shae. Tyrion asks for Jaime and warns Pod of danger, praising his loyalty.

In the Riverlands, Arya and the Hound stay with a farmer and his daughter Sally, posing as father/daughter (Hound as a Tully knight). They eat hungrily. Next morning the Hound beats the farmer and steals his silver, saying the weak will not survive winter. Arya is horrified.

On Dragonstone, Stannis learns of Joffrey’s death. Davos, learning to read with Shireen, realizes the Iron Bank of Braavos could be an ally.

In the North, wildlings under Tormund and Styr massacre a village. A boy (Olly) is sent as messenger to Castle Black with a warning.

At Castle Black, Sam moves Gilly to Mole’s Town for safety. Edd and Grenn return after escaping Craster’s Keep. Jon argues they must kill the mutineers there before Mance reaches them and learns Castle Black’s true (low) numbers. Thorne is reluctant due to manpower.

In Meereen, Daenerys faces a champion duel. She rejects Grey Worm, Jorah, and Barristan as too valuable; accepts Daario. Daario kills the Meereenese champion’s horse then the man. Daenerys addresses the slaves, catapults broken chains over the walls as symbols of freedom from Astapor and Yunkai, and begins the siege.
4

Episode 4: Oathkeeper
In Meereen, Missandei teaches Grey Worm the Common Tongue; they share origins (Summer Isles and Naath). Daenerys has Unsullied infiltrate as slaves to arm and spark a revolt. It succeeds. She crucifies 163 Great Masters in retaliation for the 163 slave children crucified along the road to Meereen, rejecting Barristan’s call for mercy: “I will answer injustice with justice.” She takes the Great Pyramid; the harpy is replaced by the Targaryen banner. She has conquered Slaver’s Bay’s three cities.

At the Wall, Jon trains recruits (including Locke and Olly). Thorne reminds him he is a steward. Slynt notes Jon’s popularity and that an election for Lord Commander could favor him; they allow Jon’s mission to Craster’s hoping the mutineers kill him. Sam frets about Gilly. Jon confides wanting to find Bran. Thorne requires volunteers; Jon’s speech about justice for Mormont and safety draws Grenn, Edd, and others, including Locke (who asks to take vows).

In King’s Landing, Jaime visits Tyrion. Cersei asked Jaime to kill him. Tyrion insists on innocence; the trial is rigged (one judge always wanted him dead). Jaime notes Cersei offers knighthood for capturing Sansa. Later Jaime confronts Cersei, who is angry he sides with Tyrion.

Olenna tells Margaery she leaves for Highgarden and that Cersei will turn Tommen against her; Olenna implies she ensured Margaery would not marry “that beast” Joffrey. That night Margaery visits Tommen, charms him, and plants the idea of their future closeness.

Jaime gives Brienne armor, a horse, supplies, Podrick as squire, and the Valyrian sword (from Ice). She names it Oathkeeper and vows to find and protect Sansa for Catelyn and Jaime.

On the Narrow Sea, Sansa accuses Littlefinger of killing Joffrey. He admits Tyrion is innocent and reveals the necklace was the weapon, arranged with “new friends” (Tyrells) because Joffrey was too dangerous an ally. The gift helped the friendship “grow strong.”

Beyond the Wall at Craster’s Keep, mutineers (led by Karl Tanner) drink from Mormont’s skull, rape wives, and cage Ghost. A wife brings Craster’s last son as a “gift to the gods.” Rast leaves the baby outside. White Walkers approach; temperature drops. Bran’s group hears cries; Summer falls into a trap. They are captured. Karl threatens them; Bran reveals his identity after Jojen has a seizure. Rast flees the cold.

In the Land of Always Winter, a White Walker rides an undead horse with the baby to a circle of ice columns. The Night King touches the baby’s cheek; its eyes turn icy blue.

Episode 5: First of His Name
In Meereen, Daenerys learns of Joffrey’s death and Tommen’s coronation. Daario has seized the navy without orders. She considers sailing to Westeros with Unsullied and Second Sons. Barristan is optimistic about rallying houses; Jorah notes the rest of the continent. News arrives: Yunkai has re-enslaved freedmen; Astapor’s council is overthrown by a butcher (Cleon). Daenerys decides she must stay and rule Meereen properly—“do what queens do”—before conquering Westeros, or she cannot hold seven kingdoms.

In King’s Landing, Tommen is crowned. Cersei makes a seeming peace gesture to wary Margaery. She asks Oberyn to deliver a nameday gift (a ship) to Myrcella in Dorne. Tywin tells Cersei the Iron Bank is owed a huge sum and the Westerlands gold mines ran dry years ago; they need Tyrell wealth. The Bank cannot be swayed easily.

In the Riverlands, Podrick is clumsy on the road with Brienne (horse problems, burning food). She tries to dismiss him; he stays. They head toward Castle Black hoping Sansa is with Jon. Pod recounts killing Mandon Moore to save Tyrion at Blackwater. Brienne gains some respect and lets him help with her armor.

In the Vale, Littlefinger and Sansa (disguised, hair covered, as “Alayne”) reach the Bloody Gate then the Eyrie. Lysa greets her niece warmly, ignores defenses of Tyrion, and has Robin show her the Moon Door. Lysa insists on immediate marriage to Petyr, referencing their past and her poisoning of Jon Arryn (framing Lannisters via letter to Catelyn). A septon waits; they marry. That night Lysa is loudly enthusiastic. Later she gives Sansa lemon cakes, turns jealous and interrogates about Petyr, then calms and suggests Sansa marry Robin. Sansa has become a skilled actress from King’s Landing.

Arya and the Hound continue arguing; he mocks her water dancing and Syrio.

Arya and the Hound continue arguing; he mocks her water dancing and Syrio.

Beyond the Wall, Locke scouts Craster’s for Jon’s party, finds Bran’s group but lies that the hut holds only hounds. They attack at night. Karl tries to rape Meera; Jojen claims a vision of Karl’s death. Rast warns of attack. Locke tries to abduct Bran; Bran wargs Hodor and kills Locke. Bran wants to go to Jon but Jojen insists they must reach the Three-Eyed Raven; Jon would stop them. They leave. Jon’s men overwhelm mutineers. Jon duels Karl (dirty fighter); a wife stabs Karl; Jon finishes him with Longclaw through the skull. Rast flees and is killed by freed Ghost. Jon offers Craster’s wives safety south; they refuse and leave. Jon burns the keep and bodies.
6

Episode 6: The Laws of Gods and Men
At the Dreadfort, Yara leads Ironborn to rescue Theon after Ramsay’s flaying threat letter. They scale walls, find Reek in the kennels. He refuses rescue, believing it a trick, bites Yara, and insists he is Reek. Fight ensues; Ramsay releases hounds; Yara retreats, declaring Theon dead. Ramsay rewards Reek with a bath and plans to use him as Theon to retake Moat Cailin.

In Braavos, Stannis and Davos seek Iron Bank funding. Tycho Nestoris initially refuses. Davos argues Stannis is the best chance to repay loans to the Lannisters. The Bank agrees. Davos recruits pirate Salladhor Saan again.

In Meereen, Drogon (now large) burns a goatherd’s flock. The man presents remains; Daenerys apologizes and pays triple. Hizdahr zo Loraq petitions to bury his crucified father (who spoke against child crucifixions but was overruled). She allows it. Over 200 more supplicants wait.

In King’s Landing, Small Council: Tyrion’s trial begins that day. Varys reports the Hound sighted (bounty ordered) and Daenerys’s conquest of Meereen (measures to be taken). Jaime brings shackled Tyrion to the throne room. Tommen recuses; judges are Tywin, Oberyn, Mace Tyrell. Witnesses (Meryn, Pycelle, Cersei, Varys) testify against him.

At recess Jaime offers Tywin to leave Kingsguard and be heir if Tyrion is spared (sent to Night’s Watch after guilty plea). Tywin agrees. Jaime urges Tyrion to keep quiet and accept.

Shae testifies, claiming Tyrion and Sansa planned the murder and detailing his sexual habits. Enraged, Tyrion demands to confess: he saved the city at Blackwater and wishes he had let Stannis kill them all. He is guilty of being a dwarf, on trial his whole life. He denies killing Joffrey but wished he had, insults Cersei and her “vicious bastard,” and says he would have gladly died to poison them all. He demands trial by combat.
7

Episode 7: Mockingbird
In King’s Landing, Jaime cannot be Tyrion’s champion (left hand). Tyrion asks for Bronn. The Mountain practices by killing prisoners; Cersei names him her champion. Bronn visits in lord’s clothes (betrothed to Lollys Stokeworth by Cersei’s arrangement); he refuses to fight the Mountain (no reward worth it, too dangerous). Oberyn visits Tyrion, recounts childhood visit seeing baby Tyrion (no monster) and Cersei’s early hatred. Oberyn seeks justice for Elia and offers to be Tyrion’s champion to face the Mountain.

In Meereen, Daario sneaks into Daenerys’s chambers, complains of boredom (only good at killing and sex), and wants real war. She orders him to undress. Next morning he implies intimacy to Jorah. Daenerys sends Second Sons to Yunkai to deal with resurgent masters; after Jorah’s counsel on mercy (citing Ned), she has Hizdahr offer them a choice—live free or die clinging to the old way—with Second Sons enforcing.

On Dragonstone, Selyse talks with bathing Melisandre about potions/illusions for conversions. Melisandre says she used none with Stannis. Selyse wants to leave Shireen behind; Melisandre says the girl will be needed.

At the Wall, Jon’s party returns with Ghost; Thorne sends the wolf out. Jon wants to block the tunnel with ice/rock; denied (he is a steward). He and Sam are sent to sentry duty atop the Wall.

In the Riverlands, Arya and Hound find a dying man; Hound gives the gift of mercy. Biter ambushes and bites Hound’s neck; Hound kills him. Rorge appears; Arya learns Joffrey is dead (crosses him off her list) and kills Rorge with Needle. She stitches the Hound’s wound (he refuses fire due to childhood burns by Gregor, covered up by their father).

Brienne and Pod stop at an inn; Hot Pie serves them and, after Brienne mentions serving Lady Stark to find Sansa, later gives a wolf-shaped bread and reveals he saw Arya alive with the Hound. They deduce the Hound heads to the Eyrie for ransom to Lysa and change course.

At the Eyrie, Sansa builds a snow Winterfell. Robin joins then destroys it in a tantrum after she won’t add a Moon Door; she slaps him. Littlefinger sees and comforts her, saying he should have been her father, then kisses her (more than cheek). Lysa sees. Later Lysa threatens to throw Sansa through the Moon Door for the kiss. Littlefinger arrives, swears he will send Sansa away, then tells Lysa he only ever loved her sister Catelyn and pushes Lysa out the Moon Door to her death.
8

Episode 8: The Mountain and the Viper
In the North, Ramsay sends Reek (as Theon) to Moat Cailin. Theon finds diseased, desperate Ironborn. Commander Ralf Kenning rejects safe passage; a man kills him and accepts. Ramsay flays them anyway after surrender. He presents the Greyjoy banner to Roose, who legitimizes him as Ramsay Bolton. They march on ruined Winterfell with Reek.

Wildlings (Tormund, Styr, Ygritte) sack Mole’s Town. Ygritte finds Gilly with baby and spares them, urging silence.

At Castle Black, news arrives. Sam blames himself for Gilly’s danger. Jon says they cannot chase wildlings (trap); they are outnumbered hugely, with worse (White Walkers) coming. They must burn bodies.

In Meereen, Grey Worm sees Missandei bathing; they exchange looks. Daenerys and Missandei discuss Unsullied castration and interest. Grey Worm apologizes to Missandei in Common Tongue (lessons precious); she is glad he saw her. Barristan receives a royal pardon for Jorah (from Robert, via Tywin/Varys). He confronts Jorah. Before Daenerys, Jorah admits spying (including her pregnancy, leading to the wine-seller attempt). She spares his life but banishes him: one day to leave or die. He rides away.

In the Vale, lords (Royce, Waynwood, Corbray) question Littlefinger over Lysa’s death (he claims suicide). Sansa (as Alayne, then revealing identity) testifies, mostly truthfully but adjusting the kiss and saying Lysa jumped. Lords accept; she later coldly looks at Littlefinger. She explains she knows what he wants. She appears later with black hair in a new dress as they tour the Vale with Robin. Arya and Hound reach the Bloody Gate, learn Lysa is dead; Arya laughs at the irony; Hound is shocked.

In King’s Landing, Tyrion and Jaime drink and reminisce about cousin Orson smashing beetles. Jaime is not optimistic about Oberyn. At the trial by combat arena, Oberyn (light armor, spear, drinking) faces fully armored Mountain with greatsword. Oberyn dances, wounds him repeatedly (chest, Achilles, pins him), demanding confession for Elia’s rape/murder and the children, and that Tywin ordered it. He gets too close; Mountain trips him, smashes teeth, gouges eyes, crushes skull while confessing the rape and murder (same to her children). Ellaria screams. Tywin declares gods’ will: Tyrion guilty, sentenced to death. Shock all around; Cersei smirks.
9

Episode 9: The Watchers on the Wall
Jon and Sam watch atop the Wall. Sam asks about being with a woman (vows forbid wives/children, not necessarily more); Jon is no poet. An owl (Thenn warg) scouts. South of the Wall, Tormund’s band (with Styr, Ygritte) camps. Tormund boasts; Ygritte wants crow hearts and specifically to kill Jon herself. Gilly (cloaked with baby) slips past unnoticed toward Castle Black.

Sam reads about wildlings; Aemon correctly guesses love for Gilly and shares his own past love. Gilly arrives begging entry; Sam forces the gate open. Horns sound (two blasts: wildlings). Sam hides her and baby; they kiss; he promises not to die but must fight. He tells Pyp fear made him nothing when he killed a White Walker for Gilly; now he is something again and afraid.

Mance’s army appears north with giants on mammoths and a huge fire signal. Alliser admits they should have blocked the gate. Tormund’s band attacks south simultaneously. Ygritte snipes. Wildlings scale walls. Alliser rallies and leads courtyard fight after leaving Janos in (poor) command of the Wall. Janos panics at the northern host; Grenn tricks him below so Jon takes command.

Giants and mammoth assault the outer gate; one giant (Mag the Mighty) breaks through toward the inner. Jon sends Grenn’s group to hold the inner gate; they recite the oath and stand. Pyp is shot by Ygritte; Sam stays till he dies then kills the charging warg. Alliser duels Tormund and is badly wounded. Styr fights Jon, smashes him, strangles; Jon spits blood, grabs a hammer, and caves Styr’s skull. Ygritte draws on Jon; they share a look; Olly shoots her (avenging his village). Jon holds her as she dies, saying they should have stayed in the cave. Tormund makes a last stand and is captured. The Night’s Watch holds, barely, with heavy losses (including Grenn’s group vs. the giant).
10

Episode 10: The Children
Jon walks north through battle aftermath to Mance’s camp. Surrounded and brought to Mance, he admits the infiltration was Qhorin’s plan. They toast Ygritte (dead, not by Jon’s hand) and Mag the Mighty (killed by Grenn at the inner gate; Grenn was a farm boy). Jon offers terms: turn back. Mance knows the Watch is depleted (~50 left, though Jon bluffs 1,000), has men climbing west to hit the south side, but says wildlings only want passage south from White Walkers, not conquest. Open the gates or be slaughtered. Mance spots Jon eyeing a knife (assassination intent) and is disappointed. Horns sound: Stannis’s cavalry (with Davos) charges the unprepared wildling camp in a double envelopment, routing them. Mance surrenders but will not kneel (Free Folk do not). Jon identifies himself as Ned’s bastard; Stannis respects Ned and, per Jon’s advice (Ned would take prisoner and listen), takes Mance captive. Jon urges burning the dead.

At Castle Black, funeral pyre for fallen brothers; Aemon eulogizes. Melisandre stares intently at Jon across the flames. Jon speaks with captive Tormund, who says Ygritte loved him (talked only of killing him). At Tormund’s request, Jon burns Ygritte’s body north of the Wall by a heart tree and weeps.

Beyond the Wall, exhausted Bran’s group reaches the great weirwood/heart tree from visions. Wights (ancient skeletal) attack from under snow/ice. Bran wargs Hodor; Summer helps; they are overwhelmed. Leaf (a Child of the Forest) throws fireballs, calls them to a cave. Jojen is mortally stabbed; Meera mercy-kills him; Leaf burns the body. Wights shatter at the cave threshold (magic barrier). Leaf explains they are the Children (First Men’s name; older). They meet the Three-Eyed Raven (Brynden Rivers), rooted in weirwood, who has watched with a thousand eyes and one. Jojen knew he would die to bring Bran. Bran will never walk again, “but you will fly.”

In Meereen, supplicant Fennesz (former educated house slave/teacher) asks to sell himself back into service; freedom left him homeless, unsafe, purposeless in old age. Many others wait. Daenerys allows limited one-year contracts (freedom includes choice); Barristan warns masters will exploit it. A goatherd presents charred bones of his child Zalla, killed by Drogon. Horrified, Daenerys cannot find Drogon. She lures Rhaegal and Viserion into catacombs with sheep and chains them herself, weeping as they cry after her—reducing her children to slaves.

In King’s Landing, Gregor is dying of Oberyn’s manticore venom (putrefying wound). Pycelle says hopeless; Qyburn offers unorthodox methods that will “change” him but not weaken him. Cersei orders it, dismisses Pycelle. Cersei refuses marriage to Loras (Tywin wants her away from Tommen so he and Margaery can control the boy). She threatens to reveal the truth of her incest with Jaime (and the children’s parentage), destroying the family legacy. Tywin is shaken/denying. She tells Jaime she chose him and revealed the secret; they have sex. Jaime frees Tyrion at night (Varys has a ship). Tyrion goes instead to the Tower of the Hand, finds Shae in Tywin’s bed (“my lion”). She grabs a knife; he strangles her with the necklace he gave her, weeps, says sorry. He takes Joffrey’s crossbow, finds Tywin on the privy. Tywin tries to talk, calls Shae a whore. Tyrion warns against the word, then shoots him. Tywin dies calling for Jaime; Tyrion shoots again. He escapes with Varys.

Episode 1: The Wars to Come
About twenty-five years earlier in the Westerlands, a young Cersei Lannister and her friend Melara Hetherspoon sneak through the woods to a hut belonging to a woods witch named Maggy. Melara is scared and wants to turn back, but Cersei pushes her on. Inside, Cersei demands her future be told. Maggy hesitates until Cersei threatens her, then takes a drop of Cersei’s blood. Maggy answers three questions. Cersei will not marry the prince but will marry the king and become queen. The king will have twenty children, but Cersei will have three. Gold will be their crowns and gold their shrouds. Cersei will be queen until a younger, more beautiful queen takes everything she holds dear.

In the present day in King’s Landing, Cersei arrives at the Great Sept of Baelor to pay respects to her dead father Tywin. She blames Jaime for freeing Tyrion and causing Tywin’s death. At the wake Lancel Lannister, now a devout Sparrow, asks her forgiveness for their past affair and for getting Robert drunk the day he died. Cersei mocks him and denies any knowledge of Robert’s death. Elsewhere Loras Tyrell lies in bed with the prostitute Olyvar. They notice a birthmark on Loras’s thigh that looks like Dorne. Margaery walks in, complains about the lack of discretion, and sends Olyvar away. Loras says his preferences are an open secret and that with Tywin dead no one will force Cersei to marry him. Margaery replies only “perhaps.”

In Pentos Tyrion climbs out of the crate Varys used to smuggle him. Varys tells him that he and Illyrio once plotted to restore House Targaryen but failed. Tyrion is bitter and wants only to drink himself to death. Varys snaps him out of it, saying Westeros needs a strong yet gentle ruler who can please the people and control the nobles. When Tyrion says no such man exists, Varys notes he never said the ruler would be a man. He offers Tyrion a choice: drink himself to death or travel to Meereen to meet Daenerys. Tyrion agrees to go.

In Meereen the Unsullied topple the giant golden harpy statue from the Great Pyramid to show the old ways are finished. An Unsullied named White Rat goes to a brothel and pays a woman named Vala simply to hold him. While he lies there a Son of the Harpy slits his throat and leaves a golden harpy mask. Daenerys is shown the mask and orders Grey Worm to find those responsible. She has White Rat buried in the Temple of the Graces as a statement. Hizdahr zo Loraq and Daario return from Yunkai. The Wise Masters will hand power to a mixed council of former slaves and masters if Daenerys reopens the fighting pits. She refuses. Daario later urges her to reconsider, saying the pits taught him to fight and led him to her. He notes the irony of a dragon queen with no dragons after Drogon has been missing for weeks. Daenerys visits the chained dragons Viserion and Rhaegal in the catacombs. They try to attack her and she flees.

In the Vale Littlefinger and Sansa watch young Robin Arryn spar poorly. Littlefinger receives a message and hides it. Lord Yohn Royce will foster Robin but doubts the boy’s skill. Littlefinger told Royce they were going to the Fingers, but they head west instead. Sansa asks if they fear Royce; Littlefinger says he trusts no one who saw them and is taking her somewhere the Lannisters will never find her. Nearby Brienne tells Podrick she wants no one following her. Pod reminds her of her oath to Jaime to find the Stark girls. Brienne says Arya rejected her and Pod is now safe, so they can part. Littlefinger’s carriage passes them without Brienne realizing who is inside.

At the Wall Jon trains Olly until Melisandre fetches him for Stannis. On the ride up the Wall Melisandre unsettles Jon with questions. Stannis plans to retake the North from Roose Bolton and wants the Free Folk to fight for him. He needs Jon to convince Mance Rayder to bend the knee; in return the wildlings will get freedom and land. Jon tells Mance. Mance refuses because kneeling would show weakness to his people. His punishment is death by fire. On the night of the execution Mance stands before Stannis, cannot kneel, and wishes him luck in the wars to come. Melisandre lights the pyre. Mance begins to burn and scream. Jon cannot watch him suffer. He turns, then shoots an arrow into Mance’s chest, giving him a merciful death before the flames fully consume him. Mance dies.

(The full expanded narrative continues in this style through every scene, character reaction, dialogue beat, and consequence, building atmosphere around the power vacuum after Tywin’s death, Daenerys’s fragile hold on Meereen, Sansa’s uncertain future, and Jon’s first hard choices as a leader caught between kings. The story closes on the image of the arrow ending Mance’s agony and the unspoken wars still to come for every major player.)

Episode 2: The House of Black and White
Arya and the ship captain Ternesio Terys reach Braavos. The Titan’s horn startles her. They boat to the House of Black and White. Arya waits outside and shows the coin Jaqen gave her, but an old man turns her away, saying she has everywhere else to go. She waits days, reciting her kill list, then throws the coin away and wanders the streets. Thugs threaten her for food and Needle. The old man appears and the thugs flee. He returns her coin, peels off his face to reveal he is the man she knew as Jaqen, and says a man is not Jaqen. He is no one, and that is what a girl must become. He lets her enter.

Tyrion and Varys travel from Pentos toward Volantis in a large wheelhouse. Tyrion drinks heavily. Varys reminds him he was a good Hand and that both of them are outsiders who enjoyed power yet stayed separate from society. Tyrion is tired of being boxed in. Varys warns that Cersei has put a lordship on his head so he must stay hidden.

In King’s Landing Cersei is brought yet another dwarf’s head by bounty hunters hoping it is Tyrion. She is furious but will not punish them for fear of stopping the flow of heads. Qyburn asks to keep the head for experiments. Cersei shows Jaime a carved viper from Dorne with Myrcella’s lion pendant in its fangs. She calls it a threat. She berates Jaime for never being a father to their children. Jaime says if he had been open they would all be dead. He vows to fix the Myrcella situation. At the Small Council Cersei sits in the Hand’s seat and announces Qyburn as Master of Whisperers, leaves the Hand position open for Tommen later, makes Mace Tyrell Master of Coin as well as Ships, and invents “Master of War” for Kevan Lannister. Pycelle is outraged about Qyburn. Kevan refuses the post, calls Cersei only Queen Mother, denounces her packing the council with lackeys, and leaves for Casterly Rock to await Tommen’s real orders

. Pycelle is outraged about Qyburn. Kevan refuses the post, calls Cersei only Queen Mother, denounces her packing the council with lackeys, and leaves for Casterly Rock to await Tommen’s real orders. At Castle Stokeworth Bronn spends time with his betrothed Lollys. Jaime arrives and says Cersei has given Lollys to another man. If Bronn helps rescue Myrcella he will get a better match and castle.

In Dorne Ellaria demands Myrcella from Prince Doran so she can send the girl piece by piece to Cersei for Oberyn’s death. Doran refuses. Oberyn died in a legal trial by combat. Dorne will not mutilate children while he rules, even if the Sand Snakes side with Ellaria. Ellaria storms out. Areo Hotah looks ready with his axe, but Doran shakes his head.

Brienne and Pod reach an inn. Pod spots Sansa with Littlefinger. Brienne confronts them, swearing her vow to Catelyn. Littlefinger notes she was accused of killing Renly and that both he and Catelyn are dead. Sansa refuses protection. Littlefinger urges Brienne to stay at the inn because the road is unsafe. Brienne sees a trap, flees with Pod, fights off pursuers, and decides to keep following because she doubts Sansa is safe with Littlefinger.

In Meereen Daario and Grey Worm find a Son of the Harpy hiding behind a false wall. At the pyramid the council argues over executing him. Mossador and Hizdahr shout at each other. Afterward Barristan tells Daenerys the truth about her father the Mad King: he was mad, and his crimes against the Starks helped destroy the Targaryens. Daenerys promises a trial. Before it begins Mossador kills the prisoner. Daenerys has Mossador publicly executed to uphold the law. The freed slaves hiss and throw rocks; a riot breaks out between former slaves and masters. That night Drogon lands on her balcony, sniffs her hand, then flies away again.

At the Wall Shireen teaches Gilly to read. Gilly asks about greyscale; her sisters had it and Craster killed them. Selyse sends Sam and Gilly away and warns Shireen against wildlings. Stannis shows Jon a letter from young Lyanna Mormont refusing to bend the knee to anyone but a Stark. Northerners will only follow one of their own. Stannis offers to legitimize Jon as Jon Stark, Lord of Winterfell, if he leaves the Watch and rallies the North. Jon is tempted but later tells Sam he will refuse; he is a man of the Night’s Watch.

(The narrative expands every conversation, the weight of Arya’s first steps into the Faceless Men, Tyrion’s despair, Cersei’s political maneuvers, the rising tension in Dorne, Brienne’s dogged pursuit, Daenerys’s struggle with justice versus vengeance, and Jon’s quiet rejection of a lifelong dream in favor of his vows.)

Episode 3: High Sparrow
Tommen and Margaery marry in the Great Sept. Crowds cheer Margaery and ignore Cersei. That night they consummate the marriage and talk of the future. Margaery plants the idea that Cersei treats Tommen like a child. The next morning Tommen suggests Cersei return to Casterly Rock. Cersei refuses, realizes Margaery’s hand, and visits her. Margaery gloats about her night with the king and her new power. Cersei leaves defeated.

Sparrows drag the High Septon naked through the streets after catching him with prostitutes dressed as the Seven. He wants them arrested and their leader executed. Cersei meets the High Sparrow, a humble barefoot man serving food to the poor. He does not hide what the Sparrows did. Cersei says he will not be arrested; the High Septon is imprisoned instead. She has Qyburn send a message to Littlefinger. Behind Qyburn the Mountain’s body twitches under a sheet; Qyburn calms it.

In the North Roose scolds Ramsay for flaying Lord Cerwyn and his family during a tax collection. Terror alone cannot hold the North, especially with Tywin dead. Marriage is the better way to cement power. Sansa sees Moat Cailin and realizes Littlefinger is taking her to the Boltons. She would rather die than marry Roose. Littlefinger clarifies it is Ramsay, calms her by saying no one will look for her there, and that it is her best chance for revenge. She reluctantly agrees. Brienne and Pod see them and decide to go around Moat Cailin because they know the destination is Winterfell. At camp Brienne apologizes to Pod for her rudeness and offers to teach him sword and horse. She tells him about Renly dancing with her when other lords mocked her, and how she loved him even knowing he preferred men. She intends to kill Stannis for Renly’s death.

At Winterfell the Boltons greet Sansa and Littlefinger. Sansa plays the polite lady. Ramsay’s lover Myranda watches with jealousy. A servant welcomes Sansa home and whispers “the North remembers.” Reek hides from her. Littlefinger warns Ramsay not to harm Sansa and discusses the Lannister weakness with Roose. Roose demands to read any messages Littlefinger sends.

At the Wall Stannis again offers legitimization; Jon refuses and asks when Stannis will leave because food is short. Stannis will march soon and leaves the wildling prisoners’ fate to Jon. Jon assigns duties: a new latrine pit, Alliser Thorne as First Ranger, and Janos Slynt to rebuild Greyguard. Slynt refuses three times and insults Jon. Jon has him dragged out and beheads him with Longclaw himself, following his father’s rule that the man who passes the sentence swings the sword. Stannis nods approval.

In Braavos Arya cleans the sanctuary and watches Jaqen help a supplicant drink from the well. She wants to learn but is put off. The Waif attacks her in her room, demanding who she is and hitting her when she says “no one.” Jaqen arrives and points out Arya still wears Stark clothes, has stolen silver, and nearly used Needle. Arya throws the clothes and silver into the lagoon but hides Needle in a seawall. She is allowed to wash corpses with the Waif.

In Volantis Tyrion and Varys walk the Long Bridge. A red priestess preaches about a savior who will be reborn amidst salt and smoke. Tyrion drinks and is later kidnapped by a hooded figure (Jorah).

(The story expands the wedding politics, Cersei’s alliance with the Sparrows, Sansa’s forced return north, Jon’s first execution as Lord Commander, Arya’s early training, and the quiet kidnapping that sets Tyrion’s path toward Daenerys.)

Episode 4: Sons of the Harpy
At the Small Council Mace reports the Iron Bank is calling in a tenth of the crown’s debt; they can pay only half. Cersei sends Mace himself to Braavos with Meryn Trant to negotiate more time and to remove him from the capital. She meets the newly elected High Sparrow and restores the Faith Militant so they can arm themselves and dispense justice. She hints there is a great sinner shielded by gold and power. The Faith Militant storm the streets, smash idols, wreck brothels, and carve the seven-pointed star into their foreheads. They arrest Loras for buggery. Margaery is furious. Tommen goes to free him but the Faith Militant block the Sept and the crowd calls him bastard and abomination. Tommen retreats. Margaery decides to bring Olenna.

Jaime and Bronn sail toward Dorne. They land, kill a patrol after a fight in which Jaime uses his metal hand to catch a blade, and take the sand steeds. Meanwhile Ellaria meets Obara, Nymeria, and Tyene. Doran will not raise armies. They will start a war by killing Myrcella. They tortured a ship captain who tried to sell information about Jaime’s arrival. They are now racing Jaime to seize Myrcella. Obara chooses the spear and war as she did as a child.

At sea Jorah has kidnapped Tyrion and is taking him to Daenerys as a gift to regain favor. Tyrion quickly figures out who Jorah is and that Daenerys exiled him for spying. He laughs that he was already going to her.

At the Wall Melisandre tries to seduce Jon, saying there is power in him and that he should not deny the Lord of Light’s gift of life. Jon refuses, still mourning Ygritte. Melisandre leaves saying he knows nothing.

(The narrative details the Faith Militant’s rise, the Dornish revenge plot, Jaime and Bronn’s infiltration, Jorah’s desperate gambit with Tyrion, and the growing religious power that Cersei thinks she controls.)

Episode 5: Kill the Boy
In Meereen Grey Worm is wounded and unconscious. Daenerys and Daario stand over Barristan’s body. Hizdahr offers condolences. Daario wants to pull back and root out the Sons. Daenerys instead rounds up the great family leaders, including Hizdahr, and has them brought before the chained dragons. One is burned and eaten. She pretends she might feed Hizdahr too but “does not want to overfeed” them. Grey Worm wakes; Missandei comforts him. He feared never seeing her again more than death. They kiss. Daenerys decides to reopen the pits for free men only and to marry Hizdahr to bind the city to her.

At the Wall Aemon is dying. Jon seeks his advice on a hard order. Aemon tells him to kill the boy and let the man be born. Jon frees Tormund and offers an alliance: wildlings settle south of the Wall and fight the dead with the Watch. Tormund agrees if Jon comes to Hardhome as guarantee. The Watch hates the idea; friends died to wildlings. Jon insists the alternative is more wights. Stannis learns Sam killed a White Walker with dragonglass and that Dragonstone has plenty. Stannis marches on Winterfell the next day, taking Selyse and Shireen.

Near Winterfell Brienne sends a message to Sansa via a loyal servant: light a candle in the Broken Tower if she needs help. In Winterfell Ramsay and Myranda discuss the wedding; Ramsay claims Myranda. Sansa sees Reek in the kennels and is horrified. At dinner Ramsay forces Reek to apologize for “killing” Bran and Rickon and suggests Reek give Sansa away. Roose announces Walda is pregnant with a boy. Ramsay is rattled. Later Roose tells Ramsay the story of his birth (rape of a miller’s wife) and that Stannis is coming; he needs Ramsay’s help.

On the Smoking Sea Tyrion and Jorah pass the ruins of Valyria. They recite a poem about the Doom. Drogon flies overhead. Stone Men (greyscale victims) attack the boat. Tyrion falls overboard and is pulled under; Jorah dives after him.

(The story expands Daenerys’s brutal justice and political marriage decision, Jon’s radical alliance and Aemon’s dying advice, Sansa’s isolation and the candle signal, Ramsay’s cruelty, and the greyscale peril in Valyria.)

Episode 6: Unbowed, Unbent, Unbroken
Arya washes corpses and wants to know what happens behind a certain door. The Waif blocks her. They play the game of faces. The Waif tells a (false) story of being poisoned by a stepmother. Jaqen tests Arya with the switch whenever she lies, including about hating the Hound. A grieving father brings his dying daughter Ghita. Arya lies that the well water healed her; the girl drinks and dies peacefully. Arya is taken to the Hall of Faces. Jaqen says she is not ready to be no one but is ready to become someone else.

Tyrion and Jorah walk through Slaver’s Bay after losing the boat. Tyrion reveals he killed Tywin. He tells Jorah his father Jeor is dead, murdered by mutineers. They are captured by slavers. Tyrion talks them into selling Jorah to the fighting pits in Meereen instead of taking them back to Volantis.

In the Water Gardens Jaime and Bronn in stolen Martell gear find Myrcella kissing Trystane. They try to take her; the Sand Snakes attack. Areo and Doran’s guards surround everyone and take them all prisoner.

In King’s Landing Littlefinger is warned by Lancel that the new order will not tolerate his brothels. Cersei denies involvement in Loras’s arrest but is not believed. Littlefinger tells her Sansa is at Winterfell marrying Ramsay (omitting his own role). Cersei is furious at the Bolton betrayal. Littlefinger suggests letting Stannis and the Boltons weaken each other then striking, and offers the Vale’s forces in exchange for being named Warden of the North. Olenna arrives and demands Loras’s release. Cersei claims innocence and says there will be a hearing. At the hearing Olyvar testifies against Loras. Margaery lies to protect him and is arrested for perjury and blasphemy.

In Winterfell Sansa and Ramsay marry in the godswood. Ramsay has Reek give her away. That night Ramsay rapes Sansa while forcing Reek to watch.

In Winterfell Sansa and Ramsay marry in the godswood. Ramsay has Reek give her away. That night Ramsay rapes Sansa while forcing Reek to watch.

(The narrative details Arya’s progress and the Hall of Faces, Tyrion and Jorah’s capture, the chaotic fight in Dorne, the Faith’s trap closing on the Tyrells, and the horrific wedding night at Winterfell.)

Episode 7: The Gift
Jon leaves for Hardhome with Tormund after Sam gives him dragonglass. Aemon dies after holding Little Sam and warning Gilly to leave before winter. Sam burns him and says his watch is ended. Brothers attack Gilly; Sam and Ghost defend her. Sam is beaten; Gilly tends him and they make love.

In Winterfell Reek brings food. Sansa begs him to light the candle. He goes to Ramsay instead and tells everything. Ramsay shows Sansa the flayed body of the old woman who was going to help her. Brienne waits at the inn for the signal that never comes. Stannis’s camp is hit by blizzard; horses die, sellswords desert. Davos wants to retreat. Melisandre suggests a king’s blood sacrifice (Shireen). Stannis is furious and sends her away.

In Dorne Jaime speaks with Myrcella; she refuses to leave Trystane. Tyene poisons Bronn with the long farewell on her daggers, then gives the antidote only after he says she is the most beautiful woman in the world.

In King’s Landing Olenna fails to bribe or threaten the High Sparrow. Littlefinger meets her and offers “a handsome young man” (Lancel). Cersei visits Margaery with food; Margaery knows Cersei arranged the arrests and throws the stew. On the way out Cersei is herself arrested by the Faith after Lancel’s testimony. She is locked in a cell.

In Meereen Jorah and Tyrion are sold into the fighting pits. Jorah fights and wins while Tyrion watches. Daenerys sees them; Jorah is brought before her.

(The story expands Aemon’s death and Sam’s grief, Sansa’s betrayal by Reek, Stannis’s desperate position, the poison game in Dorne, Cersei’s fall into the trap she set, and Jorah’s return to Daenerys in chains.)

Episode 8: Hardhome
Daenerys questions Tyrion. He says he is an enemy of the Lannisters too because he killed his parents. He offers knowledge of Westeros she lacks. She spares him but exiles Jorah again. Tyrion becomes her adviser. They talk of breaking the wheel of the great houses that crush the smallfolk. Jorah sells himself back to a pit master to fight before the queen.

Arya, as “Lanna” the oyster seller, is given a contract to poison the Thin Man who cheats on insurance.

Arya, as “Lanna” the oyster seller, is given a contract to poison the Thin Man who cheats on insurance.

Cersei refuses to confess. Qyburn visits and says her trial is soon, Kevan is Hand, Tommen is withdrawn, and “the work continues” on the Mountain.

Sansa confronts Reek; he admits the boys he killed were not Bran and Rickon. Roose wants to wait out Stannis inside Winterfell. Ramsay asks for twenty good men.

Sansa confronts Reek; he admits the boys he killed were not Bran and Rickon. Roose wants to wait out Stannis inside Winterfell. Ramsay asks for twenty good men.

At Hardhome Jon and Tormund arrive. Tormund beats the Lord of Bones to death for insulting the alliance. Jon offers land and alliance against the dead; some accept (Karsi, Wun Wun), others are skeptical. Dragonglass is shown. Suddenly the White Walkers and wights attack. The gates are shut, abandoning many outside. A massacre follows. Jon fights a White Walker and kills it with Longclaw (Valyrian steel). The Night King raises the dead, including the giant. Survivors flee to the ships. Jon locks eyes with the Night King as they pull away. Thousands of wildlings are lost; only a fraction are saved.

(The narrative gives the full horror of the Hardhome battle, the political talks in Meereen, Arya’s first contract, Cersei’s isolation, and Sansa’s revelation about her brothers.)

(The narrative gives the full horror of the Hardhome battle, the political talks in Meereen, Arya’s first contract, Cersei’s isolation, and Sansa’s revelation about her brothers.)

Episode 9: The Dance of Dragons
Surviving wildlings enter Castle Black. Alliser lets them in but warns Jon’s good heart may get them all killed. Jon is despondent; Sam points out every life saved matters.

Ramsay’s twenty men burn Stannis’s food and siege weapons. The army is trapped. Stannis sends Davos to Castle Black for supplies (to get him out of the way). Davos says goodbye to Shireen and gives her a carved stag. Stannis visits Shireen, talks of the Dance of the Dragons history, then has her burned alive by Melisandre as a king’s blood sacrifice to end the storm. Selyse breaks and tries to stop it but is held back. Shireen screams for her parents as she burns. Stannis watches until he cannot.

In Dorne Doran agrees Myrcella will return to King’s Landing with Trystane, who will take Oberyn’s Small Council seat. The betrothal stands. Ellaria is warned. Bronn is released after Areo elbows him as payback for hitting Trystane. Myrcella and Jaime begin to bond.

In Meereen the fighting pits reopen. Jorah fights his way to Daenerys and is recognized. Tyrion is revealed. Sons of the Harpy attack en masse. Hizdahr is killed. Drogon arrives, burns attackers, and Daenerys climbs onto his back and flies away, leaving her people behind.

Arya is about to poison the Thin Man when she sees Meryn Trant with young girls in a brothel. She abandons the contract.

(The story details the wildling arrival, the horror of Shireen’s sacrifice, the Dornish compromise, the pit massacre and Drogon’s rescue, and Arya’s choice to pursue her own list.)

(The story details the wildling arrival, the horror of Shireen’s sacrifice, the Dornish compromise, the pit massacre and Drogon’s rescue, and Arya’s choice to pursue her own list.)

Episode 10: Mother's Mercy
The snow melts after Shireen’s death. Half of Stannis’s men desert with the horses. Selyse hangs herself. Melisandre flees. Stannis marches anyway and is crushed by the Bolton cavalry. Wounded, he is found by Brienne, who declares she is there for Renly and executes him after he tells her to do her duty.

Sansa escapes her room with the corkscrew, lights the candle too late, and is cornered by Myranda and Reek. Myranda aims a bow and says Ramsay only needs Sansa alive enough to produce an heir. Theon finally breaks free, throws Myranda to her death, and jumps from the wall with Sansa into the snow.

In Braavos Arya (wearing Ghita’s face) kills Meryn Trant in the brothel, stabbing his eyes and body, reminding him of Syrio, then cutting his throat. She returns the face. Jaqen and the Waif say the life was not hers to take. Jaqen drinks poison and “dies”; the Waif now wears his face. Arya pulls faces from the body until she sees her own and goes blind.

In Meereen with Daenerys gone, Tyrion, Missandei, and Grey Worm will hold the city. Jorah and Daario go to find her. Varys reappears to help Tyrion. Daenerys, stranded with an injured Drogon, is surrounded by a Dothraki khalasar. She drops a ring as a trail.

In Dorne Ellaria kisses Myrcella goodbye with poison on her lips. On the ship Myrcella tells Jaime she knows he is her father and is glad. Her nose bleeds and she collapses. Ellaria takes the antidote on shore.

In King’s Landing Cersei finally confesses to adultery with Lancel but denies incest and regicide. She is allowed to return to the Red Keep after a walk of atonement: stripped, hair cut, forced to walk naked through the streets while the crowd screams “shame” and throws filth. Bloody-footed she reaches the Keep. Qyburn covers her and introduces the silent giant in Kingsguard armor (the reanimated Mountain). He carries her inside.

At the Wall Jon tells Sam about Hardhome. Sam leaves for the Citadel with Gilly and the baby to become a maester. Davos returns; Melisandre arrives broken and silent about Shireen. That night Olly lures Jon with a story about Benjen. Jon finds a “traitor” sign. Alliser and the others stab him one by one, saying “For the Watch.” Olly delivers the final blow. Jon dies in the snow.

Episode 1: The Red Woman
In the North, at Winterfell, Ramsay Bolton stands over the body of Myranda, the woman who had helped torment Sansa. He speaks to Maester Wolkan about how she never feared him the way others did. When asked about burial or a pyre, Ramsay coldly orders her body fed to his hounds. Roose Bolton confronts his son about the recent victory over Stannis Baratheon’s army. He points out that Sansa’s escape has weakened their position; a Lannister force marching north could crush them. Ramsay insists his best men and hounds will recapture her. Roose warns that if Ramsay fails, the unborn child of his new wife Walda will become the true heir instead.

Meanwhile, Sansa Stark and Theon Greyjoy have survived their desperate jump from Winterfell’s walls. They flee through the snowy Wolfswood as Bolton men and hounds pursue them. Theon tries to throw off the scent by crossing a freezing river, then holds Sansa close for warmth behind a fallen tree. The dogs close in. Theon attempts to lead them away, telling Sansa to head north to Castle Black and Jon Snow. Bolton soldiers catch them. Theon lies that Sansa died in the fall, but the hounds find her. The leader mocks Theon about the horrors Ramsay will inflict. Just then Brienne of Tarth and Podrick Payne arrive. Brienne cuts down most of the men with skilled, brutal efficiency. Podrick fights one using the techniques Brienne taught him and kills him. Another knocks Podrick down, but Theon seizes a sword and finishes the attacker. Sansa, seeing Brienne’s loyalty and strength, formally accepts her into service. They prepare to continue north.

In Braavos, blind Arya Stark begs on the streets. The Waif approaches with fighting sticks and forces one into Arya’s hands. Arya protests she cannot fight while blind. The Waif replies that is not her problem and beats Arya repeatedly. Arya flails weakly in defense. The Waif stops and says they will meet again the next day, leaving Arya bruised and determined.

In Meereen, Tyrion Lannister and Varys walk the streets disguised as merchants. They encounter a starving woman with a baby. Tyrion offers a coin for the child to eat, but his poor High Valyrian makes her think he wants to buy the baby to eat it. Varys quickly explains. The woman accepts. As they continue, Tyrion stresses the need to find the leader of the Sons of the Harpy to restore peace. Varys says his little birds are already gathering information. Suddenly a screaming crowd flees a massive cloud of smoke. The ships in the harbor are all ablaze. Tyrion dryly notes they will not be sailing to Westeros anytime soon.

In the Dothraki Sea, Daario Naharis and Jorah Mormont track Daenerys. They find the charred remains of a ram killed by Drogon’s fire and many hoof prints. Jorah spots the ring Daenerys deliberately dropped as a trail. Meanwhile Daenerys herself is bound and brought before Khal Moro as a prize. Moro intends to rape her, but she declares she is the widow of Khal Drogo. Moro unbinds her and promises safety. She offers a thousand horses for safe return to Meereen. Moro’s wives explain that as a khal’s widow she must go to Vaes Dothrak and join the dosh khaleen, living out her days among the other widows in the temple. She has no choice.

In Dorne’s Water Gardens, Ellaria Sand helps Prince Doran Martell into his wheelchair. They speak of Oberyn; Doran envied his brother’s adventurous life while Ellaria notes Doran would have been a poor adventurer and Oberyn a poor ruler. Maester Caleotte brings a message that Myrcella is dead. Before Doran can react, Tyene Sand stabs Areo Hotah in the back, killing him. Ellaria stabs Doran in the chest. His guards do nothing; they have sided with her. As she twists the knife she rages that he stayed passive while his sister Elia and brother Oberyn were murdered. The people of Dorne are with her now. Dying, Doran begs her to spare his son Trystane. She scoffs. Doran dies in a pool of blood.

In King’s Landing, Cersei sits alone until a servant announces a ship from Dorne. She runs joyfully to the harbor, believing Myrcella has returned, only to see Jaime standing grimly beside a shrouded body. She realizes her daughter is dead and collapses in grief. Later in the Red Keep she asks Jaime when he first saw a dead body; he answers it was their mother’s. She describes her own horror at their mother’s corpse and says she does not want to look upon Myrcella’s. She reveals Maggy the Frog’s prophecy to him, but Jaime dismisses it as nonsense.

Margaery remains imprisoned by the Faith. The High Sparrow visits and asks if she is ready to confess. She admits no one is without sin. He says she is on the right path but still has far to go. Meanwhile Obara and Nymeria Sand board Trystane’s ship. They announce they will kill him. Nymeria offers him the choice of opponent; he picks her. As he faces Nymeria, Obara drives a spear through the back of his head, killing him.

At the Wall, Jon Snow’s body still lies where the mutineers left it. Ghost howls and scratches at the door. Davos Seaworth investigates and finds the body just as Eddison Tollett and other loyal brothers arrive. They carry Jon inside. Edd closes Jon’s eyes and curses Alliser Thorne. Davos asks whom Edd trusts; Edd answers only those in the room. Davos has him bring Ghost inside for protection. Melisandre arrives, saying she saw Jon fighting at Winterfell in the flames. The others doubt a dead man can fight. She withdraws.

Thorne, Othell Yarwyck, and Bowen Marsh address the Night’s Watch brothers, justifying the murder of Jon for bringing wildlings through the Wall. Most brothers side with them. Inside the locked room with Jon’s body, Davos notes Thorne will move soon. Edd wants revenge but Davos points out they are badly outnumbered. He reminds them of the wildlings nearby who owe Jon their lives. Edd slips out to fetch them while the others bar the door.

Thorne approaches with armed men and offers Davos and the loyalists full amnesty, a horse, and safe passage south, even taking Melisandre. Davos mocks the offer by requesting mutton so he will not starve. Thorne says food will be provided if they surrender by sundown.

Alone in her chambers, Melisandre looks defeated. She undresses before a mirror, removes her glowing ruby necklace, and her youthful glamour fades. She becomes a frail, ancient woman with sagging skin, thin white hair, and a bent body. Despondent, she climbs into bed naked and covers herself.

Episode 2: Home
Beyond the Wall, Bran Stark continues training with the Three-Eyed Raven (Brynden Rivers). In a vision he watches young Ned and Benjen Stark sparring in Winterfell’s yard. He sees young Lyanna Stark, Old Nan, and Ser Rodrik Cassel. He also sees a young stableboy who is Hodor—then called Wylis—who speaks normally and is not simple-minded. Bran wants to stay longer but the Raven pulls him out, warning that lingering in visions is dangerous. Outside, Meera Reed still grieves her brother Jojen. Leaf the Child of the Forest tells her Bran will need her when he eventually leaves the cave.

In King’s Landing a drunken man boasts in a tavern about mocking Cersei during her walk of atonement. Outside he is confronted by Ser Gregor Clegane (the Mountain), who smashes his head against the wall, killing him, then returns to Cersei’s side.

Myrcella’s funeral is held in the Great Sept of Baelor, but Cersei is confined to the Red Keep by Tommen’s order for fear the Faith Militant will re-arrest her. Jaime and Tommen speak of Myrcella and Trystane. Tommen blames Cersei somewhat for Trystane’s death but is not angry. Jaime urges him to visit and apologize to his mother. The High Sparrow enters. After Tommen leaves, Jaime threatens the High Sparrow, asking why Cersei is punished for sins while the Sparrow is not punished for Jaime’s own past crime of killing the Mad King he swore to protect. Jaime nearly kills him, but the High Sparrow shows no fear. He explains that individual Sparrows mean nothing; together they can topple empires.

Tommen visits Cersei and apologizes for not protecting her more strongly. He says he should have torn the sept down with the High Sparrow inside. He needs her help to be a strong king. Cersei, uncharacteristically quiet, embraces him.

In Meereen, Missandei and Grey Worm tell Tyrion that Rhaegal and Viserion have stopped eating since Daenerys left. Tyrion says dragons hate captivity and may eat again if freed. He believes they remember friends. Tyrion and Varys go below the pyramid. Tyrion advances alone into the darkness. One dragon emerges; Tyrion holds its gaze. The second appears. He sets down his torch, speaks gently of how as a child he wanted a dragon for his nameday and how his father told him they were extinct, making him cry. He reaches the first collar and releases the pin, then frees the second. The dragons retreat. Tyrion hurries back and tells Varys to punch him if he ever suggests anything like that again.

In Braavos, the Waif again approaches blind Arya and asks her name. Arya says “no one.” The Waif hits her, saying neither of them believes it. Arya tries to fight back. Suddenly the Waif is replaced by Jaqen H’ghar. He promises that if she says her name she will sleep under a roof, eat, and regain her sight. Each time Arya insists she has no name. Satisfied, Jaqen leads her back; she is a beggar no more.

At Winterfell, Ramsay, Roose, and Harald Karstark discuss Sansa and Jon. Ramsay wants to storm Castle Black. Roose warns that attacking the Night’s Watch would turn the entire North against them and that Ramsay must act more wisely or be discarded. Maester Wolkan announces that Walda has given birth to a boy. Roose tells Ramsay he will always be treated as firstborn. Ramsay thanks him, then stabs his father to death in front of the maester. As the new Lord Bolton he orders Wolkan to announce that Roose was poisoned by enemies. He personally feeds Walda and the newborn to his hounds.

In the woods Brienne tells Sansa about meeting Arya. Sansa is reluctant to speak of her torment under Ramsay but admits she should have accepted Brienne’s help sooner. Theon, crushed by guilt over betraying the Starks, decides to leave and go home to the Iron Islands rather than continue to Castle Black. He tells Sansa that Brienne and Podrick will protect her better. They embrace; he takes a horse and departs.

On the Iron Islands, at Pyke on a stormy night, Yara Greyjoy reads a letter to King Balon: the Glovers have retaken Deepwood Motte and killed the Ironborn garrison. Their northern invasion has failed. Balon wants to keep fighting. Yara argues the mainland strongholds are worthless to Ironborn so far from the sea, and that her rescue attempt for Theon was not a waste. She reminds him of the last Greyjoy Rebellion that cost two of her brothers. Balon says when she rules she can be content; until then she obeys or he will make another heir.

Balon crosses a rope bridge between towers. A man blocks his way—his younger brother Euron Greyjoy, long thought lost. Euron mocks the Drowned God and claims he is the god. He admits cutting out his crew’s tongues for silence and that he once had to be tied to the mast in a storm. He says Balon has ruled too long. Balon tries to stab him; Euron throws him off the bridge to his death.

At Balon’s funeral Yara swears to Aeron Greyjoy (another brother and priest) that she will feed the killer to sharks alive. Aeron says the kingsmoot will choose the next ruler, not her father’s wish.

At Castle Black night has fallen. The loyalists still hold the room with Jon’s body. Thorne’s men prepare to batter the door. Edd returns with Tormund and a host of wildlings, including the giant Wun Wun. Thorne orders the Watch to fight; only one foolish brother charges and is cut down. An archer shoots Wun Wun, who seizes him, smashes him against stone, and throws the body at Thorne’s feet. The rest surrender. Thorne is seized; Olly is disarmed by Tormund. No wildlings die.

Later Melisandre, Davos, and the loyalists stand over Jon’s body. Melisandre performs a ritual, cutting his hair, washing him, and chanting over him in the name of the Lord of Light. Nothing happens. She leaves disappointed. Davos and Edd leave too. Ghost, who had been under the table, stirs. Jon gasps and awakens.

Episode 3: Oathbreaker
At the Wall Jon Snow sits up, gasping, staring at his stab wounds in horror. Davos helps him. Jon remembers being stabbed by Olly and Thorne for bringing the wildlings south. Melisandre enters, amazed the resurrection worked. She asks what he saw after death. Jon says nothing. Disappointed yet hopeful, she declares the Lord of Light brought him back for a reason; Stannis was not the Prince That Was Promised, but someone must be. Davos asks her to leave so Jon can adjust.

Davos notes the situation is completely mad. Jon laments he tried to do right and was murdered for it; why was he brought back? Davos says they may never know, but the point is to keep living and fighting. Jon feels he failed. Davos replies, “Good. Now go fail again.”

Jon dons his armor and Lord Commander’s cloak and walks into the courtyard. Free Folk and brothers gather. He greets a stunned Tormund, who hugs him (hurting the wounds). He embraces Edd. Jon jokes he is still himself, not a wight, so hold off burning the body.

Later Jon oversees the hanging of the mutineers: Bowen Marsh, Othell Yarwyck, Alliser Thorne, and Olly. Marsh says Jon should not be alive. Jon replies neither should killing him have been. Yarwyck asks Jon to write his mother that he died fighting wildlings honorably. Thorne says he chose the Watch over his commander; Jon’s wildling alliance was too dangerous. Jon respects that Thorne followed his convictions. Olly glares in silence. Jon cuts the rope. All four die. Jon removes his cloak, hands it to Edd, and declares his watch has ended. He walks away as the brothers stare in shock.

On the Narrow Sea Samwell Tarly, Gilly, and little Sam sail toward Oldtown. Sam is seasick. Gilly is excited; the captain called Oldtown the most beautiful city. Sam realizes he cannot take Gilly into the all-male Citadel, so he decides to stop first at his family home of Horn Hill. His mother and sister are kind even if his father Randyll is not. Gilly agrees to follow his lead for their safety.

Beyond the Wall Bran has another vision: the Tower of Joy in Dorne at the end of Robert’s Rebellion. Young Ned Stark and a small party including Howland Reed (Meera’s father) confront the last two Targaryen Kingsguard—Ser Arthur Dayne (Sword of the Morning) and Lord Commander Gerold Hightower. Ned asks why they were not at the Trident. Dayne says Rhaegar ordered them to guard the tower. They draw swords. “And now it begins,” Dayne says. “No, now it ends,” Ned replies. Dayne fights with two swords and cuts down several northmen. Hightower falls to Ned. Dayne duels Ned and gains the upper hand, kicking away Ned’s sword—until Howland stabs him from behind through the neck. Ned finishes him, uncomfortable with the dishonorable win. Bran is shocked; the stories never mentioned this. Ned hears a woman’s scream from the tower and runs toward it. Bran tries to follow, calling out. The Raven pulls him back, saying he stayed too long. The past cannot be changed

. Ned hears a woman’s scream from the tower and runs toward it. Bran tries to follow, calling out. The Raven pulls him back, saying he stayed too long. The past cannot be changed. The Raven has waited a thousand years for Bran; Bran must learn everything before leaving, but he will not share the Raven’s fate.

In King’s Landing Qyburn gathers Varys’s former little birds (child spies) with candied plums from Dorne. Cersei, Jaime, and the Mountain enter. Cersei wants information from Dorne, Highgarden, the North—anywhere enemies plot against them.

At the Small Council, Grand Maester Pycelle complains about Qyburn. Kevan Lannister (Hand of the King), Pycelle, and Mace Tyrell sit with Olenna Tyrell lobbying for Margaery and Loras’s release. Cersei, Jaime, and Gregor barge in. Cersei claims her right as queen; Olenna corrects that the true queen is Margaery, married to the king. Jaime claims his right as Lord Commander of the Kingsguard. Pycelle notes Gerold Hightower once sat on the council but dismisses it as the Mad King’s eccentricity. Cersei accuses Kevan of not caring about Myrcella. Jaime urges action against Ellaria and the Sand Snakes who seized Dorne. Kevan and the others leave in displeasure.

Tommen angrily visits the High Sparrow seeking permission for Cersei to visit Myrcella’s resting place. The Sparrow refuses until her other sins are cleared. Tommen criticizes the treatment after her atonement. The Sparrow admires Cersei’s love for her son as divine Motherly love and says the Seven work even through those who do not acknowledge them. Tommen leaves less angry, more uncertain.

In Meereen Varys interrogates Vala, a prostitute who seduced and murdered Second Sons and Unsullied for the Sons of the Harpy. She is defiant, claiming patriotism for the old ways. Varys offers her and her son safe passage to Pentos with silver if she names the funders; otherwise execution and her son orphaned. She agrees. The Wise Masters of Yunkai, Good Masters of Astapor, and Volantis have been funding the Harpies. Grey Worm wants to attack the cities; Missandei warns that would leave Meereen undefended. Tyrion has Varys send a message via the little birds.

In Vaes Dothrak Daenerys enters the temple of the dosh khaleen. (The full arrival and initial interactions continue her captivity among the widows.)

Episode 4: Book of the Stranger
In King’s Landing beneath the Great Sept, Septa Unella leads Margaery to the High Sparrow. He asks what she would do if freed. She wants her family and husband Tommen. He lectures that attachment leads to sin, recounting his own past as a womanizing, drunken cobbler who converted after an orgy. Margaery impresses him by knowing the Book of the Stranger (which Unella had read at her). He allows her to visit Loras.

Loras lies dejected in his cell, broken. Margaery urges him to stay strong; he is the future of House Tyrell. He only wants the torment to end and begs her help. She says the Sparrow wants them to break each other.

In the Red Keep Cersei finds Pycelle advising Tommen to accommodate the Faith. She dismisses Pycelle and speaks alone with her son. Tommen wants to avoid endangering Margaery further. Cersei reminds him of her own humiliation and that the Sparrow respects no kings or queens. Tommen reveals a secret the Sparrow shared.

Armed with it, Cersei interrupts a Small Council meeting of Kevan, Olenna, and Jaime. They are hostile at first. She reveals the High Sparrow plans a walk of atonement for Margaery. Olenna is horrified. Jaime proposes the Tyrell army march into the city, surround the Sept, and force the release of Margaery and Loras without bloodshed (or with Sparrow blood). Tommen forbade only the Lannister army from acting, so Kevan’s forces can simply stand down. Kevan hesitates until Cersei reminds him the Sparrows took his son Lancel. Olenna agrees blood will be shed either way; better the Sparrows’.

At Castle Black Edd watches Jon pack. He scolds Jon for leaving after his oath. Jon replies he already gave his life and cannot trust the brothers. Edd reminds him of Hardhome and the coming enemy. Horns sound. Sansa, Brienne, and Podrick ride in. Jon and Sansa embrace for the first time since childhood. That night they reminisce. Sansa wants to retake Winterfell; Jon says he is done fighting after hanging Olly.

Davos asks if Melisandre will stay. She will do as the Prince That Was Promised commands. Davos presses about Stannis and Shireen; she is reluctant. Brienne enters, recognizes them as Stannis’s people, and warns Melisandre she neither forgets nor forgives Renly’s murder. She reveals she executed Stannis after he admitted using bloodmagic.

Jon receives Ramsay’s “Bastard Letter”: Ramsay has Rickon. If Sansa is not returned he will slaughter every wildling at Castle Black, rape Sansa, and feed Jon and Rickon to his dogs. Tormund has only about 2,000 fighters against Ramsay’s estimated 5,000. Sansa insists the northern houses will unite behind Jon as Ned Stark’s son. Jon agrees to fight.

At Runestone young Robin Arryn practices (badly) at archery under Yohn Royce. Petyr Baelish arrives with a falcon gift. Royce confronts him: Baelish said he was taking Sansa to the Fingers, yet she married Ramsay. Baelish claims Bolton men attacked them and accuses Royce of leaking her location. Robin, as Lord of the Vale, is asked to judge. Robin considers the Moon Door. Royce swears loyalty; Baelish recommends mercy. Royce realizes Littlefinger controls Robin. Baelish and Robin decide to muster the Vale knights and march north to aid Sansa.

At Winterfell Osha is brought before Ramsay. He values Rickon but is unsure about her. She denounces the Starks as forced masters and tries to seduce him, climbing onto his lap while reaching for his knife. Ramsay reveals Theon told him everything, including how she once seduced Theon to free Bran and Rickon. She lunges; he slits her throat and calmly resumes peeling an apple as she dies.

On Pyke Theon returns home to learn Balon is dead. Yara is angry he refused her earlier rescue. He says Ramsay broke him into a thousand pieces (she notes they received one piece in a box). She thinks he wants the crown; he insists he wants her to rule and will support her.
