In Meereen Tyrion, Grey Worm, Missandei, and Varys meet envoys from the masters of Astapor, Yunkai, and Volantis (including Yezzan zo Qaggaz, whom Tyrion once served as a slave). Grey Worm wants force. Tyrion claims empathy from one day as a slave; Missandei says that is not true slavery. They negotiate terms for peace and the end of funding the Harpies. (Tyrion’s deal-making continues, securing a fragile truce while Daenerys is still absent.)

Episode 5: The Door
At the Wall Sansa receives a message from Littlefinger requesting a meeting in Mole’s Town. With Brienne she confronts him furiously about knowing what Ramsay was. He claims ignorance and offers the knights of the Vale waiting at Moat Cailin. She describes her wedding night torment; he looks horrified and apologizes, offering protection. She doubts him and threatens Brienne will kill him. He will do whatever she asks. She orders him never to return. As he leaves he informs her that Brynden “Blackfish” Tully has retaken Riverrun and she should seek his help. She says she already has Jon’s wildling army. “Half-brother,” he corrects.

A war council at Castle Black: Sansa, Brienne, Podrick, Jon, Davos, Melisandre, Tormund, Edd. The Karstarks and Umbers have declared for Ramsay. They must summon the remaining northern houses—Mormont, Glover, Cerwyn, Mazin. Sansa says “the North remembers” and will fight for the Stark name. She reveals the Blackfish holds Riverrun (claiming she learned it from Ramsay’s ravens to hide Littlefinger’s involvement). She sends Brienne and Podrick to secure Tully help while the rest build an army. Before leaving she gives Jon a new cloak bearing the Stark direwolf, like their father’s.

In Braavos the Waif drills Arya, mocking her high birth. Jaqen explains the Faceless Men began as Valyrian slaves who founded Braavos and the House of Black and White. He gives Arya a vial of poison; her target is the actress Lady Crane. Arya watches a play, The Bloody Hand, a crude retelling of recent Westerosi wars. She enjoys the spectacle until her father Ned is portrayed as a buffoon and the actress playing Sansa bares her breasts. Afterward she observes Lady Crane (playing Cersei), who seems decent. Arya plans to poison Crane’s private rum, suspecting a jealous younger actress Bianca hired the kill. Jaqen cuts her off: a servant does not question.

In Vaes Dothrak Daenerys struggles with what to do about Jorah, who has returned twice after banishment and saved her life twice. He confesses his love but also shows his spreading greyscale. This time he must leave for good and will end his life before the disease takes him fully. She tearfully orders him to find a cure and return when she conquers Westeros. He departs. Daenerys and Daario lead the Dothraki horde toward Meereen.

In Meereen, with a fragile peace holding, Tyrion wants the people to believe everything is done with Daenerys’s blessing so the masters cannot use his and Varys’s foreign status against them. He invites Kinvara, High Priestess of the Red Temple of Volantis. She readily agrees to spread word that Daenerys is the Prince That Was Promised. Varys is skeptical, recalling Melisandre’s failed declaration for Stannis. Kinvara says humans err even when the Lord of Light has a plan. She unnerves Varys by knowing exactly how a second-rate sorcerer castrated him and offering to repeat the words he heard in the flames. She promises to send suitable preachers.

On the Iron Islands the kingsmoot is held on Old Wyk. Yara claims the Salt Throne first, arguing they must do more than raid—they must teach the mainland a lesson with real force. A man challenges her for being a woman and notes Theon’s return. Theon endorses Yara as a true warrior and reaver. Many shout for her. Euron arrives, mocks Theon’s emasculation and Yara’s sex, admits killing Balon because he was leading them to defeat, and regrets not doing it sooner. The crowd cheers. Theon notes Euron was away while Yara commanded ships. Yara proposes a massive fleet to strike Westeros. Euron agrees to expand the fleet and reveals his plan: marry Daenerys Targaryen and bring her army and dragons to Westeros. The Ironborn acclaim him king. Aeron drowns and revives him in the traditional rite. Yara, Theon, and their loyalists flee during the ceremony with the best ships of the Iron Fleet. Euron, upon learning, orders new ships built to pursue and kill them.

Beyond the Wall the Three-Eyed Raven shows Bran a vision of the creation of the first White Walker: Leaf and the Children of the Forest, desperate in their war with the First Men, drive a dragonglass dagger into a captive man’s chest, transforming him into the Night King. Bran confronts Leaf; she says they were losing and had no choice. Later, alone, Bran wargs into the weirwood without permission and walks among the Army of the Dead. The Night King and White Walkers see him. The Night King grabs Bran’s arm, marking him. Bran wakes screaming. The Raven says the Night King can now find him and bypass the cave’s protective magic. They must leave immediately; Bran must become the Three-Eyed Raven. Bran asks if he is ready. “No,” the Raven says, and Bran’s eyes whiten as another vision begins.

Outside, the air turns freezing. The Night King and White Walkers approach. The Children fire magical projectiles and light a fire barrier, but the Walkers extinguish a path and the wights swarm over and through the weirwood roots. Meera kills one Walker with dragonglass and fights beside the remaining Children. Summer the direwolf dies attacking wights. Leaf sacrifices herself in an explosion. Meera screams for Bran to warg into Hodor. In the vision Bran is at Winterfell watching young Ned say goodbye to his father Rickard before going to the Vale as a ward. Hearing Meera, and urged by the Raven, Bran wargs simultaneously into present-day Hodor and young Wylis. Hodor loads Bran onto a sled and hauls him toward the exit tunnel with Meera and Leaf. The Night King kills the Three-Eyed Raven; his form in the vision disintegrates

. Hodor loads Bran onto a sled and hauls him toward the exit tunnel with Meera and Leaf. The Night King kills the Three-Eyed Raven; his form in the vision disintegrates. At the door Meera yells “Hold the door!” Wylis in the past seizes and begins repeating the words; they slur and shorten until he can only say “Hodor.” Present Hodor holds the door against the wights as Meera and Bran escape, sacrificing himself as the undead pour through and tear him apart.

Episode 6: Blood of My Blood
Beyond the Wall Meera pulls Bran’s sled through the snow while he remains locked in cascading visions: Aerys screaming “Burn them all!”, the Red Wedding, his family, Hardhome wights, wildfire, dragons, Jaime and the Iron Throne. Wights close in. Meera collapses, draws her sword, and apologizes for failing him. A mysterious rider appears, cutting down wights with a sickle and flaming flail. He urges them onto his horse because the dead do not rest. Later, safe for the moment, the rider reveals he was sent by the Three-Eyed Raven who “lives again.” Bran wakes. The rider is Benjen Stark, Bran’s uncle—disfigured. A White Walker stabbed him and left him for dead, but the Children saved him and halted the transformation into a full wight. He tells Bran he must now be the Three-Eyed Raven and wait for the White Walkers when they come for the realms of men.

At Horn Hill Sam, Gilly, and little Sam arrive. Sam warns they must claim the baby is his son and hide that Gilly is a wildling; his father hates them. Lady Melessa and sister Talla greet them warmly, delighted at the “grandchild.” Talla offers Gilly a dress and room. At dinner Lord Randyll and brother Dickon join. Sam announces he will train as a maester then return to the Wall. Randyll mocks Sam’s weight and false claims of hunting and fighting skill (which Sam admits belong to Gilly and Jon). Gilly defends Sam by listing his real heroics, accidentally revealing she is from beyond the Wall. Randyll’s prejudice erupts. Melessa, furious, says Randyll is the one dishonoring the house and storms out with the women. Randyll allows Gilly and the baby to stay (she will work in the kitchens; the boy raised as a bastard) but Sam must leave forever at first light. Sam later apologizes to Gilly for not standing up, then returns, saying they stay together
. Sam later apologizes to Gilly for not standing up, then returns, saying they stay together. They leave immediately; Sam takes the family Valyrian steel sword Heartsbane.

In King’s Landing Tommen speaks with the High Sparrow about Margaery’s planned walk of atonement. The Sparrow lets him see her. Tommen finds Margaery speaking positively of the Sparrow and contritely about her past vanity. He begins agreeing with her.

Mace Tyrell leads a Tyrell army through the streets to Jaime. Together they reach the Great Sept where the High Sparrow, Unella, Faith Militant, and crowd prepare for the walk. Jaime demands the release of Margaery and Loras. The Sparrow refuses, saying every Sparrow yearns to die for the gods. Then he announces there will be no walk: Margaery has already atoned by bringing another into the Faith. The doors open and Tommen emerges, escorted, wearing a seven-pointed star on his Kingsguard’s breastplates. He joins the Sparrow and Margaery, declaring the Crown and Faith are the two pillars of the realm and will bring glory together. The crowd cheers. Olenna realizes the Sparrow has beaten them. Jaime seethes.

Later Tommen strips Jaime of his Kingsguard position because an attack on the Faith is an attack on the Crown, but allows him to continue serving elsewhere. Jaime complains to Cersei; he wants Bronn to gather killers and storm the Sept. Cersei says he must go to Riverrun instead and take the castle cleanly. She does not need him for her trial—it will be trial by combat and she has the Mountain. They will still defeat their enemies. They kiss.

In Braavos Arya watches the play again. The Cersei monologue has been changed per her earlier suggestion (vengeance instead of pure grief). She is moved by Lady Crane’s performance and notices Bianca mouthing the lines. Backstage she poisons Crane’s rum but hesitates. Crane recognizes her from the audience. They talk; Arya feels kinship. She suggests the original speech was wrong for the real Cersei. Crane is impressed and asks if Arya likes pretending to be someone else. Unsettled, Arya leaves. Crane argues with the company leader about the script. Just as she raises the poisoned rum Arya returns, knocks it away, points at Bianca, and warns her. The Waif witnesses and reports to Jaqen, requesting permission to kill Arya. Jaqen reluctantly agrees—she is not to suffer. Arya retrieves Needle, hides in a dark room, blows out the candle, and waits.

At the Twins Walder Frey learns Riverrun is lost to the Blackfish. He blames his sons for letting the Blackfish escape the Red Wedding. Despite numbers, Houses Mallister and Blackwood have risen and the Brotherhood Without Banners raids their lines. Walder demands the castle back and brings out his prisoner Edmure Tully as leverage, joking that Edmure is going home.

In the Dothraki Sea Daenerys and Daario continue with the khalasar toward Meereen (further travel and planning occur).

In the Dothraki Sea Daenerys and Daario continue with the khalasar toward Meereen (further travel and planning occur).

Episode 7: The Broken Man
In the Riverlands Sandor Clegane (the Hound), revealed to have survived his fight with Brienne, lives among a peaceful congregation led by Brother Ray, a septon who found him near death. Ray speaks of justice; Sandor says if there were justice he would already be punished. Ray replies perhaps he has been. Brotherhood Without Banners men arrive demanding tribute; finding nothing of value they leave. Sandor warns they will return and that Ray should arm himself. Ray says violence is a disease not cured by spreading it. Sandor answers it is not cured by dying either. He returns from chopping wood to find the villagers slaughtered and Ray hanged. Enraged, he takes an axe and leaves for revenge.

Jaime and Bronn arrive with the Lannister army at Riverrun. The Freys threaten to hang Edmure if the Blackfish does not surrender. The Blackfish calls their bluff. Disgusted by Frey incompetence, Jaime takes command, parleys with the Blackfish, and offers to spare the garrison if they yield. The Blackfish refuses; he has two years of food and will make the Lannisters pay dearly in blood.

In King’s Landing Margaery studies the Seven-Pointed Star with the High Sparrow. They discuss the Mother’s mercy. She admits she once only pitied the poor while pretending to love them. He asks why she has not joined Tommen in the marriage bed; she says former desires are gone. He reminds her of her duty to produce an heir and makes a veiled threat against Olenna as an unrepentant sinner.

Margaery meets Olenna under Unella’s watch. Olenna insults the septa; Margaery defends her. Alone (as much as possible) Olenna tries to pull Margaery away and urges her to leave for Highgarden. Margaery refuses, insisting her place is with Tommen, but secretly slips Olenna a paper with a drawn rose—the Tyrell sigil—signaling she is only pretending loyalty to the Faith and that Olenna should leave for safety. Olenna understands and plays along.

Cersei confronts Olenna about leaving, begging her to stay for Margaery and Loras’s sake. Olenna blames Cersei for arming the Faith Militant in the first place. Cersei admits the mistake but insists their alliance is more vital than ever. Olenna says Cersei has no power left and that Cersei’s defeat is her only consolation; she will leave at once.

In the North Jon, Sansa, and Davos recruit. With Tormund and Wun Wun they secure the wildlings, who still owe Jon for Hardhome. Davos shows Jon and Sansa Lyanna Mormont’s earlier rejection letter to Stannis. At Bear Island the ten-year-old Lady Lyanna Mormont is blunt and unimpressed. She initially refuses, saying House Stark is dead, Jon is a bastard, Sansa has married enemies, and she needs her men to defend her island. Davos intervenes, speaking of the White Walkers’ threat to all living. She agrees to send all 62 men she can spare, each fighting like ten.

At Deepwood Motte Robett Glover gives a cold reception. Robb Stark failed to protect them from the Ironborn; he will not risk more for the remaining Starks. They leave with only minor houses (Mormont, Hornwood, Mazin)—about 405 extra men. Jon wants to attack Winterfell soon before Ramsay gathers more and winter deepens. Sansa wants more houses (Cerwyn). When Jon refuses she secretly writes to Littlefinger accepting his earlier offer of Vale troops.

In Volantis Theon and Yara hide with the Iron Fleet. In a brothel Yara carouses while Theon sits despondent. She pushes him to drink, reclaim himself, and help her take revenge on Euron and retake the Iron Islands. “Fuck justice,” she says; they will get revenge. He drinks and steadies. She reveals the plan: sail to Meereen and ally with Daenerys before Euron can. She then leaves with a prostitute.

In Braavos Arya walks openly, arranges passage back to Westeros with traders for a large sum, then stands on a bridge gazing at the Titan. An old woman approaches—the Waif in disguise—and repeatedly stabs Arya in the gut, twisting the knife. Arya leaps into the canal and stumbles through the streets, bleeding and terrified.

Episode 8: No One
In Braavos the acting troupe performs the revised Bloody Hand with Lady Crane’s vengeful Cersei speech. Afterward Crane finds injured Arya and tends her wounds. They talk of the future; Crane invites Arya to join the company bound for Pentos. Arya warns of coming danger. Crane gives her milk of the poppy so she can sleep and heal.

The next morning Crane reaches for medicine on a high shelf. Arya wakes to a crash and finds Crane murdered—stabbed by the Waif. The Waif rebukes Arya for not completing the original kill (so Crane would have died cleanly) and now comes for her. Arya flees through streets, under a wagon, into a bathhouse, down stairs overturning vegetable baskets. Her wound reopens. She leaves a bloody trail into a darkened room, hides Needle under a blanket, and waits. The Waif enters, closes the door, and offers Arya the choice of dying on her knees or her feet. Arya stands, draws Needle, slices the candle, and plunges the room into blackness.

Later Jaqen enters the Hall of Faces, follows a blood trail, and finds the Waif’s face (eyes gouged) placed on a shelf. Arya confronts him. He admits sending the Waif. He says she has become No One and passed the test. Arya corrects him: she is Arya Stark of Winterfell and she is going home. Jaqen nods with the faintest smile. Arya leaves.

In Meereen red priestesses preach that Daenerys was sent by the Lord of Light to end slavery. Tyrion and Varys walk the market; Varys is leaving on a secret mission to find Daenerys friends in Westeros. He parts before the docks so the famous dwarf is not seen with him. Tyrion corrects: “the most famous dwarf in the world.”

Later Tyrion drinks with Grey Worm and Missandei to celebrate the city’s recovery. They reluctantly join in honor of their queen. Grey Worm dislikes the taste. Tyrion dreams of a vineyard after conquest. They attempt jokes; Missandei tells one about translators; Grey Worm claims it is the worst he has heard, then smiles—he was joking. Suddenly bombardment begins. Slaver ships from Astapor, Yunkai, and Volantis attack with trebuchets. Diplomacy has failed. Grey Worm takes command, preferring to defend the pyramid. Then they hear movement on the roofs: Daenerys has returned on Drogon.

In King’s Landing Qyburn tells Cersei the Faith Militant have entered the Red Keep demanding she come to the Sept. Lancel is among them. Cersei refuses, citing the Sparrow’s promise she could remain until trial. Lancel says no such promise was made. The Mountain threatens them. One Faith Militant stabs Gregor’s chest; Gregor rips the man’s head off. The others back down.

Later a royal announcement fills the throne room. Kevan bars Cersei from standing beside Tommen; she must sit with the other ladies. Tommen declares Crown and Faith are the two pillars; the Father judges all. Loras and Cersei’s trials will be on the first day of the Festival of the Mother. After prayer he abolishes trial by combat as a scheme to escape the gods’ judgment; they will be tried by seven septons as in the Faith’s early days. Cersei, who planned to use the Mountain as champion, is stunned. Qyburn whispers that his little birds have confirmed an old rumor of hers—and it is far more than rumor.

In the Riverlands Sandor finds Brotherhood men (including those who massacred the village) joking by a fire. He kills two instantly with his axe, then gut-stabs Gatins after a fight and finishes him when the man gives poor last words. Later he comes upon Beric Dondarrion and Thoros of Myr hanging Lem and two other renegades for the unauthorized attack. Sandor wants to kill them himself more painfully. Out of respect Beric lets him hang two; Thoros will not allow butchery. Sandor kicks the blocks and takes Lem’s boots while the body twitches. Afterward he shares a meal. Beric invites him to join; cold winds rise in the North and they fight things that would destroy all life. It is not too late for Sandor to help.

Brienne and Podrick reach Riverrun and find it under Lannister-Frey siege. Lannister horsemen surround them. Brienne says she has come to see Jaime and return Oathkeeper. While she speaks with Jaime, Bronn playfully chokes Podrick then offers lessons in dirty fighting.

(The siege negotiations and further Riverlands events continue, with Jaime weighing options regarding the Blackfish and Edmure.)

Episode 9: Battle of the Bastards
In Meereen the pyramid is bombarded. Daenerys wants to slaughter the masters’ army; Tyrion urges talking first, reminding her of her father’s wildfire plot and what Jaime did to stop it. They meet the masters (Razdal, Belicho, Yezzan). The masters offer safe departure if the Unsullied and Missandei are returned to slavery and the dragons killed. Daenerys says she came to offer them surrender. Drogon lands; she mounts him. Rhaegal and Viserion break free and join. They burn ships. Daario and the Dothraki arrive and rout the Sons of the Harpy at the gates. The masters’ soldiers abandon them. Tyrion demands one master die as punishment. The other two immediately scapegoat lowborn Yezzan. Grey Worm instead slits Razdal’s and Belicho’s throats. Tyrion tells Yezzan to spread word of what he saw.

Afterwards Daenerys and Tyrion meet Yara and Theon, who offer a hundred ships if she helps against Euron and supports their claim to the Iron Islands. Tyrion is wary of Theon because of Winterfell, but Theon says he has paid. Daenerys agrees to an independent Iron Islands on condition the Ironborn stop reaving, pillaging, and raping. Yara balks; Daenerys says their fathers left the world worse—together they can leave it better. Yara agrees. They seal the pact.

In the North Jon, Sansa, Tormund, Davos, Lyanna Mormont and other northern lords parley with Ramsay, Harald Karstark, and Smalljon Umber. Ramsay offers pardon if Jon hands over Sansa. Jon refuses and challenges single combat. Ramsay declines, confident in numbers, and produces Rickon (proved by tossing Shaggydog’s head). Sansa tells Ramsay he will die tomorrow and rides off.

In camp Sansa scolds Jon for not waiting for more men. He says this is all they could gather. She warns of Ramsay’s cruelty; he says he has faced worse and will protect her. She replies no one can keep anyone safe. Davos and Tormund talk of serving Stannis and Mance and wonder if they backed the wrong kings. Davos finds the remains of Shireen’s pyre and the wooden stag he carved for her; he finally understands how she died. Jon tells Melisandre not to resurrect him if he falls. She says the Lord of Light decides.

Next morning Ramsay brings Rickon out, cuts his bonds, and tells him to run to his brother. As Rickon runs, Ramsay shoots arrows. Jon races on horseback. Just as Jon nears, an arrow takes Rickon in the back. Enraged, Jon charges the Bolton lines alone. Davos sends the Stark cavalry. Bolton archers kill Jon’s horse. Ramsay orders his cavalry to crush Jon. The Stark horse smash into the Boltons, saving Jon. Davos holds his archers because the melee is too mixed. Ramsay has no such care and rains arrows on everyone, creating a corpse barrier. Bolton infantry form a three-sided shield-and-spear phalanx that compresses the Stark forces against the body pile. Smalljon leads men over the corpses to complete the encirclement. Wun Wun kills some but cannot break it. Panic spreads; Tormund urges retreat over the pile. Jon is trampled and nearly suffocates under bodies but fights free.

A horn sounds. Sansa and Littlefinger arrive with the Knights of the Vale. They smash the Bolton rear. Smalljon is distracted; Tormund bites his throat and stabs him repeatedly. Ramsay retreats into Winterfell. Jon, Wun Wun, and Tormund pursue. Wun Wun breaks the gates; wildlings pour in and slaughter the remaining garrison. Wun Wun is riddled with arrows and finally killed by Ramsay’s shot through the eye. Ramsay taunts that he will now accept single combat. Jon advances, blocking three arrows with a Mormont shield, knocks the bow away, and beats Ramsay savagely with his fists. Ramsay grins through it until the beating continues. Jon stops when he sees Sansa and has Ramsay locked up.

Stark banners replace Bolton ones. Melisandre watches the courtyard; Davos glares, clutching Shireen’s stag. Jon orders Rickon buried in the crypts beside Ned. Sansa demands to know where Ramsay is held.

That night Sansa visits the kennels. Ramsay is bound to a chair. He goads that she will never be rid of him—he is part of her now. She says his name and deeds will be forgotten. He realizes the hounds (starved for a week by his own order) are approaching, doors left open, his blood scenting them. He orders them to heel; they ignore him. As they tear him apart he screams. Sansa walks away, smiling coldly.

Episode 10: The Winds of Winter
At the Twins Jaime and Bronn arrive to celebrate the retaking of Riverrun. Walder Frey crows and compares them both as kingslayers. Jaime, insulted, mocks Walder’s lack of real battle experience and asks why the Lannisters need the Freys if they cannot even hold the Riverlands, then storms out.

Later Walder eats alone. A new servant girl serves pie. He does not recognize her and gropes her while complaining his sons Black Walder and Lothar are late. She says they are already present and indicates the pie. He opens it and sees their flesh, a fingertip with nail still attached. The girl peels off her face—Arya Stark. She tells him the last thing he will see is a Stark smiling as he dies. She cuts his throat and watches with satisfaction as the architect of the Red Wedding bleeds out.

In King’s Landing the trials of Loras and Cersei are set. Smallfolk, Margaery, Mace, and Kevan enter the Great Sept. Pycelle is lured away by a little bird. Loras is brought first. Instead of trial he confesses everything and begs to join the Faith, renouncing name and Highgarden. The Sparrows carve a seven-pointed star into his forehead. Mace tries to intervene; Margaery holds him back, then protests the mutilation. The Sparrow says he only promised Loras could leave after Cersei’s trial.

Tommen prepares to leave for the trial but the Mountain blocks him. Lancel is sent to fetch Cersei. A little bird lures Lancel into the catacombs. Another leads Pycelle to a room where Qyburn waits; children swarm and stab Pycelle to death. Margaery realizes Cersei and Tommen’s absence means a trap and tries to clear the Sept. The Faith Militant block the doors. Below, the little bird stabs Lancel in the spine. Paralyzed, Lancel sees a cache of wildfire and three candles about to ignite it. He crawls desperately. The wildfire explodes, green fire racing through the tunnels and erupting under the Sept. The High Sparrow is burned to bone; the entire Great Sept and surrounding district are obliterated in a massive blast that levels a wide area of the city.

Cersei watches from a window and smiles amid the screams. Tommen stares from his chambers in shock. Informed that Margaery is dead, he removes his crown, sets it aside, and calmly steps out the window to his death.

Cersei visits captive Septa Unella, strapped to a table. She pours wine on her to wake her, forces her to admit she enjoyed the torment for its own sake, then “confesses” her own crimes (incest, Robert’s death, the Sept massacre) because they felt good. She reminds Unella of the promise that Cersei’s face would be the last she saw, then brings in the Mountain (helmet off) to begin prolonged torture. Cersei leaves, echoing “Shame” three times as Unella screams.

After Tommen’s body is found Cersei’s triumph fades. She insists on seeing his face once more. She orders the body burned and the ashes buried where the Sept stood so he can rest with Joffrey, Myrcella, and Tywin.

Jaime and the army return to see smoke rising from the ruined Sept district. Later Cersei enters the throne room. Qyburn, now Hand, proclaims her Queen of the Seven Kingdoms and crowns her. She sits the Iron Throne. The assembled nobles glare with hatred but fear; she looks only at Jaime, whose face is stony. She has claimed the throne—or what remains of Lannister power.

In Oldtown Sam, Gilly, and little Sam arrive as white ravens are released, announcing winter. At the Citadel a maester is skeptical because records still list Jeor Mormont and Aemon, but allows Sam into the vast library (barring Gilly). Sam wanders in awe among the countless books and scrolls.

Beyond the Wall Benjen leaves Meera and Bran at a weirwood grove within sight of the Wall; the Wall’s magic bars the dead (including him). He will fight for the living as he can. Bran insists he must become the Three-Eyed Raven fully and touches the tree. He returns to the Tower of Joy vision. Ned enters and finds dying Lyanna in a blood-soaked bed. A handmaiden gives him a newborn. Lyanna whispers the baby’s identity and begs Ned to protect him—Robert would kill the child if he knew. As Ned holds his infant nephew the baby’s eyes open: dark, like Jon Snow’s. Bran understands: Jon is Lyanna’s son.

At Winterfell the northern lords gather. Lyanna Mormont shames those who held back and declares Jon the King in the North. One by one the lords (including former doubters) draw swords and acclaim him. Sansa watches with mixed feelings; Littlefinger watches Sansa. Jon is proclaimed King in the North.

In Meereen Daenerys prepares to sail for Westeros. She names Tyrion Hand of the Queen. The fleet—including the Iron Fleet ships of Yara and Theon, the ships taken from the masters, and her own—sets out. Daenerys stands at the prow of her ship with her advisors and dragons flying overhead, finally heading home to reclaim the Iron Throne.

Episode 1: Dragonstone
The story opens in the Riverlands at the Twins. Walder Frey hosts a feast for every Frey who helped in the Red Wedding. He calls them together under the pretense of sharing plans. They offer her rabbit meat and blackberry wine. The soldiers are homesick and talk about missing their families. They ask why she rides south. Arya says she is going to King's Landing to kill the queen. The soldiers laugh, thinking it a joke. Arya smiles and laughs with them.

Elsewhere in the snowy Riverlands, Sandor Clegane travels north with the Brotherhood Without Banners: Beric Dondarrion, Thoros of Myr, and others. They stop at an abandoned farmhouse. Sandor talks with Beric about why the Lord of Light keeps bringing Beric back. Beric does not know. Sandor says he does not believe in divine justice after seeing the farmer and girl die that way. Thoros urges Sandor to look into the fire. At first Sandor sees only logs. At Winterfell, King in the North Jon Snow holds a meeting with the Northern lords and ladies. He organizes defenses against the Night King and the army of the dead. A message arrives from Queen Cersei Lannister. She claims she does not oppose the Starks reclaiming the North from the Boltons but demands they bend the knee to her. Jon focuses on the dead. Sansa warns him not to underestimate Cersei.

Brienne of Tarth spars with Podrick Payne in the yard. Podrick struggles. Tormund watches and comments. Littlefinger tries to needle Sansa about looking unhappy. Sansa says she wants peace. Brienne sees the exchange and walks over. Littlefinger leaves quickly. Brienne asks why Littlefinger is still there. Sansa says the Knights of the Vale helped win the Battle of the Bastards. She knows what Littlefinger wants.

Beyond the Wall, a column of White Walkers on undead horses leads a vast army of wights through a snowstorm. The horde includes undead giants. Bran Stark and Meera Reed reach the gate under Castle Black. Acting Lord Commander Eddison Tollett and Night's Watch brothers challenge them. Meera introduces herself and Bran. Bran proves he knows Edd by mentioning the Fist of the First Men and Hardhome and that Edd has seen the dead. Edd lets them inside, looking nervously at the lands beyond the Wall.

Jaime predicts Daenerys will land at Dragonstone, her birthplace, which is empty after Stannis left and has deep water for ships. Cersei lists enemies: Dorne in the south, the Tyrells in the west/reach, the Starks in the north.

She and Jaime are the only Lannisters who matter. Jaime says they need allies. He reports House Frey has been wiped out. Cersei reminds him she has listened to their father Tywin for forty years and learned.

Neither Gilly nor Sam grasps the full meaning for Jon. Sam is miserable copying bodily functions of old septons. He quits, grabs books, and leaves the Citadel with Gilly and little Sam that night. On Dragonstone Jon walks the grounds. Daenerys arrives on Drogon. The dragon roars at Jon then calms and lets Jon stroke his snout (sensing Targaryen blood?). Daenerys is surprised. Tyrion and Varys discuss the Tarly executions. Varys worries Daenerys has a ruthless streak like her father that Tyrion must curb. They have Bran's message about the dead.

At Winterfell Arya talks to Sansa about practicing with Bran's bow until she hit the bullseye while Ned watched and clapped. She says Ned knew the rules were wrong but she was right. She confronts Sansa with the letter Sansa wrote to Robb. Sansa explains Cersei forced her. Arya says she was not tortured and she saw Sansa at Ned's execution (Sansa did nothing either). Arya accuses betrayal. Sansa says they are only home because of her efforts; Arya chased her own list. The Knights of the Vale (Littlefinger) saved Jon. Maester Wolkan brings a letter from Cersei. Sansa decides to send Brienne as envoy to the parley (Brienne can reason with Jaime). Brienne warns it is dangerous to leave Sansa alone with Littlefinger. Sansa insists her men are loyal. Brienne offers to leave Podrick; Sansa declines.

At Dragonstone Daenerys and Tyrion talk. She likes that he is not a hero who does stupid dangerous things. She lists past loves who were heroes: Drogo, Jorah, Daario, Jon. Tyrion notes they all fell in love with her. She dismisses that Jon is in love. She accidentally insults Tyrion's height then apologizes. They discuss the coming meeting with Cersei. Tyrion knows she cannot be trusted but Daenerys has armies and dragons as backup. Daenerys wonders if they should plan deceit too. Tyrion is against ruling only by fear (like Cersei, Tywin, Joffrey). Beyond the Wall the ranging party (Jon, Jorah, Gendry, Tormund, Beric, Thoros, Sandor, and wildlings/Night's Watch) trudges through snow. Gendry complains of cold; Tormund talks wildling life. Tormund tells Jon the mission is foolhardy; Northern pride costs lives (like Mance). Jon talks of hard talks with Daenerys. Gendry confronts the Brotherhood about selling him to Melisandre. Sandor and Tormund banter about sex. Tormund asks about Sandor's burns; Sandor is offended. Tormund talks of his crush on Brienne and "monstrous" babies. Beric and Jon talk of resurrection by the Lord of Light and fighting death as the enemy. Jon recalls the Night's Watch oath as the shield that guards the realms of men. Sandor sees the arrowhead mountain from his vision and leads them that way.

In a snowstorm they are attacked by a massive undead snow bear (blue eyes, rotting). It kills three men. Beric sets it on fire with his sword but it keeps coming. Thoros is mauled saving Sandor (who freezes at the flames). Jorah kills it with dragonglass. Beric cauterizes Thoros's wounds with his flaming sword. They follow the tracks.

They find a White Walker leading a small group of wights. They ambush. Jon kills the White Walker with Longclaw; the wights it raised collapse except one. The wights stop at the thin ice. The group is trapped on a rock island in the middle as night falls and the dead surround them on all sides. Thoros dies of his wounds; Beric cannot revive him. Gendry is sent running back to Eastwatch to raven Daenerys for help. They wait in the cold, burning the last wood, fighting off probes when the ice thickens.

Daenerys, against Tyrion's counsel, flies north with all three dragons to rescue them. The dragons burn swathes of wights. The party climbs onto the dragons. The Night King appears, takes an ice spear, and hurls it with perfect aim. It pierces Viserion through the neck. Viserion crashes, thrashing, and dies. Daenerys is devastated. Another spear nearly hits Drogon. They escape, but Jon is separated, pulled down fighting. Benjen Stark (Coldhands) suddenly appears on horseback, rescues Jon, and sacrifices himself holding off the dead so Jon can reach the Wall.

At Eastwatch Tormund and others pull Jon inside. Daenerys waits. Jon, half-frozen, finally bends the knee and calls her his queen. He swears loyalty. She accepts, emotional over Viserion. They sail south with the captured wight.

(The Winterfell sister confrontation escalates with the faces and dagger. Littlefinger's schemes continue. The wight hunt is desperate, costly, and succeeds only at the price of a dragon. The Night King now has an undead dragon.)

Outside King's Landing the Unsullied under Grey Worm form ranks. Dothraki hordes ride past. On the walls Jaime and Bronn watch. Bronn is unnerved by soldiers without genitals who fight without the usual motivations. The two armies (former enemies) stand together for the parley.

Episode 1: Winterfell

Jon Snow, Daenerys Targaryen, and their combined army of Unsullied, Dothraki, and northern allies arrive at Winterfell. The people of the winter town watch warily as the foreign forces and two dragons, Drogon and Rhaegal, pass overhead. Northerners fear the dragons and the outsiders. Arya Stark spots Jon and smiles, then reacts with mixed feelings upon seeing Sandor Clegane (the Hound) and brightens at Gendry. Sansa Stark watches from the battlements with caution.

Inside the courtyard, Jon reunites with Bran (now the Three-Eyed Raven) and Sansa. He introduces Daenerys. Formal greetings are brief because Bran immediately announces that the Night King has Viserion and the Army of the Dead has breached the Wall and marches south. There is no time for ceremony.

In the Great Hall, Jon tries to organize defenses. Northern lords, led by young Lyanna Mormont, angrily challenge Jon for bending the knee to Daenerys after they named him King in the North. Jon explains that only with Daenerys’s dragons and armies can they hope to survive. Tyrion Lannister speaks in support, noting that without Jon they would already be dead and that Lannister forces should soon arrive. Sansa questions how they will feed the massive army of Dothraki, Unsullied, and dragons through winter when her stores were planned only for the North. Daenerys replies that dragons eat whatever they want.

Jon later visits the godswood. Arya surprises him. They embrace tightly. She still carries Needle. He shows her Longclaw. They talk of family and Sansa’s distrust of Daenerys. Arya defends Sansa as the smartest person she knows who is protecting their family.

Tyrion reunites awkwardly with Sansa in the courtyard and notes her cleverness in escaping after Joffrey’s death. He still trusts Cersei’s promised armies; Sansa calls him foolish for it. From a distance, Tyrion, Varys, and Davos Seaworth watch Jon and Daenerys together and discuss a possible marriage alliance to strengthen their position.

Jon and Daenerys inspect defenses. She notes Sansa’s dislike. They ride the dragons together over the countryside. Rhaegal accepts Jon easily (a sign of his Targaryen blood, unknown to them). They share a private, romantic moment at a waterfall.

At the forge, Gendry finishes a dragonglass weapon for the Hound. Arya and the Hound exchange gruff words but part on better terms. Arya reunites with Gendry after years apart; he is flustered by how she has grown.

Sansa tells Jon that Lord Glover refuses to come to Winterfell in protest of Jon bending the knee and will face the dead alone at Deepwood Motte. Jon is furious. Sansa shares the anger and questions whether Jon bent the knee purely to save the North or because he loves Daenerys.

Daenerys and Jorah Mormont thank Samwell Tarly in the library for curing Jorah’s greyscale. Sam mentions stealing his father’s Valyrian steel sword Heartsbane. Daenerys reveals she executed Randyll Tarly and his son Dickon after they refused to bend the knee at the Battle of the Goldroad. Sam is devastated and flees in tears.

Sam finds Bran waiting “for an old friend.” Bran urges Sam to tell Jon the truth of his parentage. Sam finds Jon in the crypts by Eddard Stark’s tomb. After sharing the news of his father and brother’s deaths, Sam reveals that Jon’s mother was Lyanna Stark and his father was Rhaegar Targaryen. Jon is Aegon Targaryen, the true heir to the Iron Throne. Jon refuses to believe it at first, insisting Eddard was too honorable to lie, but Sam explains the promise to Lyanna and the danger from Robert Baratheon.

A hooded rider arrives at Winterfell: Jaime Lannister, who has abandoned Cersei to keep his promise to fight for the living. Bran waits for him in the courtyard—the boy Jaime once pushed from a tower.

In King’s Landing, Euron Greyjoy returns with the Golden Company (20,000 men and horses, but no elephants) and presents them to Cersei. He propositions her and they sleep together. Euron boasts he will give her a prince. Meanwhile, Theon Greyjoy and his men free Yara from Euron’s ship. Yara plans to retake the Iron Islands as a safe haven for Daenerys (wights cannot swim) and allows Theon to go north to help the Starks.

Bronn is interrupted while with prostitutes by Qyburn, who rehires him on Cersei’s orders to assassinate both Jaime and Tyrion with Joffrey’s old crossbow if they survive the dead, promising gold, a castle, and a wife.

At Last Hearth, Tormund, Beric Dondarrion, and survivors from Eastwatch meet Eddison Tollett and the remaining Night’s Watch from Castle Black. They find the castle empty of living people but marked by blood. Young Ned Umber’s corpse is pinned to a wall in a spiral of severed limbs—a message from the Night King. The body reanimates as a wight; Beric burns it with his flaming sword. They realize the dead will reach Winterfell soon and ride hard south.

The episode ends with the living gathering at Winterfell under growing tension, secrets, and the approaching Long Night.

Episode 2: A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms

Episode 2: A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms

Jaime stands before Daenerys, Jon, Sansa, Bran, Tyrion, and others in the Great Hall. Daenerys recounts childhood stories of revenge against the man who killed her father. She notes Cersei promised armies but sent only one man. Jaime explains Cersei lied to him too and has Euron’s fleet plus the Golden Company. He came because he promised to fight for the living. Tyrion defends him; Daenerys suspects assassination. Sansa sides against Jaime at first, citing his past attacks on her family. Jaime refuses to apologize for wartime acts done for his house. Bran quietly says, “The things we do for love.” Jaime quotes Brienne: this is about survival beyond loyalty.

Brienne steps forward and defends Jaime’s honor. He lost his hand protecting her, armed her, and sent her to find Sansa because of his oath to Catelyn. Sansa accepts him. Jon says they need every man. Daenerys agrees. Grey Worm returns Widow’s Wail to Jaime. Afterward Daenerys angrily berates Tyrion for trusting Cersei and threatens to replace him as Hand.

At the forge, Arya presses Gendry for her special weapon while he forges dragonglass. She demonstrates deadly throwing skill with arrowheads and speaks of knowing death’s many faces. Gendry describes the wights as pure death.

In the godswood, Jaime finds Bran and apologizes for crippling him. Bran notes Jaime was not sorry then and that the act made Bran into what he is now (the Three-Eyed Raven). Bran is not angry and did not reveal the truth earlier because Jaime was needed for the war. He asks how anyone knows there will be an “afterwards.”

Jaime and Tyrion reunite warmly. They discuss Daenerys, northern distrust of Targaryens and dragons, and Cersei’s real pregnancy. Tyrion feels foolish for believing her. Jaime goes to Brienne on the practice grounds and asks to serve under her command on the left flank, admitting he is no longer the fighter he once was.

Jorah urges Daenerys to forgive Tyrion, saying he learns from mistakes and has her best interests at heart. Daenerys speaks privately with Sansa in the library. They find common ground as women who rule well in a man’s world and share complicated families. Daenerys is at Winterfell because she loves and trusts Jon. Sansa softens but presses what will happen to the North’s independence if Daenerys wins the throne. The conversation is interrupted by news of Theon’s arrival.

Theon reports Yara’s plan for the Iron Islands and asks to fight for the Starks. Sansa embraces him. Missandei faces northern prejudice; Grey Worm promises that after the wars they will go to Naath together with the Unsullied to protect her people.

Edd, Beric, Tormund, and the Night’s Watch arrive with news that Last Hearth has fallen and the dead will reach Winterfell by dawn. Tormund joyfully tackles Jon.

In the war council, Jon notes the dead outnumber them too heavily for a conventional fight even with dragonglass and Valyrian steel. The plan is to target the Night King: if he dies, his army falls. Bran will wait in the godswood as bait because the Night King wants to erase the Three-Eyed Raven’s memory of the world and can track him via the mark from their earlier encounter. Theon and his Ironborn will guard Bran. Dragons will be held back until the Night King commits, then strike. Non-combatants go to the crypts. Tyrion and others are ordered there for safety.

That night the defenders gather. Tyrion and Bran exchange stories. Around the fire, Tyrion, Jaime, Brienne, Podrick, Davos, and Tormund drink and talk. Tormund brags about his giant-related nickname and propositions Brienne (who is uninterested; Jaime intervenes lightly). Arya shares a drink with the Hound. Later Jaime knights Brienne of Tarth as a Knight of the Seven Kingdoms in a quiet, emotional ceremony before the fire—any knight can make a knight. She kneels and rises as Ser Brienne.

Gendry finishes Arya’s weapon (a staff with dual dragonglass blades). They sleep together. Jon tells Daenerys the truth of his parentage in private. She is shaken and wants him to keep it secret so nothing changes between them. He insists he must tell his sisters. Tension grows as the dead draw near. The episode ends on the eve of battle with quiet moments of connection, fear, and resolve among the living.

Episode 3: The Long Night

Episode 3: The Long Night

Night falls at Winterfell. Defenders take positions. Sam receives dragonglass daggers. Tyrion takes wine to the crypts with the non-combatants (women, children, elderly, Varys, Missandei, Sansa eventually). Bran is wheeled to the godswood with Theon, Ironborn, and Alys Karstark as bait. Sansa and Arya oversee walls; Davos another section; Lyanna Mormont the courtyard. Outside, Brienne commands the left flank with Jaime, Podrick, the Hound, Gendry, Edd, and Sam. Grey Worm leads Unsullied. Jorah and Qhono ride with Dothraki cavalry and Ghost. Jon and Daenerys hold the dragons back initially.

Melisandre arrives alone. She has the Dothraki raise their arakhs and prays to the Lord of Light; the blades burst into flame. She tells Davos not to kill her yet—she will be dead before dawn—and looks intently at Arya before entering the castle.

The flaming Dothraki charge into the darkness and are quickly overwhelmed; their lights extinguish amid screams. Jorah returns battered. The massive Army of the Dead advances. Catapults fire flaming barrels. Unsullied form phalanxes but are swarmed by endless wights climbing over each other. Living soldiers kill many with dragonglass and Valyrian steel but are outnumbered.

Daenerys, seeing her Dothraki slaughtered, breaks the plan and attacks on Drogon; Jon follows on Rhaegal. They incinerate thousands of wights in strafing runs, briefly stemming the tide. Jon tries for the White Walkers but a magical blizzard summoned by them blinds everyone. The Night King on Viserion pursues Daenerys; the dragons clash above the clouds.

On the ground the living retreat behind the walls. Edd saves Sam but is killed. Unsullied form a rearguard. Melisandre lights the pitch-filled trench around Winterfell with prayer just in time; the flames hold the wights briefly. Grey Worm and survivors get inside as gates close.

Arya sends Sansa to the crypts with a dragonglass dagger (“stick them with the pointy end”). In the crypts, Tyrion and Sansa talk of their past marriage and Daenerys; Missandei defends her queen. Theon apologizes to Bran, who says everything led him home. Bran wargs into ravens and spots the Night King.

Wights smother sections of the burning trench with their bodies and climb the walls in massive waves. Defenders on the battlements kill many but are overwhelmed in the whiteout. Jaime is saved by Brienne; Jorah saves Sam with Heartsbane. Arya shoots flaming arrows. The Hound freezes in fear of fire until Beric urges him on, pointing to Arya.

A giant wight bashes through the main gate. Lyanna Mormont is crushed in its hand but stabs its eye with dragonglass before dying; the giant falls. The courtyard is overrun. Order collapses.

Arya is knocked out, recovers in the library, and uses Faceless Men stealth to kill wights quietly until spotted. She flees through the castle. Beric and the Hound find her; Beric sacrifices himself holding off wights so Arya and the Hound can escape. Melisandre finds the injured Arya and reminds her of the prophecy about brown eyes, blue eyes, green eyes—and “what do we say to the God of Death?” Arya answers “Not today” and leaves with purpose.

In the godswood the Ironborn fall one by one to wights until only Theon remains. He charges the Night King with a dragonglass spear; the Night King breaks it and impales Theon, who dies at Bran’s feet after Bran thanks him. The Night King approaches the defenseless Bran.

Meanwhile Jon faces Viserion on the ground after being thrown from Rhaegal. Daenerys tries to burn the Night King with Drogon but the fire does nothing. The Night King dismounts and approaches; Drogon is wounded and flees. Wights swarm Daenerys until Jorah fights them off, dying of his wounds in her arms after she reaches him.

Arya sneaks up behind the Night King in the godswood as he reaches for Bran. She leaps with the Valyrian steel dagger (Catspaw). He catches her by the throat mid-air. She drops the dagger from her restrained hand, catches it with the other, and stabs him in the chest. The Night King shatters into ice. All White Walkers shatter. All wights collapse lifeless across the battlefield and castle, including Viserion. The Long Night ends.

Survivors emerge. Melisandre removes her necklace, ages rapidly into dust, and dies as dawn breaks—her purpose fulfilled. The living have won at terrible cost.

Episode 4: The Last of the Starks

Episode 4: The Last of the Starks

Winterfell is cleared of corpses. Dozens of funeral pyres burn. Jon gives a eulogy: the dead were the shields that guarded the realms of men; their watch is ended. Sansa places a Stark direwolf pin on Theon’s body. Daenerys lights Jorah’s pyre. Others light pyres for Lyanna Mormont, Beric, Edd, and the rest.

That night a somber victory feast turns celebratory with heavy drinking. Daenerys legitimizes Gendry as Gendry Baratheon, Lord of Storm’s End, rewarding his heroism and creating a political counter to Cersei in the Stormlands. The hall toasts him. Tyrion notes the shrewdness to Daenerys; Sansa watches uneasily.

Tormund and others toast Jon and Daenerys. Daenerys toasts Arya as the hero of Winterfell. She grows isolated watching the northern camaraderie around Jon and leaves. Tyrion, Jaime, Brienne, and Podrick play a drinking game. Tormund propositions Brienne again and is rebuffed. Sansa sits with the Hound; they talk of her past suffering under Ramsay making her strong, and how she fed him to his hounds.

Gendry finds Arya practicing archery and proposes marriage now that he is a lord. She kisses him passionately but refuses—she is not a lady and will not marry. Later Jaime comes to Brienne’s chambers; they sleep together (her first time).

Daenerys comes to Jon. They nearly make love but he stops because of their blood relation. She wishes he had never told her the truth. She sees how the northerners look at him as a king. He kneels and swears she is his queen forever and he will refuse any claim, but he must tell Sansa and Arya. She begs him not to, fearing it will destroy them. He insists family and truth matter; they can live with it.

The next day a war council maps the path south. Half the Unsullied and half the northern/Vale forces are dead; most Dothraki are gone. The Golden Company has reinforced Cersei. Daenerys wants to attack King’s Landing immediately. Sansa wants the exhausted armies to rest and recover. Tension rises. Jon reveals his parentage to Sansa and Arya in the godswood. Sansa is stunned and later tells Tyrion (knowing he will tell Varys). Arya accepts it quietly. Jon swears them to secrecy for now.

Daenerys grows more paranoid and isolated. Ghost is left behind injured. Rhaegal is also wounded. The armies prepare to march south. Tormund and the wildlings (with Ghost) head back north of the Wall. Brienne is left to hold Winterfell with some forces. Jaime decides to stay with her initially but later rides south alone toward Cersei after a quiet farewell.

In King’s Landing, Euron and Cersei prepare. Missandei is later captured in a trap (shown in next episode context). The living turn south for the last war, fractured by secrets and losses.

Episode 5: The Bells

Episode 5: The Bells

On Dragonstone, Varys writes letters spreading the truth of Jon’s claim, believing Daenerys is becoming unstable (“when a Targaryen is born the gods flip a coin”). He urges Jon to take the throne; Jon refuses—she is his queen. Daenerys has isolated herself, barely eating. Tyrion tells her Varys betrayed her with the secret (which Sansa told Tyrion, who told Varys). Daenerys has Varys executed by Drogon’s fire on the beach. Tyrion watches unhappily; Jon is concerned.

Later Jon tries to comfort Daenerys. She feels the people love him, not her—only fear remains for her. He says he loves her. They kiss but he pulls away over the incest. She accepts coldly: “Let it be fear.”

Daenerys orders the sack of King’s Landing. Tyrion begs against burning innocents. She sees the smallfolk as hostages of a tyrant and mercy as strength for future generations. Tyrion bargains to go into the city, convince Cersei to surrender, and ring the bells as the signal of full surrender. Daenerys reluctantly agrees but warns that further failure means his death. Part I: The Shadow in the North and the Call to Command
The story begins not with kings, but with a warning. In the frozen wilds beyond the Great Wall, three rangers of the Night’s Watch encounter the White Walkers—ancient, icy creatures thought to be extinct for thousands of years. Only one ranger, Will, escapes to the south, only to be executed as a deserter by Eddard "Ned" Stark, Lord of Winterfell. Ned carries out the sentence himself, teaching his young son Bran that "the man who passes the sentence should swing the sword."

On their way back to Winterfell, the Starks find a dead direwolf—the sigil of their house—who has left behind six pups. One is given to each Stark child, including Ned’s bastard son, Jon Snow. This discovery serves as a dark omen: the direwolf was killed by a stag’s antler (the sigil of the ruling House Baratheon).

Word arrives from the capital, King’s Landing, that the King’s Hand (the chief advisor), Jon Arryn, has died. King Robert Baratheon, Ned’s oldest friend, travels to Winterfell to ask Ned to take Arryn’s place. Along with the King comes the Lannister family: the beautiful but cold Queen Cersei, her twin brother Jaime (the "Kingslayer"), and their younger brother Tyrion, a witty dwarf.

Ned is reluctant, but his wife Catelyn receives a secret letter from her sister Lysa (Jon Arryn’s widow), claiming that Arryn was murdered by the Lannisters. Fearing for the King and the realm, Ned accepts the position to investigate. During the royal visit, young Bran Stark accidentally climbs a tower and witnesses Jaime and Cersei Lannister engaged in an incestuous affair. To protect their secret, Jaime pushes Bran from the window, intending to kill him. Bran survives but is left paralyzed and in a coma, with no memory of the fall.

Part II: The Game Begins (The Journey South)
As Ned journeys south with his daughters Sansa (betrothed to the cruel Prince Joffrey) and Arya, Jon Snow heads north to join the Night’s Watch, seeking a life of honor away from his status as a bastard. He is accompanied by Tyrion Lannister, who wishes to see the edge of the world.

The journey to King’s Landing reveals the deep rot in the kingdom. A conflict breaks out between Arya and Prince Joffrey. Arya’s direwolf, Nymeria, bites Joffrey to defend her. In the political fallout, Cersei demands the death of the wolf. Since Nymeria has fled, Ned is forced to execute Sansa’s innocent direwolf, Lady, a moment that shatters the girls' innocence and marks the beginning of the Stark-Lannister blood feud.

In Winterfell, an assassin attempts to kill the comatose Bran with a unique Valyrian steel dagger. Catelyn fights the assassin off, and her direwolf, Summer, finishes the job. Convinced the Lannisters are behind this, Catelyn travels secretly to King’s Landing to warn Ned.

Part III: The Dragon Queen Awakens
Across the Narrow Sea in the continent of Essos, the exiled Viserys Targaryen plots to reclaim his father’s throne. He "sells" his sister, Daenerys, to Khal Drogo, the leader of a massive Dothraki horse-lord army, in exchange for military support.

Initially terrified, Daenerys receives three petrified dragon eggs as a wedding gift. As she adapts to the Dothraki culture, she grows in confidence, eventually earning Drogo’s love and the respect of the tribe. She realizes that her brother Viserys is a weak, entitled coward who will never be a true king. When Viserys threatens Daenerys and her unborn child in a drunken rage, Drogo "crowns" him by pouring molten gold over his head, killing him. Daenerys watches without flinching, realizing that "fire cannot kill a dragon."

Part IV: The Web of King’s Landing
Upon arriving in the capital, Ned Stark finds himself outmatched by the political "players": Petyr "Littlefinger" Baelish (the Master of Coin and a childhood friend of Catelyn) and Lord Varys (the Master of Whispers).

Ned investigates Jon Arryn’s final days and discovers a pattern. Arryn had been researching the lineages of Great Houses. Ned eventually realizes the truth: all of King Robert’s "children" are blonde-haired, while every Baratheon in history had black hair. He concludes that Joffrey, Myrcella, and Tommen are not Robert’s children, but the products of Jaime and Cersei’s incest.

Meanwhile, Catelyn encounters Tyrion Lannister at a roadside inn while returning home. On a whim, she arrests him for the attempted murder of Bran and takes him to her sister Lysa at the Eyrie. This act of aggression brings the Starks and Lannisters to the brink of war. Tywin Lannister, the family patriarch, responds by sending raiders into the Stark-aligned Riverlands.

Part V: The Fall of the Hand
In the Eyrie, Tyrion survives a trial by combat when the mercenary Bronn fights on his behalf. Tyrion is freed, but the damage is done. Back in King’s Landing, Ned confronts Cersei with his knowledge of her children's parentage, offering her a chance to flee into exile to spare her children's lives. Cersei famously warns him: "When you play the game of thrones, you win or you die. There is no middle ground."

King Robert is mortally wounded by a boar during a hunt—an "accident" likely orchestrated by the Lannisters. On his deathbed, he names Ned the Protector of the Realm until Joffrey comes of age. Ned, ever honorable, alters the will to say "rightful heir" instead of Joffrey, intending to give the throne to Robert’s brother, Stannis Baratheon.

Ned asks Littlefinger to secure the support of the City Watch (the Gold Cloaks). However, when Robert dies and Ned presents the will, Littlefinger betrays him. The Gold Cloaks slaughter Ned’s guards, and Ned is arrested for treason.

Part VI: The War of the Five Kings
With Ned in the dungeons, his eldest son Robb Stark calls his banners and marches south to rescue his father and sisters. Robb proves to be a brilliant strategist, winning the Battle of the Whispering Wood and capturing Jaime Lannister as a prisoner of war.

In the capital, Sansa pleads for her father’s life. Joffrey, now King, promises to be merciful if Ned confesses his "treason" and acknowledges Joffrey as the true king. To save his daughters, Ned swallows his pride and makes a false public confession at the Great Sept of Baelor.

However, the sadistic Joffrey breaks the agreement. To the horror of Cersei and the crowd, Joffrey orders Ned’s execution. Ilyn Payne, the King’s Justice, beheads Ned Stark with his own Valyrian steel sword, Ice. Arya, watching from the crowd, is rescued by a Night’s Watch recruiter and begins a journey of survival, while Sansa remains a captive of the Lannisters.

Part VII: The Blood of the Dragon and the New King
The news of Ned’s execution sends shockwaves through Westeros. The Northern lords, unwilling to serve the Lannisters or the Baratheon brothers, proclaim Robb Stark as "The King in the North." The realm is now fractured into a multi-sided civil war.

In Essos, Daenerys’ world collapses. Khal Drogo suffers an infected wound. In a desperate attempt to save him, Dany uses a blood-magic ritual performed by a witch, Mirri Maz Duur. The ritual costs the life of Dany’s unborn son and leaves Drogo in a vegetative state. Daenerys smothers Drogo to end his suffering.

She builds a massive funeral pyre for Drogo, tying the witch to the stakes and placing her three dragon eggs on the wood. As the fire roars, Daenerys herself walks into the flames.

The next morning, the Dothraki find her amidst the ashes, unharmed. Clinging to her are three newly hatched dragons—the first seen in the world for over a century. The season ends with the birth of magic and the rise of a new power, while the Seven Kingdoms descend into total war.

Key Thematic Analysis (Expansion for Depth)
1. The Death of Honor: Season 1 is defined by the deconstruction of the "hero." Ned Stark is the traditional protagonist—honorable, loyal, and just. However, in the world of King’s Landing, these traits are his downfall. The season teaches the audience that "doing the right thing" does not guarantee safety or victory.

2. The Coming of Winter: The Stark words, "Winter is Coming," serve as a double metaphor. Literally, the long summer is ending and a harsh winter is approaching. Figuratively, it refers to the dark times ahead (war, famine, and the White Walkers). While the lords fight over a chair, the true threat accumulates in the North.

3. The Agency of Women: The season highlights the limited power of women in a patriarchal society and how they navigate it. Cersei uses sex and manipulation; Catelyn uses family duty and diplomacy; Sansa attempts to survive through courtesy; Arya rejects gender roles entirely; and Daenerys transforms from a bartered object into a god-like queen.

4. The Illegitimacy of Power: The central conflict stems from the question: Who has the right to rule? Is it the man with the strongest claim (Stannis), the man with the biggest army (Robb), the man currently sitting on the throne (Joffrey), or the man who understands how to pull the strings (Littlefinger)? By the end of the season, the concept of a "rightful" king is shattered.

Joffrey offers a false account of the incident, and Cersei asks Sansa to confirm it. Put in an impossible position, Sansa refuses to contradict him, enraging Arya. The king decides to let Ned discipline Arya while he will do the same to Joffrey, but Cersei demands that the direwolf be put down. When Nymeria cannot be found, Cersei spitefully requests that Sansa's direwolf Lady be killed instead, and Robert acquiesces, upsetting Sansa and further angering Arya.

Furious, Eddard attends to the matter himself, passing the Hound arriving with Mycah's bloodied corpse. Eddard is shocked and disgusted, and when he asks if the Hound rode Mycah down, the Hound responds that he ran, but not very fast. Eddard kills Lady with a dagger, and hundreds of miles away, Bran awakens.

The Stark party arrives in King's Landing.
The Stark party arrives in King's Landing.

The royal party reaches King's Landing. Almost immediately, Lord Eddard Stark is asked to attend a meeting of the king's Small Council and to change his clothes, but he refuses to the latter. Before that he encounters Jaime Lannister in the throne room. Jaime is still unhappy that Eddard judged him dishonorable for killing the Mad King, the murderer of Eddard's father and brother, and for having the nerve to casually seat himself upon the Iron Throne after mayhem was through. Jaime is unrepentant about it. Eddard meets the council members: Lord Petyr "Littlefinger" Baelish, the king's Master of Coin and a friend of Eddard's wife from childhood; Grand Maester Pycelle, the king's adviser in all matters scientific and academic; Lord Renly Baratheon, the younger of the king's two brothers and Master of Laws; and Varys, a eunuch and the Master of Whisperers (the head of the king's intelligence network).

Varys tells Eddard that the council members heard about his "troubles on the Kingsroad" and that they pray for Joffrey's recovery. Eddard grimly responds "It's a shame no one prayed for the butcher's boy", which visibly upsets Varys.

Eddard is stunned to learn that the crown is six million gold dragons in debt, half of which is to Lord Tywin Lannister. To make matters worse, King Robert has just ordered a lavish tournament to celebrate Eddard's appointment. He resolves to advise Robert to cancel the tournament, but the council is doubtful that the king will listen.

Cersei and her son Joffrey.
Cersei and her son Joffrey.

Queen Cersei talks to Joffrey about the incident on the river. She tells him that when he is king, the truth will be whatever he decides it will be. Joffrey thinks there will be trouble with the Starks, and promises that when he is king, he will double their taxes, force them to contribute to a standing army and, should they object, crush them and install someone loyal, such as his great-uncle Kevan, as Warden of the North. Cersei points out that the North is too vast and wild to be militarily conquered by outsiders, and a king needs to be more clever. She also advises him to be kind to his betrothed Sansa Stark to avoid stirring up trouble for later, and concludes that "Anyone who isn't us is an enemy."

Arya and Sansa are still at odds over the incident with Joffrey and her direwolf. Eddard explains to Arya that Sansa was put in a difficult position by the king and queen, and while she shouldn't have lied, winning the long-term approval of Joffrey, her future husband, was important. Arya is unhappy with the situation, but Eddard mollifies her by allowing her to practice with her sword, Needle.

Catelyn Stark and Ser Rodrik arrive at King's Landing and attempt to sneak into the city, but are spotted by one of Littlefinger's men. They are taken to meet Littlefinger at a brothel he owns, where Lord Varys is also waiting. He explains that one of his 'little birds' told him they were coming. Catelyn is angered by the way they've been treated, but asks Littlefinger for aid in finding the people who tried to have Bran killed. Littlefinger is able to answer this quickly stating that the elaborate dagger wielded by the assassin used to be his, but he lost it in a gamble with Tyrion Lannister.

Littlefinger fetches Eddard to meet his wife, but Eddard suspects a trick and pushes Littlefinger up against a wall outside the brothel wanting to know what his game is. Catelyn then appears, and Eddard is pacified. After hearing her news, he vows to find the truth and expose the Lannisters to Robert. Littlefinger agrees to be his ally in this, for the affection he once bore Catelyn as a youngster.

Ravens arrive at King's Landing with news of Bran's recovery. Cersei fears he will expose their secret, but Jaime comforts her, confident they can outwit a child if need be.

Elsewhere, Robert swaps old war stories with Ser Barristan Selmy, a distinguished and famous knight and the commander of the Kingsguard. Summoning Jaime Lannister, Robert jokingly questions him about Aerys Targaryen's death, wondering if the Mad King died begging for mercy, but Jaime rather coldly replies that the master he betrayed died screaming the same words he'd been saying since the siege of King's Landing began: "Burn them all".

Eddard has contracted a swordmaster, Syrio Forel, the former First Sword of Braavos, to teach Arya how to use her sword properly. Arya is thrilled, and 'the dance' begins. At Winterfell, Bran has awoken but has no memory of his accident. His injuries have left him bedridden and unlikely to walk again. Old Nan, the oldest servant in the castle, tells Bran stories to pass the time, but he doesn't want her usual heroic stories about the likes of Ser Duncan the Tall. She instead speaks of the White Walkers and the coming of a vast winter that will blanket the world. When Robb pays a visit, Bran asks his brother if it is true that he will never walk again. Robb reluctantly says this is so. Bran remarks that he would rather be dead.

At the Wall
At Castle Black, the primary redoubt of the Night's Watch in the shadow of the Wall, Jon Snow shows his worth to the trainer, Ser Alliser Thorne, by besting several fellow members of the Watch in the practice yard. Thorne is disgusted at the poor performance of the others but has no praise for Jon either, dubbing him Lord Snow and describing him as "the least useless person here". Watching over the new recruits with Lord Commander Jeor Mormont, Tyrion notes Thorne's stern and unusual ways, but Jeor doesn't care as he only requires Thorne to turn the "thieves and runaways" into men of the Night's Watch. Later on, several of the other recruits gang up on Jon, but the situation is defused by Tyrion. Tyrion points out to Jon that none of the other recruits had the benefit of a skilled master-at-arms to train them, and that Jon is alienating them through his standoffish attitude and superior combat skills.

Benjen talks with Jon on the Wall.
Benjen talks with Jon on the Wall.

Benjen talks with Jon on the Wall.

Benjen Stark meets Jon atop the Wall and tells him he is going on a ranging in the Haunted Forest. He refuses to take Jon with him, telling him he isn't ready, and that here rank and nobility mean nothing. Every man must earn everything he gets. Before departing, Benjen stops by the eating area to say farewell to Yoren, a fellow Night's Watchman who scouts for new recruits in the capital. Benjen also scolds Tyrion for his naivety regarding what is north of the Wall and states that Tyrion has no authority to say what is or isn't beyond the Wall as he hasn't been out there himself.

Later, Tyrion discusses north of the Wall with Jeor Mormont and his chief adviser, the ancient and blind Maester Aemon. Jeor asks for Tyrion to intercede at court and get the Watch more men as they are dangerously undermanned. Aemon warns that the Stark words are right. Winter is coming. It will be more harsh and terrible than any in living memory. More dangerous things than just wildlings might come with it. After all, one of their number swore that the White Walkers had returned ... right up to the moment Ned Stark cut his head off. Tyrion admits his skepticism that supernatural creatures might exist, but he agrees to bring word to his queen.

Before departing for King's Landing, Tyrion fulfills an old ambition by climbing to the top of the Wall and urinating off the edge of it. He and Jon share a moment of fellowship before Tyrion departs for the capital in the company of Yoren.

Daenerys rides with the khalasar.

Daenerys commands the khalasar to halt on a whim, exercising her growing authority and power. Viserys does not take well to being commanded and threatens his sister, whereupon he is lassoed around the neck by Rakharo, a Dothraki warrior wielding a whip. Daenerys calms the situation and Viserys is forced to walk, a sign of shame amongst the horse-riding Dothraki. Later, Irri reveals to Daenerys that Daenerys is pregnant. Daenerys relays the news to Khal Drogo and tells him she thinks it will be a boy as they lie naked in each other's arms. Ser Jorah Mormont and Rakharo compare the Westerosi and Dothraki ways of battle: the heavily-armored but slow knights, with longswords good for piercing armor, versus the lightly-armored but fast-moving horse-warriors. Jorah has heard of Rakharo's father, a great warrior, but admits that he disgraced his own father, a man of great honor

. Jorah has heard of Rakharo's father, a great warrior, but admits that he disgraced his own father, a man of great honor. When he learns that Daenerys is pregnant, he announces he must split off from the column to ride to the Free City of Qohor, but will rejoin them before they reach Vaes Dothrak.

In Winterfell, Bran Stark has a nightmare in which he sees a raven with three eyes, sitting on one of the stone direwolves outside the doorway to the Stark crypts. He wakes up to find his direwolf Summer by his side. Theon Greyjoy summons Hodor, the castle's dim-witted stableboy, who can only say the word "Hodor", to help carry Bran down to the throne room, where Robb Stark is hosting a meeting with Tyrion Lannister and Yoren, both traveling down from the Wall to King's Landing together. Robb very pointedly offers hospitality to any man of the Watch, silently letting Tyrion know he is not invited to stay at Winterfell.

When Bran arrives, Tyrion asks if he likes to ride and sympathizes with him for being a cripple, which annoys Bran, but Tyrion simply says that like being a dwarf, it is the truth, no less so for being a hard truth. He gives Bran the design of a saddle which will allow Bran to ride even in his current state; Tyrion explains to Robb that "you must shape the horse to the rider," by starting with a yearling and training it to respond to the reins and Bran's voice (as he can't use his heels). He does it to repay Bran's half-brother's friendship and because he has a weakness for "cripples, bastards and broken things." Due to this kindness, Robb says he can stay, but Tyrion says he would prefer the brothel in town. As he prepares to leave the castle, Theon comes to Tyrion and rather condescendingly sends him off, recommending the prostitute Ros at the brothel. Tyrion asks Theon why Lady Catelyn was not present to receive him and concludes that Catelyn is not in Winterfell

. Tyrion asks Theon why Lady Catelyn was not present to receive him and concludes that Catelyn is not in Winterfell. He also taunts Theon about how the son of the ferocious Balon Greyjoy has been reduced to playing lackey in Winterfell to his captors, which infuriates Theon, and gives him a coin, assuming that he has not already had sex with Ros.

At the Wall
Samwell Tarly joins the new recruits at Castle Black.
Samwell Tarly joins the new recruits at Castle Black.

At Castle Black, a new recruit for the Night's Watch has arrived: Samwell Tarly, the son of the famous Lord Randyll Tarly. Samwell is fat, soft and pampered, and in his first practice fight does dismally. Ser Alliser Thorne has no time for his weakness. He directs the other recruits to attack 'Ser Piggy', but Jon Snow finds this cruel and unfair, and takes pity on Sam and fends off the attackers. Thorne tries to turn it into a game, ordering three trainees take on Sam's protector (taunting Jon that he has found a new Lady love), but Jon nevertheless fends them all off. Samwell is naive and self-deprecating, claiming to be a coward and craven, to Jon's astonishment. No one admits to being a coward, and Grenn says that they shouldn't even be seen talking to him.

Sam joins Jon on the Wall for sentry duty, even though he says his eyesight is weak, he is afraid of heights, and can't take the cold. Jon asks why he joined the Night's Watch as he is afraid of everything. Sam tells him that on his eighteenth nameday his father offered him a choice. Sam was a man and his heir, but he was not skilled at combat, he was unworthy of his name and birthright. Samwell's father forced him to join the Night's Watch, and told him that if he refused, he would arrange a "hunting trip" with his son in the woods, and implied that Sam would be killed in a way that looked accidental. Jon is shocked that a true born son of high birth should be treated worse than he himself had been as a bastard. Sam knows that the next day he will be made to fight again and expects it to be bad.

Grenn yields to Samwell.
Grenn yields to Samwell.

At the Wall, Jon orders the recruits to go easy on Sam, but Rast refuses, saying that if Ser Alliser orders him to fight 'Lady Piggy', he will slice himself off a side of bacon. In response to Rast's comments, Jon goes to his bed that night and uses his direwolf Ghost to intimidate Rast into playing along. The next day, no one will fight Sam. After Grenn takes a very weak blow from Sam and yields, Ser Alliser scolds Jon for his rebellious actions. Later, when Jon and Sam are cleaning the dining hall, they talk about how neither of them have been with a woman. Sam tells Jon that he has not had success with girls, while Jon reveals he'd rather not risk siring a child that will have the life of a bastard like himself. A furious Alliser Thorne comes in and tells Jon that this charity won't help Sam harden up to survive the winter that is coming. He tells them the truly horrific experience he went through trapped by a blizzard north of the Wall that ended in cannibalism.

In Vaes Dothrak
Khal Drogo's khalasar arrives at Vaes Dothrak, the Dothraki city. There are no city walls, but there is a large gateway arch made of two statues of rearing horses. Viserys is annoyed that Drogo has been taking 'his' army in the wrong direction. Later, he bathes with Doreah and tells her about how he was raised with stories about the Targaryen dragons and his own destiny. He recites the names of several dragons, and tells her about the skulls of dragons that once decorated the throne room at King's Landing, but she starts to annoy him with talk of dragons, reminding him that they are dead. He tells her to finish pleasuring him in silence.

Later that day, Viserys is enraged when Daenerys sends Doreah with an invite for him to dine with her, as he interprets this as his sister commanding him to come. He drags Doreah into Daenerys' tent, and insults her dinner and the gifts of clothes she tries to give him as a way of making amends for having previously confiscated his horse. He is still dressed in his now ragged clothes from Pentos, having refused to dress like a Dothraki, whom he regards as savages. He sneers that next she will try to braid his hair like a Dothraki. Angered by his ingratitude, Daenerys retorts that he has no right to braid his hair until he is victorious in battle, which further infuriates him. A furious Viserys tackles her to the ground and tries to strike her, calling her nothing but a "horselord's slut", and warning her that she's "awoken the Dragon", but this time she fights back, hitting him in the face with a metal and leather belt

. She tells a stunned Viserys, who can only gawp at her in astonishment, that she is the Khal's wife, and is carrying his child (and by implication, Viserys is nothing to the Dothraki), and warns that if he raises a hand against her again, he will lose his hands. Later, Daenerys confides in Mormont her realization that Viserys will never become King of Westeros. He is so weak and ineffectual that he couldn't command an army even if Drogo gave him one, to which Jorah agrees.
